# Tapir commands

All 641 commands Tapir adds to Archicad, by group.

## How a Tapir command is sent

Archicad (with a project open) answers JSON on `http://127.0.0.1:19723`. Tapir's commands go
through Archicad's own `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand`, in the namespace `TapirCommand`:

```json
{"command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand",
 "parameters": {"addOnCommandId": {"commandNamespace": "TapirCommand", "commandName": "GetAddOnVersion"},
                "addOnCommandParameters": {}}}
```

The answer is `{"succeeded": true, "result": {"addOnCommandResponse": {...}}}`. Python's standard
library is enough (`urllib.request`); the official `archicad` package and the Tapir Grasshopper
plugin send the same JSON. Every command, with its parameters and an example, is in
[commands.md](https://archicad-api.com/commands.md) and [commands.json](https://archicad-api.com/commands.json).

### GetPointFromUser

Asks the designer to click a point in the current window and returns it. Archicad waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; the call fails when the input is cancelled.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.9. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetPointFromUser

Parameters:

- `prompt` (string): Shown in the control box while Archicad waits for the click. Single-byte text: the box takes a char field. Archicad's main thread waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then.

Returns:

- `position` (Coordinate3D, required): The clicked point in the project's coordinates.

Grasshopper: `GetPointFromUserComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/GetPointFromUser.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/GetPointFromUser.py): Asks the user to click a point in the current window with GetPointFromUser and prints it. Waits for a click in Archicad; Escape cancels the input and the command fails.

### ModelToScreen

Converts model coordinates to pixel positions local to the current Archicad view window (not global desktop coordinates), using the current window's size, drawing scale and zoom. In a 3D window the coordinates are projected with the current camera; in other windows z is disregarded. Available from Archicad 29.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModelToScreen

Parameters:

- `coordinates` (array of Coordinate3D, required): Model coordinates in the current database (meters). In a 3D window they are projected with the current camera; in other windows z is disregarded.

Returns:

- `screenPoints` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): One item per input coordinate, in the same order: the pixel position local to the current Archicad view window (not global desktop coordinates), or an error.

Grasshopper: `ModelToScreenComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/ModelToScreen.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/ModelToScreen.py): Converts two model points to pixel positions of the current view window with ModelToScreen. The pixels depend on the window's size, scale and zoom. Requires Archicad 29 or later.

### ScreenToModel

Converts pixel positions local to the current Archicad view window to 2D model coordinates of the current database, using the current window's size, drawing scale and zoom. It is a 2D mapping: it does not reconstruct a 3D point, and several model coordinates can map to the same pixel.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ScreenToModel

Parameters:

- `screenPoints` (array of object, required): Pixel positions local to the current Archicad view window (not global desktop coordinates).
  - `h` (integer, required): Horizontal pixel position from the left edge of the view window.
  - `v` (integer, required): Vertical pixel position from the top edge of the view window.

Returns:

- `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D or ErrorItem, required): One item per input screen point, in the same order: the 2D model coordinate in the current database (meters), or an error. This is a 2D mapping: it does not reconstruct a 3D point, and in a 3D window the result is not a point of the model.

Grasshopper: `ScreenToModelComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/ScreenToModel.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/ScreenToModel.py): Converts two pixel positions of the current view window to model coordinates with ScreenToModel. The result depends on the window's size, scale and zoom.

### GetElementFromUser

Asks the designer to click an element in the current window and returns its id, its type and the clicked point. A click on empty space or on an element of a type not asked for asks again. Archicad waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; cancelling returns cancelled.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementFromUser

Parameters:

- `prompt` (string): Shown in the control box while Archicad waits for the click. Single-byte text: the box takes a char field. Archicad's main thread waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then.
- `elementTypes` (array of ElementType): Only an element of one of these types is accepted. A click on empty space or on an element of another type asks for the click again. Default: any element.

Returns:

- `elementId` (ElementId): The clicked element. In a section or elevation window it is the model element the section element was cut from.
- `elementType` (string): The type of the clicked element (one of the ElementType values, or Unknown).
- `position` (Coordinate3D): The clicked point in the project's coordinates, as GetPointFromUser returns it.
- `elementPosition` (Coordinate3D): The coordinate of the clicked part of the element (e.g. its node or hotspot), when Archicad gives one for it.
- `cancelled` (boolean): True when the input was cancelled with Escape; no other field is returned then.

Grasshopper: `GetElementFromUserComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/GetElementFromUser.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/GetElementFromUser.py): Asks the user to click a wall or a column with GetElementFromUser and prints its id, type and the clicked point. Waits for a click in Archicad; Escape returns cancelled.

### GetCurrentWindowType

Returns the type of the current (active) window and, when it has one, the databaseId of the database it shows, which ChangeWindow takes to bring the window back after a script switched to another one. The saved view (View Map item) the window was opened from is not returned, as Archicad does not tell which one it was.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetCurrentWindowType

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `currentWindowType` (WindowType, required)
- `databaseId` (DatabaseId): The database shown in the current (active) window, the same id GetDatabases and GetContainingDatabases return. Pass it to ChangeWindow to bring this window back. Missing when the window has no database of its own that can be identified, for example a report, a rendering or a custom add-on window. The saved view (View Map item) the window was opened from is not returned: Archicad does not tell which one it was, and several saved views can show the same database.

Grasshopper: `GetCurrentWindowTypeComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/GetCurrentWindowType.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/GetCurrentWindowType.py): Prints the type and the database id of the current window with GetCurrentWindowType.

### GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale

Returns the drawing scale of the current (active) window, the scale shown in the bottom bar, as its denominator: 100.0 for 1:100, 20.0 for 1:20. Unlike GetViewSettings it needs no saved view. It reads the scale of the current database: the floor plan, a section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet or 3D document window, each of which has its own. Layouts always return 1.0.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `scale` (number, required): The denominator of the drawing scale of the current window: 100.0 for 1:100, 20.0 for 1:20. Always 1.0 for layouts.

Grasshopper: `GetCurrentWindowDrawingScaleComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale.py): Prints the drawing scale of the current window (100.0 for 1:100) with GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale.

### SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale

Changes the drawing scale of the current (active) window, the scale shown in the bottom bar, to the given denominator: 100 for 1:100. It changes the scale of the current database: the floor plan, a section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet or 3D document window, each of which has its own. Layouts are always 1:1 and are rejected. The scale must be between 1 and 30000. The change is undoable.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale

Parameters:

- `scale` (number, required): The denominator of the new drawing scale: 100 for 1:100, 20 for 1:20. Archicad accepts scales between 1 and 30000.
- `rebuild` (boolean): Rebuild the window after the scale changed (the API's zoom flag). Default: false.


Grasshopper: `SetCurrentWindowDrawingScaleComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale.py): Sets the drawing scale of the current window to 1:50 with SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale, then restores it. Needs a window other than a layout (layouts are always 1:1).

### ChangeWindow

Changes the current (active) window to the given window. A databaseId on its own is enough; the window type is taken from the database. The databaseId of a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened opens its Project Map item instead (from Archicad 27). With windowType 'FloorPlan' and a storyIndex it also activates that story on the floor plan. windowType 'Report' on its own opens the Session Report window (from Archicad 26); its text cannot be read through the Archicad API.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.3.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ChangeWindow

Parameters: none.


Grasshopper: `ChangeWindowComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/ChangeWindow.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/ChangeWindow.py): Switches to the floor plan of the lowest story with ChangeWindow, then back to the window that was open.

### GetContainingDatabases

Returns the database (window type, database id and name) that contains each of the given elements, from any database, not only the current one. Pass the windowType and databaseId to ChangeWindow to open it, for example to find an element placed on a layout.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetContainingDatabases

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `databases` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The database of each element, in the order of the input elements. Pass windowType and databaseId to ChangeWindow to open it.

Grasshopper: `GetContainingDatabasesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/GetContainingDatabases.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/GetContainingDatabases.py): Prints the database (window type, id and name) that contains each of the first two walls, with GetContainingDatabases. Needs at least one Wall.

### CloseWindows

Closes the windows of the given databases (for example layouts, sections or details opened earlier with ChangeWindow), with one execution result per window; a window Archicad cannot close gets a failed result. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CloseWindows

Parameters:

- `windows` (array of object, required): The windows to close.
  - `databaseId` (DatabaseId, required): The database shown in the window, as GetDatabases, GetContainingDatabases or GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId return it.
  - `windowType` (WindowType): Optional. When given, the window is only closed when its database is of this type.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `CloseWindowsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/CloseWindows.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/CloseWindows.py): Opens the first layout, goes back to the floor plan and closes the layout's window with CloseWindows. Needs at least one Layout. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### DeleteGhostRecords

Deletes the trace (ghost) record of each given parent database, which removes the trace reference shown in that database's window. A database without a trace reference gets a failed execution result. Not undoable.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteGhostRecords

Parameters:

- `databases` (Databases, required): The parent databases whose trace (ghost) record is deleted, as returned by GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId or GetContainingDatabases.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `DeleteGhostRecordsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/DeleteGhostRecords.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/DeleteGhostRecords.py): Deletes the trace reference (ghost) of the first section with DeleteGhostRecords. ### GetEditModeState

Tells whether Archicad is in a hierarchical editing mode (curtain wall, stair, beam or column editing), and which element is being edited. Read only: it never enters, leaves or cancels an editing mode. Commands that modify the project can fail while such a mode is active. The overall inEditMode flag requires Archicad 29 or later; the command requires Archicad 27 or later.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetEditModeState

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `inEditMode` (boolean): True when Archicad is in any hierarchical editing mode (curtain wall, stair, railing, beam, column, MEP elements, etc.). Only returned from Archicad 29.
- `curtainWall` (EditModeStateItem, required): Curtain wall editing mode.
- `stair` (EditModeStateItem, required): Stair editing mode.
- `beam` (EditModeStateItem, required): Beam editing mode.
- `column` (EditModeStateItem, required): Column editing mode.

Grasshopper: `GetEditModeStateComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/GetEditModeState.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/GetEditModeState.py): Prints whether Archicad is in curtain wall, stair, beam or column editing mode with GetEditModeState. Requires Archicad 27 or later (the overall inEditMode flag needs Archicad 29).

### SetArchicadVisibility

Hides or shows the Archicad application, e.g. to keep it out of the way while a batch runs. A script that hides Archicad must show it again, also when the script fails (e.g. in a finally block). Supported on Windows only; on macOS it returns an error.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetArchicadVisibility

Parameters:

- `isVisible` (boolean, required): True shows the Archicad application, false hides it.


Grasshopper: `SetArchicadVisibilityComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/SetArchicadVisibility.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/SetArchicadVisibility.py): Hides Archicad for two seconds with SetArchicadVisibility, then shows it again. Windows only; on macOS it returns an error.

### RunActionCenterChecks

Runs the given checks of the Action Center (by default the hotlink check). A successful result means the check ran, not that nothing was found: Archicad does not report the outcome to the caller, it shows the Action Center tab when the check found an issue.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RunActionCenterChecks

Parameters:

- `checks` (array of string ("Hotlinks", "All", "Libraries", "Drawings", "Licenses")): The Action Center checks to run, in this order. Omitted means ["Hotlinks"]. "Hotlinks" is available on every Archicad version; "All", "Libraries", "Drawings" and "Licenses" only on Archicad 25, later versions return an error for them in their execution result.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `RunActionCenterChecksComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/RunActionCenterChecks.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/RunActionCenterChecks.py): Runs the hotlink and library checks of the Action Center with RunActionCenterChecks. Archicad shows the Action Center tab when a check finds an issue; the result only says the check ran.

### RedrawCurrentDatabase

Redraws the current database, even when its window is in the background. Only the visible region of its window is updated.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RedrawCurrentDatabase

Parameters: none.


Grasshopper: `RedrawCurrentDatabaseComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/RedrawCurrentDatabase.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/RedrawCurrentDatabase.py): Redraws the current database with RedrawCurrentDatabase.

### GetProductVersionInfo

Retrieves the version information of the running Archicad: build number, language code, product family and version text, plus the product name, product type, main/update/hotfix versions, the available domains (Architecture, MEP) and the CEIP project identifier of the open project from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetProductVersionInfo

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `productName` (string): The name of the product. Archicad 29 or later.
- `productType` (string): The Graphisoft product type. Archicad 29 or later.
- `productFamilyId` (string, required): The identifier of the product family.
- `languageCode` (string, required): The Graphisoft language code of the running Archicad (for example INT, GER).
- `buildNumber` (integer, required): The build number of the running Archicad.
- `versionString` (string, required): The full version of the running Archicad as text.
- `mainVersion` (string): The main version, as text. Archicad 29 or later.
- `updateVersion` (string): The update version, as text. Archicad 29 or later.
- `hotfixVersion` (string): The hotfix version, as text. Archicad 29 or later.
- `versionNumbers` (array of integer): The three parts of the version number. Archicad 28 only.
- `availableDomains` (array of string ("Architecture", "MEP")): The domains available in the running Archicad. Archicad 29 or later.
- `ceipProjectId` (string): The CEIP project identifier of the open project. Left out when no saved project is open. Archicad 29 or later.

Grasshopper: `GetProductVersionInfoComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/GetProductVersionInfo.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/GetProductVersionInfo.py): Prints the build number, language, product name and version of the running Archicad with GetProductVersionInfo. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

In Archicad 25-27 the 3D window may need to be open.

Turns 3D Cutaway on or off and shows or hides the cutting planes in the 3D window. In Archicad 25-27 the 3D window may need to be open.

In Archicad 25-27 the 3D window may need to be open.

### SetDialogAutoClose

Turns the dialog auto close on or off. While it is on, Archicad closes the dialogs it would show with their default button instead of waiting for the user, so automation is not blocked by them. To have it on already while Archicad opens a project (before any command can be sent), set the TAPIR_DIALOG_AUTOCLOSE environment variable to true for the Archicad process before starting it.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetDialogAutoClose

Parameters:

- `enabled` (boolean, required): True turns the dialog auto close on: Archicad closes the dialogs it would show with their default button instead of waiting for the user. False turns it off.


Grasshopper: `SetDialogAutoCloseComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/SetDialogAutoClose.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/SetDialogAutoClose.py): Turns the dialog auto close on with SetDialogAutoClose, reads it back, then restores the original state. While it is on, Archicad closes its dialogs with their default button instead of waiting for the user.

### GetDialogAutoClose

Tells whether the dialog auto close is on, the same state SetDialogAutoClose writes, so a script can restore it afterwards. The state belongs to the running Archicad process: it is off when Archicad starts (unless the TAPIR_DIALOG_AUTOCLOSE environment variable is true), it stays as last set until Archicad quits, and it is shared by every add-on and script in that Archicad.

Group: Application Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetDialogAutoClose

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `enabled` (boolean, required): Whether the dialog auto close is on: true while Archicad closes the dialogs it would show with their default button instead of waiting for the user. This is the same state SetDialogAutoClose writes.

Grasshopper: `GetDialogAutoCloseComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Application/GetDialogAutoClose.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Application/GetDialogAutoClose.py): Prints whether the dialog auto close is on with GetDialogAutoClose.

### GetAutoTextKeys

Retrieves the available autotext keys (name and embeddable key): the Project Info, layout, drawing, date and other autotexts Archicad lists, and the property based ones, optionally for a specific element. Embed a key in a Text or Label content by surrounding it with '<' and '>'.

Parameters:

- `elementId` (ElementId): Optional. The element to retrieve context dependent autotext keys for (its own properties, plus the ones common to all element types, e.g. 'Element ID', 'Area'). When omitted, only the property based autotext keys common to all element types are returned. The other autotexts (Project Info, layout, drawing, date, ...) are returned either way.

Returns:

- `autoTextKeys` (array of object, required)
  - `name` (string, required): The autotext's name, as shown in the Insert Autotext dialog of Archicad.
  - `key` (string, required): The autotext's key. To embed it in the content of a Text or Label element, surround it with '<' and '>', e.g. '<PROJECTNAME>' or '<PROPERTY-69A58F6F-DD3B-478D-B5EF-09A16BD0C548>'.

Grasshopper: `GetAutoTextKeysComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetAutoTextKeys.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetAutoTextKeys.py): Prints the autotext keys (name and key) that a Text or Label can embed as <KEY>, with GetAutoTextKeys. Pass an elementId to get the keys of that element's type as well.

### CreateHotlinkNodes

Creates hotlink module nodes from source files. A node that already points at the same file is returned instead of duplicated (Archicad 26 and later; 25 cannot see an unplaced node).

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.9. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateHotlinkNodes

Parameters:

- `hotlinkNodes` (array of object, required): The hotlink module nodes to create. A node that already points at the same source file (compared case-insensitively) is returned as it is, with existing: true, and the name and story settings asked for are ignored. On Archicad 25 a node that has not been placed yet cannot be found, so a repeated request there creates a second node.
  - `sourceLocation` (string, required): Absolute path of the module source file (.mod or .pln).
  - `name` (string): Optional display name of the node. Defaults to the file name. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.
  - `storyRangeType` (string ("AllStories", "SingleStory")): Optional. Which stories of the source are placed: all of them, or the single reference story. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.
  - `refFloorIndex` (integer): Optional index of the reference story in the source file. Defaults to 0. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

Returns:

- `hotlinkNodes` (array of HotlinkNodeCreatedOrError, required): One item per requested node, in order: the node guid with its existing flag, or an error.

Grasshopper: `CreateHotlinkNodesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/CreateHotlinkNodes.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/CreateHotlinkNodes.py): Saves the first wall as a module in the temp folder, creates a hotlink node from it with CreateHotlinkNodes, then deletes the node. Needs at least one Wall.

Moves, rotates or mirrors placed hotlink instances by changing their transformation. MoveElements and RotateElements do not work on hotlink instances.

- `hotlinkInstances` (array of HotlinkInstanceChange, required): The placed hotlink instances to change. Every field but elementId is optional; a field that is omitted keeps its current value.

Needs at least one placed Hotlink.

### UpdateHotlinks

Re-reads the source files of hotlink module nodes and refreshes their cached content in the project, as the Hotlink Manager's Update button does.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#UpdateHotlinks

Parameters:

- `hotlinkNodes` (array of object, required): The hotlink nodes to update, from GetHotlinks or CreateHotlinkNodes. Each node's cached content is re-read from its source file, as the Hotlink Manager's Update button does.
  - `hotlinkNodeId` (HotlinkNodeId, required)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `UpdateHotlinksComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/UpdateHotlinks.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/UpdateHotlinks.py): Re-reads the source files of every top-level hotlink node with UpdateHotlinks, as the Hotlink Manager's Update does. Needs at least one hotlink.

### ChangeHotlinkNodes

Repoints hotlink module nodes at other source files, as the Hotlink Manager's Relink button does. Follow it with UpdateHotlinks to re-read the content.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ChangeHotlinkNodes

Parameters:

- `hotlinkNodes` (array of object, required): The hotlink nodes to repoint at another source file, as the Hotlink Manager's Relink button does. The placed instances stay where they are. Follow it with UpdateHotlinks on the same nodes to re-read the content from the new file.
  - `hotlinkNodeId` (HotlinkNodeId, required)
  - `sourceLocation` (string, required): Absolute path of the new module source file (.mod or .pln).

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ChangeHotlinkNodesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/ChangeHotlinkNodes.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/ChangeHotlinkNodes.py): Relinks the first hotlink node to a copy of its source file in the temp folder with ChangeHotlinkNodes, then back. Needs at least one hotlink whose source is a file on disk.

### BreakHotlinkNodes

Breaks hotlink nodes, as the Hotlink Manager's Break Hotlink does: the elements of each node's placed instances stay in the project as ordinary elements, no longer tied to the source file.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#BreakHotlinkNodes

Parameters:

- `hotlinkNodes` (array of object, required): The hotlink nodes to break, from GetHotlinks or CreateHotlinkNodes. The elements of each node's placed instances stay in the project as ordinary elements, no longer tied to the source file, as the Hotlink Manager's Break Hotlink does. In Teamwork the Hotlink and XRef management has to be reserved first (ReserveHotlinkCacheManagement).
  - `hotlinkNodeId` (HotlinkNodeId, required)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `BreakHotlinkNodesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/BreakHotlinkNodes.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/BreakHotlinkNodes.py): Places a hotlink made from the first wall and breaks it with BreakHotlinkNodes. The node's source is the first wall, saved as a module in the temp folder. After the break the placed copy of the wall stays in the project as an ordinary wall at (50, 0). Needs at least one Wall.

### SaveProject

Saves the currently opened project.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.3.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SaveProject

Parameters:

- `projectPath` (string): Optional. Full path of a .pln file to save the project to, as File > Save As does: the open project then refers to that file. This saves an untitled project, or one opened from an older Archicad version, which cannot be saved in place. An existing file at the path is overwritten. When omitted, or when it is the project's own file, the project is saved in place, which keeps the refusal of a project opened read-only.


Grasshopper: `SaveProjectComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/SaveProject.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/SaveProject.py): Saves the open project to its file with SaveProject. Overwrites the project file with the current state. An untitled project needs projectPath.

### SaveAsModuleFile

Saves the given elements, or the current selection, as a hotlink module (.mod) file.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.9. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SaveAsModuleFile

Parameters:

- `moduleFilePath` (string, required): Absolute path of the .mod file to write. An existing file is overwritten. The current window must be a floor plan, section, elevation or detail.
- `elements` (Elements): Optional. The elements that go into the module; omitted, the current selection does, as Save Selection as Module would. Pass GetAllElements for the whole project. Archicad 25 and 26 support the selection form only.


Grasshopper: `SaveAsModuleFileComponent`

Needs at least one Wall. Without elements the current selection is saved.

### SaveProjectAsArchive

Saves the open project as an archive (.pla) file, with the library parts it uses inside.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.6.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SaveProjectAsArchive

Parameters:

- `archiveFilePath` (string, required): Absolute path of the .pla archive to write. An existing file is overwritten. The archive becomes the open project, as Save As does.
- `includeLibraryParts` (boolean): Optional, true by default. Whether the library parts the project uses go into the archive, which makes the archive usable as a linked library of another project.
- `includeProperties` (boolean): Optional, true by default. Whether the properties go into the archive.
- `includeTextures` (boolean): Optional, false by default. Whether the linked textures go into the archive.
- `includeBackgroundPicture` (boolean): Optional, false by default. Whether the background picture goes into the archive.


Grasshopper: `SaveProjectAsArchiveComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/SaveProjectAsArchive.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/SaveProjectAsArchive.py): Saves the open project as an archive (.pla) in the temp folder with SaveProjectAsArchive.

### SaveCurrentWindowAsImage

Saves what the current window shows as an image file (png, jpg, bmp, tiff or gif), as File > Save as does with a picture format. Master layout windows are not supported: save a layout that uses the master layout instead.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SaveCurrentWindowAsImage

Parameters:

- `imageFilePath` (string, required): Absolute path of the image file to write. An existing file is overwritten.
- `format` (string ("png", "jpg", "bmp", "tiff", "gif")): Optional. The image file format; omitted, it comes from the extension of imageFilePath (.png, .jpg or .jpeg, .bmp, .tif or .tiff, .gif).
- `colorDepth` (string ("blackAndWhite", "16Colors", "256Colors", "16Grays", "256Grays", "trueColor", "trueColorWithAlpha")): Optional, trueColor by default. The color depth of the image, as in the Save as picture dialog.
- `dithered` (boolean): Optional, false by default. Whether the image is dithered when its color depth drops colors.
- `entireDrawing` (boolean): Optional, false by default. Whether the image covers the entire drawing of a 2D window instead of its current zoom, as the Entire Drawing option of the Save as picture dialog does.

Returns:

- `imageFilePath` (string, required): The path of the written image file.
- `zoom` (Zoom): The zoom of the window the image shows, as GetView2DTransformations reports it. Absent for the 3D window.
- `rotation` (number): The orientation of the window in radian, as GetView2DTransformations reports it. Absent for the 3D window.

Grasshopper: `SaveCurrentWindowAsImageComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/SaveCurrentWindowAsImage.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/SaveCurrentWindowAsImage.py): Saves what the current window shows as a png in the temp folder with SaveCurrentWindowAsImage. Master layout windows are not supported.

### PhotoRender

- `sceneName` (string): Optional. The rendering scene to render with, one of the names GetRenderingScenes returns. It is made the current scene first, as SetCurrentRenderingScene does, and stays current afterwards. Omitted, the current scene is used.

### GetProjectPreferences

Gets pages of the project preferences (Options > Project Preferences): the working units, the dimensions, the calculation units and the zones. Further pages may follow.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetProjectPreferences

Parameters:

- `preferenceTypes` (array of string ("WorkingUnits", "Dimensions", "CalculationUnits", "Zones")): The preference pages to get. Every page when missing.

Returns:

- `workingUnits` (object): The Working Units page: the units and the number of decimals the model's lengths, areas, volumes and angles are shown with.
  - `length` (object, required)
  - `area` (object, required)
  - `volume` (object, required)
  - `angle` (object, required)
- `dimensions` (object): The Dimensions page: the dimension standard and the format (unit, decimals, extra accuracy and zero handling) of each dimension type.
  - `dimensionStandardIndex` (integer, required): The index of the dimension standard the page follows.
  - `linear` (object, required): The format of the linear dimensions.
  - `angle` (object, required): The format of the angle dimensions.
  - `radial` (object, required): The format of the radial dimensions.
  - `level` (object, required): The format of the level dimensions.
  - `elevation` (object, required): The format of the elevation dimensions.
  - `doorWindow` (object, required): The format of the door, window and skylight dimensions.
  - `parapet` (object, required): The format of the sill height (parapet) dimensions.
  - `area` (object, required): The format of the area values the dimensions show (area calculations).
- `calculationUnits` (object): The Calculation Units page: the units, the number of decimals and the extra accuracy of the values in element lists and schedules. GetCalculationUnits answers the same page.
  - `length` (object, required)
  - `area` (object, required)
  - `volume` (object, required)
  - `angle` (object, required)
- `zones` (object): The Zones page: the reduction of the calculated zone area under a low ceiling. The wall inset (niche) sizes of the page are not available through the API.
  - `lowCeilingAreaReduction` (object, required): Up to three ceiling height limits split a zone into height ranges; the area of each range is reduced by its own percent in the calculated area of the zone.

Grasshopper: `GetProjectPreferencesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetProjectPreferences.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/GetProjectPreferences.py): Prints the working units, the reference levels and the floor plan cut plane with GetProjectPreferences. Without preferenceTypes every page is returned.

### SetProjectPreferences

Changes pages of the project preferences (Options > Project Preferences): the working units, the dimensions, the calculation units and the zones. Only the given fields change, the rest of each page keeps its value. In Teamwork the PreferencesDialog lockable object set has to be reserved first (ReserveLockableObjectSet). Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetProjectPreferences

Parameters:

- `workingUnits` (object): The Working Units page: the units and the number of decimals the model's lengths, areas, volumes and angles are shown with.
  - `length` (object)
  - `area` (object)
  - `volume` (object)
  - `angle` (object)
- `dimensions` (object): The Dimensions page: the dimension standard and the format (unit, decimals, extra accuracy and zero handling) of each dimension type.
  - `dimensionStandardIndex` (integer): The index of the dimension standard the page follows.
  - `linear` (object): The format of the linear dimensions.
  - `angle` (object): The format of the angle dimensions.
  - `radial` (object): The format of the radial dimensions.
  - `level` (object): The format of the level dimensions.
  - `elevation` (object): The format of the elevation dimensions.
  - `doorWindow` (object): The format of the door, window and skylight dimensions.
  - `parapet` (object): The format of the sill height (parapet) dimensions.
  - `area` (object): The format of the area values the dimensions show (area calculations).
- `calculationUnits` (object): The Calculation Units page: the units, the number of decimals and the extra accuracy of the values in element lists and schedules. GetCalculationUnits answers the same page.
  - `length` (object)
  - `area` (object)
  - `volume` (object)
  - `angle` (object)
- `zones` (object): The Zones page: the reduction of the calculated zone area under a low ceiling. The wall inset (niche) sizes of the page are not available through the API.
  - `lowCeilingAreaReduction` (object): Up to three ceiling height limits split a zone into height ranges; the area of each range is reduced by its own percent in the calculated area of the zone.

Returns:

- `workingUnits` (ExecutionResult)
- `dimensions` (ExecutionResult)
- `calculationUnits` (ExecutionResult)
- `zones` (ExecutionResult)

Grasshopper: `SetProjectPreferencesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Project/SetProjectPreferences.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Project/SetProjectPreferences.py): Sets the working length unit to millimeters and the floor plan cut plane height to 1.2 m with SetProjectPreferences, then restores both. Only the given fields change. In Teamwork the PreferencesDialog lockable object set must be reserved first. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### ConvertUnitValues

Formats lengths, areas, volumes and angles (given in meters, square meters, cubic meters and radians) as Archicad shows them with the unit and rounding of the given Project Preference, returning the text, its extra accuracy decimals and the unit. The output is aligned with the input array of values. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Project Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ConvertUnitValues

Parameters:

- `values` (array of object, required): The values to convert.
  - `value` (number, required): The value to convert, in meters, square meters, cubic meters or radians, matching the kind of the preference.
  - `preference` (string ("WorkModel", "WorkLayout", "WorkAngle", "DimLinear", "DimAngle", "DimRadial", "DimLevel", "DimElevation", "DimDoorWindow", "DimParapet", "DimArea", "CalcLength", ...), required): The Project Preference whose unit and rounding are applied: WorkModel, WorkLayout and WorkAngle are the Working Units; the Dim ones are the Dimensions (DimDoorWindow the door, window and skylight dimensions, DimParapet the sill height, DimArea the area calculations); the Calc ones are the Calculation Units & Rules.

Returns:

- `convertedValues` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The converted values, in the order of the input. A value that cannot be converted is an error item.

Values are given in meters, square meters and radians. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

## Custom Data Commands

### SetElementUserData

Stores string values under keys on elements, for scripts to keep their own state per element (external database ids, sync timestamps, markers). The data is saved with the project as the user data of the Tapir add-on on the element and appears nowhere in the Archicad UI. The given keys are merged into what the element already holds: a key that exists gets the new value, other keys are left as they are, and the keys listed in keysToDelete are removed. Prefix the keys with the script's name so that scripts do not overwrite each other's data. One undo step per call; in a Teamwork project the element has to be reserved.

Group: Custom Data Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetElementUserData

Parameters:

- `elementUserData` (array of object, required): The elements with the key-value pairs to store on them. Each item needs userData, keysToDelete or both.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `userData` (array of object): The key-value pairs to store on the element. A key that already exists on the element gets the new value; other keys are left as they are.
  - `keysToDelete` (array of string): The keys to remove from the element. A key the element does not hold is ignored.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required): One result per input item, in the input order.

Grasshopper: `SetElementUserDataComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/CustomData/SetElementUserData.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/CustomData/SetElementUserData.py): Stores a key-value pair on the first wall with SetElementUserData, reads it back, then removes it. The data is saved with the project, invisible in the Archicad UI. Needs at least one Wall.

### GetElementUserData

Reads the values stored on elements by SetElementUserData: every key of each element, or only the given keys.

Group: Custom Data Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementUserData

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `keys` (array of string): Optional. Only the pairs with these keys are returned; a key an element does not hold is left out of its pairs. When omitted, every pair stored on each element is returned.

Returns:

- `elementUserData` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): One item per element, in the input order: the pairs stored on the element (none when the element holds no user data of Tapir), or an error when the element was not found or its data could not be read.

Grasshopper: `GetElementUserDataComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/CustomData/GetElementUserData.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/CustomData/GetElementUserData.py): Prints the key-value pairs that scripts stored on the first ten walls (SetElementUserData) with GetElementUserData. Needs at least one Wall.

### CaptureElementState

Captures the current state of the elements of the project and returns a stateId for it, so that GetElementChangesSince can later list what was created, modified and deleted since. The optional type selects how changes are detected (modification stamps by default, or the 3D model). The state is kept in a file in the temporary folder for the Archicad session only: it is lost when the project is closed or Archicad restarts, and ReleaseElementState frees it earlier.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CaptureElementState

Parameters:

- `type` (string ("ModificationStamp", "3DModel")): How GetElementChangesSince finds the changed elements between this state and another one. ModificationStamp (the default) compares the modification stamps of the elements, so any change to an element counts. 3DModel compares the 3D model of the elements, so only a change that alters the 3D model counts, and capturing it generates the 3D model of the project. Two states can only be compared when they were captured with the same type.

Returns:

- `stateId` (object, required): The identifier of the captured state, accepted by GetElementChangesSince and ReleaseElementState. It is only valid in the Archicad session and project it was captured in.
  - `guid` (Guid, required)
- `type` (string ("ModificationStamp", "3DModel"), required): The type the state was captured with.

Grasshopper: `CaptureElementStateComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CaptureElementState.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CaptureElementState.py): Captures the current state of the project's elements with CaptureElementState. GetElementChangesSince can compare a later state to it. The script releases the state at the end.

### GetElementChangesSince

Returns the new, modified and deleted elements between a state captured by CaptureElementState and either another captured state (toStateId) or the current state of the project. Scripts that keep an external copy of the model use it to sync only what changed instead of re-reading every element. Fails for a stateId that is unknown - never captured, released, or lost because the project was closed or Archicad restarted.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementChangesSince

Parameters:

- `stateId` (object, required): The state to compare from, as returned by CaptureElementState.
  - `guid` (Guid, required)
- `toStateId` (object): The state to compare to, as returned by CaptureElementState with the same type as stateId. If omitted, the current state of the project is used, so the response lists what changed since stateId was captured.
  - `guid` (Guid, required)

Returns:

- `newElements` (Elements, required): The elements that exist in the later state but not in the earlier one.
- `modifiedElements` (Elements, required): The elements that exist in both states and changed between them.
- `deletedElements` (Elements, required): The elements that exist in the earlier state but not in the later one. They cannot be read any more, only their identifiers are known.

### FilterElements

Keeps the elements that match all the given criteria: Archicad's flag filters (filters), layer (layerIndices), home story (floorIndices) and element type (elementTypes). Within one criterion any of the listed values matches; an omitted criterion does not filter.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#FilterElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `filters` (array of ElementFilter): Optional. Archicad's own flag filters. An element is kept only when it fulfills all of them.
- `layerIndices` (array of integer): Optional. An element is kept only when it is on one of these layers (the layerIndex field of GetDetailsOfElements).
- `floorIndices` (array of integer): Optional. An element is kept only when its home story is one of these (the floorIndex field of GetDetailsOfElements).
- `elementTypes` (array of ElementType): Optional. An element is kept only when its type is one of these.

Returns:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

### GetDetailsOfElements

Gets the details of the given elements (geometry parameters etc). Use the optional fields parameter to return only the fields you need and skip the computation of the others (for example floorPlanPolygons). An element of another database (a layout, a section, a worksheet ...) returns only its header fields (type, floor index, layer, draw index) with fromOtherDatabase set to true.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetDetailsOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `fields` (array of ElementDetailsField): Optional filter for the fields to return for each element. When omitted, every field is returned. Fields not listed are not computed at all, so listing only what you need skips in particular the floorPlanPolygons extraction, which regenerates each element's 2D drawing primitives and can dominate the execution time of batch reads.

Returns:

- `detailsOfElements` (array of object or object or ErrorItem, required): One entry per input element, in the same order as the input elements array. An element that cannot be read gets an error entry in its place, so the position of an entry tells which input element it belongs to.

### GetElementAtCoordinate

Finds the element of the given polygonal type (for example Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone or Hatch) at a coordinate of the floor plan of the current database, the way a click there would. Use the optional filters parameter (the values of FilterElements) to consider only, for example, the elements visible by layer, and the optional z parameter to give the elevation of the point. Returns found: false when there is no such element. Useful together with GetPointFromUser.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementAtCoordinate

Parameters:

- `elementType` (ElementType, required): The type of the element to look for. Only polygonal element types can be searched, for example Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone or Hatch.
- `coordinate` (Coordinate2D, required): The point to search at, in the project's coordinates, on the floor plan of the current database.
- `z` (number): Optional. The elevation of the search point, handed to Archicad together with the coordinate. Default is 0; without z a point 1 mm higher is also tried, so an element whose top is at 0 (for example a slab at the story level) is found.
- `filters` (array of ElementFilter): Optional. Only an element passing every given filter is found (the same values as FilterElements accepts).

Returns:

- `found` (boolean, required): True when an element of the given type was found at the coordinate.
- `elementId` (ElementId): The identifier of the found element. Absent when nothing was found.

Grasshopper: `GetElementAtCoordinateComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementAtCoordinate.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementAtCoordinate.py): Finds the Slab at a point of the floor plan, the way a click there would, with GetElementAtCoordinate. The point is the average of the first slab's outline vertices. Needs at least one Slab.

Gets the absolute bottom level of curtain walls or their subelements (segments, frames, panels, junctions, accessories). The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

### GetQuantitiesOfElements

Gets the quantities of the given elements calculated by Archicad (volumes, surfaces, lengths etc.), together with the volume and projected area per building material (one item per skin of composite and complex profile elements, one item for basic elements). Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Zone, ColumnSegment, BeamSegment. Use the optional minOpeningSize parameter to control the conditional values, and calculateInOneCall to calculate all the elements in one Archicad call.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetQuantitiesOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `minOpeningSize` (number): Optional minimum opening size in square meters. Openings smaller than this are not subtracted when the conditional values (for example volumeConditional of a Wall) are calculated. Archicad only uses it for walls. Default value is 0, so every opening is subtracted.
- `calculateInOneCall` (boolean): Optional. When true, Archicad calculates the quantities of all the supported elements in one call instead of one call per element, which can be faster for many elements. The output has the same format. If that one call fails, every supported element gets the same error. Default value is false.

Returns:

- `quantitiesOfElements` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The quantities of the elements, in the order of the given elements. Lengths are in meters, areas in square meters and volumes in cubic meters.

Grasshopper: `GetQuantitiesOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetQuantitiesOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetQuantitiesOfElements.py): Reads the quantities Archicad calculates (volumes, surfaces, lengths ...) of the first walls with GetQuantitiesOfElements. Openings smaller than 0.5 m2 are not subtracted. Needs at least one Wall.

### TriangulatePolygonsOfElements

Triangulates the plan polygon of the given elements, holes excluded, as Archicad does it: the outline of a Slab, Zone, Hatch or Mesh and the polygon of a Roof. Each triangle is given by the 2D coordinates of its three vertices. With convex: true, the faces of the 3D model of the elements (of any type) are decomposed into convex polygons instead, given by the 3D coordinates of their vertices. The output is aligned with the input array of elements; an element of another type gets an error item.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#TriangulatePolygonsOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `convex` (boolean): Optional. When true, the faces of the 3D model of each element (its own bodies, any element type) are decomposed into convex polygons instead, as Archicad does it, and returned as convexPolygons. Default value is false.

Returns:

- `triangulations` (array of object or object or ErrorItem, required): The triangulation of the polygon of each element, aligned with the input: its triangles (or with convex: true its convex polygons), or an error (for example for an element type that has no polygon).

Grasshopper: `TriangulatePolygonsOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/TriangulatePolygonsOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/TriangulatePolygonsOfElements.py): Triangulates the plan polygon of the first slabs with TriangulatePolygonsOfElements. Needs at least one Slab.

### GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements

Gets the exposed surface areas of the given elements calculated by Archicad: for each element one item per surface attribute and building material pair with the area that is not covered by the covering elements (for example the wall area behind a slab is taken off the wall's surface). The covering elements are the optional coverElements; by default every construction element of the project. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): The elements to get the surface quantities of.
- `coverElements` (Elements): Optional covering elements: the area where one of them overlaps a surface of an element is subtracted from that surface, so for example a slab on a wall takes its footprint off the top surface of the wall. When omitted, every Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Stair and Curtain Wall of the project is a covering element. Pass an empty array to get the whole surfaces with nothing subtracted. An element never covers itself.

Returns:

- `surfaceQuantitiesOfElements` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The surface quantities of the elements, in the order of the given elements. Areas are in square meters.

Grasshopper: `GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements.py): Reads the exposed surface areas of the first walls, with the slabs as covering elements, with GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements. Needs at least one Wall. Without coverElements every construction element covers the surfaces.

### EditHierarchicalElement

Opens the given hierarchical element (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column) in its hierarchical 3D editing mode, as the Edit button of the element does. Fails when Archicad is already in an editing mode. Leave the mode with FinishHierarchicalEditing. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#EditHierarchicalElement

Parameters:

- `elementId` (ElementId, required): The hierarchical element (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column) to open in hierarchical editing mode.


Grasshopper: `EditHierarchicalElementComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/EditHierarchicalElement.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/EditHierarchicalElement.py): Opens a curtain wall in its hierarchical editing mode with EditHierarchicalElement. While the mode is open, Archicad refuses every JSON command with error 4001 (ongoing user input), so the script cannot leave it: leave it yourself in Archicad, with the button of the edit mode palette. Needs at least one Curtain Wall. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### FinishHierarchicalEditing

Finishes the current hierarchical editing mode (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column): accept true keeps the changes (OK), accept false discards them (Cancel). The accept parameter is required, so changes are never discarded silently. Fails when Archicad is not in such an editing mode. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#FinishHierarchicalEditing

Parameters:

- `accept` (boolean, required): True to accept the changes made in the hierarchical editing mode (OK), false to discard them (Cancel).


Grasshopper: `FinishHierarchicalEditingComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/FinishHierarchicalEditing.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/FinishHierarchicalEditing.py): Tries to leave a hierarchical editing mode with FinishHierarchicalEditing, discarding the changes (Cancel). accept True would keep the changes (OK). Limitation: while an editing mode is open, Archicad refuses JSON commands with error 4001 (ongoing user input) before they run, so this call is refused then; leave the mode in Archicad, with the button of the edit mode palette. When no editing mode is open, it fails with "not in a hierarchical editing mode". Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### GetElementsInDrawOrder

Returns the identifier of every element of the current database, or of the given databases, in Archicad's drawing order (the order set by Bring to Front and Send to Back), as ACAPI_DrawOrder_DrawOrderGetNext walks it. Use the optional elementType and filters parameters for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given.

### LinkElements

Creates persistent links between pairs of elements, each from one element to another, with an optional integer flags value per link. Scripts can record their own relations between elements this way (for example which label documents which column) instead of storing GUIDs in properties. The links are stored in the project and have no effect on geometry; they are independent from groups, hotlinks and solid element operations. A link is directional: it is returned by GetLinksOfElements for the element it starts from only, and removed by UnlinkElements. Undoable.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#LinkElements

Parameters:

- `links` (array of ElementLinkData, required): The links to create, each from one element to another.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required): One result per link, aligned with the input.

Grasshopper: `LinkElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/LinkElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/LinkElements.py): Links the first wall to the second one with LinkElements, reads the link back, then removes it. Scripts can record their own relations between elements this way. Needs at least two Walls.

### UnlinkElements

Removes the links created by LinkElements between the given pairs of elements. The direction matters: the link starting from fromElementId and pointing to toElementId is removed. Undoable.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#UnlinkElements

Parameters:

- `links` (array of ElementLinkReference, required): The links to remove, each from one element to another.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required): One result per link, aligned with the input.

Grasshopper: `UnlinkElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/UnlinkElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/UnlinkElements.py): Removes a link created by LinkElements with UnlinkElements. Links the first wall to the second one first, so it needs at least two Walls. Only the link in the given direction is removed.

### GetZoneBoundaries

Gets the boundaries of the given Zones (connected elements, neighbour zones, etc.). Accepts either a single zoneElementId or a list of zones. Prefer the list: the expensive boundary recalculation runs once per call, so querying many Zones in one call is much faster than calling the command once per Zone.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.2.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetZoneBoundaries

Parameters:

- `zoneElementId` (ElementId): The identifier of a single Zone. Prefer the zones array: querying many Zones in one call is much faster than one call per Zone.
- `zones` (Elements): A list of Zones. Only one of zoneElementId and zones can be given.


Grasshopper: `GetZoneBoundariesComponent`

Needs at least one Zone.

### GetZoneReductions

### GetCollisions

Detect collisions between the given two groups of elements.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.2.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetCollisions

Parameters:

- `elementsGroup1` (Elements, required)
- `elementsGroup2` (Elements, required)
- `settings` (object)
  - `volumeTolerance` (number, required): Intersection body volume greater then this value will be considered as a collision. Default value is 0.001.
  - `performSurfaceCheck` (boolean, required): Enables surface collision check. If disabled the surfaceTolerance value will be ignored. By default it's false.
  - `surfaceTolerance` (number, required): Intersection body surface area greater then this value will be considered as a collision. Default value is 0.001.

Returns:

- `collisions` (array of object, required)
  - `elementId1` (ElementId, required)
  - `elementId2` (ElementId, required)
  - `hasBodyCollision` (boolean, required)
  - `hasClearenceCollision` (boolean, required)

### DeleteElements

Deletes elements. The zones of the call are deleted before all the other elements, so an automatic zone deleted together with its bounding walls is gone before its boundary is; deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed polygon found' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it in Archicad. Returns an execution result for each input element: an element that could not be deleted (for example because its layer is locked) or a guid that is not in the project gets a failed execution result instead of being skipped silently, and does not stop the other elements from being deleted.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.2.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): The elements to delete. The zones among them are deleted before all the others, so an automatic zone deleted together with its bounding elements is gone before its boundary is. Deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed polygon found around the clicked point' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it in Archicad.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `DeleteElementsComponent`, `ElementMetadata`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/DeleteElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/DeleteElements.py): Creates a wall and deletes it again with DeleteElements, first as a dry run that deletes nothing.

### ChangeLibraryPartOfElements

Changes the library part of the given Object, Lamp, Window, Door, Skylight, Zone and symbol Label elements to another library part of the same type, given by name, index or guid, e.g. to replace missing library parts with ones from the loaded libraries. The elements themselves (guid, properties, classifications) are kept. Components of stairs and railings are not supported, even when they are reported as Objects. Optionally keeps the values of the GDL parameters with the same name and type, and the size (A and B).

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ChangeLibraryPartOfElements

Parameters:

- `elementsWithLibraryPart` (array of object, required): The elements with the library part to change them to. Components of stairs and railings are not supported, even when they are reported as Objects.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `libraryPart` (object or object or object, required): The new library part, given by one of name, index or guid. It has to be a placeable library part of the element's type in the loaded libraries.
  - `keepParameters` (boolean): Copies the values of the element's GDL parameters to the parameters of the new library part that have the same name, type and array dimensions; the other parameters get the new part's defaults. Default: true.
  - `keepSize` (boolean): Keeps the size (A and B) of the element; when false, the element gets the new part's default size. Default: true.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ChangeLibraryPartOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ChangeLibraryPartOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ChangeLibraryPartOfElements.py): Sets the first object to the library part it already uses with ChangeLibraryPartOfElements. Needs at least one Object. Giving the part it already has leaves the project unchanged; give the name of another library part (see GetAvailableLibraryParts) to replace it.

### CreateColumns

Creates Column elements based on the given parameters.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateColumns

Parameters:

- `columnsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Columns.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.
  - `coordinates` (object, required): 3D coordinate.
  - `height` (number): Optional column height.
  - `axisRotationAngle` (number): Optional column rotation angle in radians.
  - `slantAngle` (number): Optional slant angle in radians. A non-zero value also makes the column slanted, unless isSlanted is given explicitly.
  - `isSlanted` (boolean): Optional explicit slanted state. By default it is derived from slantAngle.
  - `slantDirectionAngle` (number): Optional rotation angle of the slanted column on the horizontal plane in radians.
  - `width` (number): Cross section width of the column. Applied to all segments.
  - `depth` (number): Cross section depth (height) of the column. Applied to all segments. Only effective for rectangular columns.
  - `coreAnchor` (ColumnCoreAnchor)
  - `circleBased` (boolean): True for a round column cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored if profileId is also given. Applied to all segments.
  - `isWidthAndHeightLinked` (boolean): When true (the default), Archicad keeps width and depth equal and setting one changes the other - set to false to give width/depth independent values. Applied to all segments.
  - `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId): Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.
  - `profileId` (AttributeId): Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the coordinate's z value.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `ColumnsComponent`, `CreateColumnsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateColumns.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateColumns.py): Creates two columns with CreateColumns: one with the Column tool defaults and one round, 3 m high column. Coordinates are in meters; z is the elevation of the column base.

### CreateWalls

Creates Wall elements based on the given parameters.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.4.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateWalls

Parameters:

- `wallsData` (array of object, required)
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a Wall favorite to base the new element on. Its settings (structure, reference line location, top link, offsets, ...) are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them. With a favorite only begCoordinate and endCoordinate are needed.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.
  - `begCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
  - `endCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Story index (as returned by GetStories). When provided, zCoordinate is interpreted as bottomOffset relative to the floor. Takes priority over zCoordinate for floor assignment.
  - `zCoordinate` (number): Absolute Z when floorIndex is absent; bottomOffset relative to the floor when floorIndex is provided.
  - `height` (number): Optional explicit height. Sets relativeTopStory to 0, so it replaces the top link of the favorite or the tool default. When omitted, the height and top link of the favorite (or of the Wall tool defaults) are kept.
  - `thickness` (number): Optional thickness. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's thickness is kept. Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) wall - a Composite or Profile wall takes its thickness from the composite or profile attribute. Without structureType the new wall keeps the structure of the favorite (or the wall tool default), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.
  - `offset` (number): Optional reference line offset. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's offset is kept.
  - `arcAngle` (number): Arc angle in radians; non-zero creates a curved wall (begCoordinate/endCoordinate are the chord endpoints).
  - `referenceLineLocation` (WallReferenceLineLocation): Optional. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's reference line location is kept. The Core* values only have an effect on a Composite or Profile wall.
  - `flipped` (boolean): Optional. True mirrors the wall to its reference line (the side GetDetailsOfElements reports as flipped). When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's side is kept, which for a Profile wall mirrors its whole cross section.
  - `structureType` (WallStructureType): Optional. When neither this nor one of the attribute ids below is given, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's structure is kept.
  - `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId)
  - `compositeId` (AttributeId)
  - `profileId` (AttributeId)
  - `contourPen` (integer): Pen of the wall's own contour/reference outline (API_WallType::contPen) - distinct from cutFillPen, which is the cut fill pattern's pen.
  - `contourPen3D` (integer): Pen of the wall's contour in 3D views (API_WallType::contPen3D).
  - `contourLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the wall's own contour (API_WallType::contLtype) - pairs with contourPen, which only sets the pen, not the line type.
  - `belowViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type used when "OutLines Only" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup (API_WallType::belowViewLineType).
  - `aboveViewLinePen` (integer): Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup.
  - `aboveViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.
  - `displayOption` (DisplayOption)
  - `viewDepthLimitation` (ViewDepthLimitation): Only has an effect on a multi-story wall (relativeTopStory/topOffset making it span more than one story).
  - `useCompositePriority` (boolean): When true, the Composite's own priority is used at junctions instead of connectionPriority.
  - `linkToSettings` (LinkToSettings): When newCreationMode is true, homeStoryDifference overrides the home story selected by floorIndex or derived from zCoordinate.
  - `inheritEndSurface` (boolean): The end surface of the wall is inherited from the adjoining wall.
  - `alignTexture` (boolean): Align texture mapping to the wall's edges.
  - `polyCanChange` (boolean): The polygonal wall's corners can be changed in case of L and T connections. Only meaningful for a Polygonal wall (geometryType).
  - `materialsChained` (boolean): Whether the surface materials are chained.
  - `logHeight` (number): Height of the log for log walls. 0 means a normal (non-log) wall.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateWallsComponent`, `WallsApiComponent`, `WallsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateWalls.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateWalls.py): Creates a straight and a curved wall with CreateWalls. Fields not given (structure, top link, ...) come from the Wall tool defaults, or from favoriteName.

### CreateBeams

  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.
