### CreateStairs

Creates Stair elements based on the given baseline and parameters.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateStairs

Parameters:

- `stairsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Stair elements.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `baseLinePoints` (array of Coordinate2D, required): 2D coordinates defining the stair baseline polyline. Minimum 2 points for a straight stair, 3+ for L-shaped or U-shaped stairs.
  - `zCoordinate` (number, required): The Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the stair base.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.
  - `totalHeight` (number): Total height of the stair.
  - `flightWidth` (number): Width of the stair flight.
  - `stepNum` (integer): Number of risers (steps).
  - `riserHeight` (number): Height of each riser.
  - `treadDepth` (number): Depth (going) of each tread.
  - `finishVisible` (boolean): Optional. If false, the tread/riser finishes are hidden and only the stair structure (e.g. a monolith) is modeled.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateStairsComponent`

Two baseline points make a straight stair; more points make an L- or U-shaped one. The straight stair's baseline runs along the middle of its flight (baselinePosition). Fields not given come from the Stair tool defaults.

### SolveStairBaseline

Runs the Archicad stair solver on the given Stair baselines and parameters without creating any element. Returns for each one whether the baseline was already correct, could be solved or could not be solved, with the baseline and the main stair settings after solving. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SolveStairBaseline

Parameters:

- `stairsData` (array of object, required): Array of Stair data to check, with the same fields as the items of CreateStairs (without favoriteName). Nothing is created.
  - `baseLinePoints` (array of Coordinate2D, required): 2D coordinates defining the stair baseline polyline. Minimum 2 points for a straight stair, 3+ for L-shaped or U-shaped stairs.
  - `zCoordinate` (number, required): The Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the stair base.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.
  - `totalHeight` (number): Total height of the stair.
  - `flightWidth` (number): Width of the stair flight.
  - `stepNum` (integer): Number of risers (steps).
  - `riserHeight` (number): Height of each riser.
  - `treadDepth` (number): Depth (going) of each tread.
  - `finishVisible` (boolean): Optional. If false, the tread/riser finishes are hidden and only the stair structure (e.g. a monolith) is modeled.

Returns:

- `solutions` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The results of the stair solver, aligned with the input stairsData.

Grasshopper: `SolveStairBaselineComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SolveStairBaseline.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SolveStairBaseline.py): Checks an L-shaped stair baseline with SolveStairBaseline, without creating a stair. Prints whether the baseline is Correct, Solved (with the solved baseline) or NotSolved. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### CreateSlabs

Creates Slab elements based on the given parameters.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateSlabs

Parameters:

- `slabsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Slabs.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

### GetOpeningDefault

Returns the settings of the Opening tool defaults: the extrusion parameters (as GetOpeningDetails returns them) and the floor plan parameters (as GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters returns them). Available from Archicad 29.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetOpeningDefault

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `extrusionParameters` (object, required): The size and extrusion settings. A size Archicad does not give for the opening's shape is left out.
  - `constraint` (string ("ForcedVertical", "ForcedHorizontal", "Aligned", "Free")): How the opening's orientation is constrained.
  - `limitType` (string ("Infinite", "Finite", "HalfInfinite")): How far the opening's extrusion reaches.
  - `linkedStatus` (string ("Linked", "NotLinked")): Whether the opening's width and height are linked. Left out when Archicad gives none.
  - `shapeType` (string ("Rectangular", "Circular", "Polygonal")): The shape of the opening's polygon.
  - `width` (number)
  - `height` (number)
  - `anchor` (string ("TopLeft", "TopCenter", "TopRight", "MiddleLeft", "Center", "MiddleRight", "BottomLeft", "BottomCenter", "BottomRight"), required): The anchor point of the opening's polygon.
  - `anchorAltitude` (number)
  - `extrusionStartOffset` (number)
  - `finiteBodyLength` (number)
  - `isExtrusionSurfaceOverridden` (boolean, required)
  - `extrusionSurfaceId` (AttributeId): The surface of the extrusion faces. Only given when it is overridden.
  - `isEndSurfaceOverridden` (boolean, required)
  - `endSurfaceId` (AttributeId): The surface of the end faces. Only given when it is overridden.
  - `areOverriddenSurfacesLinked` (boolean, required)
- `floorPlanParameters` (object, required)
  - `floorPlanDisplayMode` (string ("Symbolic", "SymbolicCut", "SymbolicOverhead", "Projected")): How the opening is shown on the floor plan.
  - `dividedOpeningMode` (string ("Disconnected", "Connected")): How the parts of an opening divided by the floor plan cut are shown.
  - `openEdgeStyle` (string ("Hide", "ShowUncut", "ShowOverhead")): How the open edges of the opening are shown on the floor plan.
  - `showReferenceAxis` (boolean): Whether the reference axis of the opening is shown on the floor plan.
  - `referenceAxisPen` (integer)
  - `referenceAxisLineTypeId` (AttributeId): The line type of the reference axis.
  - `referenceAxisOverhang` (number): How far the reference axis reaches beyond the opening.
  - `cutSurfacesUseLineOfCutElements` (boolean): Whether the cut surfaces use the line of the cut elements instead of cutSurfacesLinePen and cutSurfacesLineTypeId.
  - `cutSurfacesLinePen` (integer)
  - `cutSurfacesLineTypeId` (AttributeId)
  - `outlinesUseLineOfCutElements` (boolean): Whether the outlines use the line of the cut elements instead of the uncut and overhead lines below.
  - `outlinesUncutLinePen` (integer)
  - `outlinesUncutLineTypeId` (AttributeId)
  - `outlinesOverheadLinePen` (integer)
  - `outlinesOverheadLineTypeId` (AttributeId)
  - `useCoverFills` (boolean)
  - `coverFillsUseFillsOfCutElements` (boolean): Whether the cover fills are the fills of the cut elements instead of coverFillId.
  - `coverFillId` (AttributeId): The fill of the cover fills.
  - `coverFillPen` (integer)
  - `coverFillBackgroundPen` (integer)
  - `coverFillOrientation` (HatchOrientationType)
  - `coverFillTransformation` (CoverFillTransformation): The orientation and distortion of the cover fill. Left out when Archicad gives none.
  - `cutSymbolLibPartId` (Guid): The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the cut opening. Left out when the opening has no cut symbol.
  - `unCutSymbolLibPartId` (Guid): The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the uncut opening. Left out when the opening has no uncut symbol.

Grasshopper: `GetOpeningDefaultComponent`

Requires Archicad 29 or later.

### SetOpeningDefault

Changes the settings of the Opening tool defaults, with the names GetOpeningDefault returns. Only the given settings change. Available from Archicad 29.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetOpeningDefault

Parameters:

- `extrusionParameters` (object): The size and extrusion settings to change, with the names GetOpeningDetails returns. The ones left out are not changed.
  - `constraint` (string ("ForcedVertical", "ForcedHorizontal", "Aligned", "Free")): How the opening's orientation is constrained.
  - `limitType` (string ("Infinite", "Finite", "HalfInfinite")): How far the opening's extrusion reaches.
  - `linkedStatus` (string ("Linked", "NotLinked")): Whether the opening's width and height are linked. While they are linked, giving both width and height makes a square of the height; give NotLinked with them to get a different width and height.
  - `shapeType` (string ("Rectangular", "Circular", "Polygonal")): The shape of the opening's polygon.
  - `width` (number): The opening's width. See linkedStatus.
  - `height` (number): The opening's height. See linkedStatus.
  - `anchor` (string ("TopLeft", "TopCenter", "TopRight", "MiddleLeft", "Center", "MiddleRight", "BottomLeft", "BottomCenter", "BottomRight")): The anchor point of the opening's polygon.
  - `anchorAltitude` (number)
  - `extrusionStartOffset` (number)
  - `finiteBodyLength` (number)
  - `isExtrusionSurfaceOverridden` (boolean)
  - `extrusionSurfaceId` (AttributeId): The surface of the extrusion faces. Only used when the surface is overridden.
  - `isEndSurfaceOverridden` (boolean)
  - `endSurfaceId` (AttributeId): The surface of the end faces. Only used when the surface is overridden.
  - `areOverriddenSurfacesLinked` (boolean)
- `floorPlanParameters` (object): The floor plan settings to change, with the names GetOpeningDefault returns. The ones left out are not changed.
  - `floorPlanDisplayMode` (string ("Symbolic", "SymbolicCut", "SymbolicOverhead", "Projected")): How the opening is shown on the floor plan.
  - `dividedOpeningMode` (string ("Disconnected", "Connected")): How the parts of an opening divided by the floor plan cut are shown.
  - `openEdgeStyle` (string ("Hide", "ShowUncut", "ShowOverhead")): How the open edges of the opening are shown on the floor plan.
  - `showReferenceAxis` (boolean): Whether the reference axis of the opening is shown on the floor plan.
  - `referenceAxisPen` (integer)
  - `referenceAxisLineTypeId` (AttributeId): The line type of the reference axis.
  - `referenceAxisOverhang` (number): How far the reference axis reaches beyond the opening.
  - `cutSurfacesUseLineOfCutElements` (boolean): Whether the cut surfaces use the line of the cut elements instead of cutSurfacesLinePen and cutSurfacesLineTypeId.
  - `cutSurfacesLinePen` (integer)
  - `cutSurfacesLineTypeId` (AttributeId)
  - `outlinesUseLineOfCutElements` (boolean): Whether the outlines use the line of the cut elements instead of the uncut and overhead lines below.
  - `outlinesUncutLinePen` (integer)
  - `outlinesUncutLineTypeId` (AttributeId)
  - `outlinesOverheadLinePen` (integer)
  - `outlinesOverheadLineTypeId` (AttributeId)
  - `useCoverFills` (boolean)
  - `coverFillsUseFillsOfCutElements` (boolean): Whether the cover fills are the fills of the cut elements instead of coverFillId.
  - `coverFillId` (AttributeId): The fill of the cover fills.
  - `coverFillPen` (integer)
  - `coverFillBackgroundPen` (integer)
  - `coverFillOrientation` (HatchOrientationType)
  - `coverFillTransformation` (CoverFillTransformation): The orientation and distortion of the cover fill. Left out when Archicad gives none.
  - `cutSymbolLibPartId` (Guid): The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the cut opening. Left out when the opening has no cut symbol.
  - `unCutSymbolLibPartId` (Guid): The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the uncut opening. Left out when the opening has no uncut symbol.
  - `clearCutSymbol` (boolean): Removes the cut symbol. Cannot be given together with cutSymbolLibPartId.
  - `clearUnCutSymbol` (boolean): Removes the uncut symbol. Cannot be given together with unCutSymbolLibPartId.

Returns:

- `elementType` (ElementType, required): The type of the elements the changed settings are the defaults of.

Grasshopper: `SetOpeningDefaultComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetOpeningDefault.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetOpeningDefault.py): Changes the floor plan display mode of the Opening tool defaults with SetOpeningDefault, then restores it. Requires Archicad 29 or later.

### PlaceOpenings

Places openings with the Opening tool settings at points of their parent elements. A point off the parent element's surface is moved to the closest point of the surface. Each opening can be given its own extrusion and floor plan settings, which change only that opening and not the tool's settings. Available from Archicad 29.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#PlaceOpenings

Parameters:

- `openingsData` (array of object, required)
  - `parentElementId` (ElementId, required): The element to place the opening in.
  - `point` (Coordinate3D, required): Where to place the opening. A point off the parent element's surface is moved to the closest point of the surface.
  - `extrusionParameters` (object): The size and extrusion settings to change, with the names GetOpeningDetails returns. The ones left out are not changed.
  - `floorPlanParameters` (object): The floor plan settings to change, with the names GetOpeningDefault returns. The ones left out are not changed.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `PlaceOpeningsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/PlaceOpenings.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/PlaceOpenings.py): Creates a wall and places two openings in it with PlaceOpenings. The first opening uses the Opening tool settings, the second gets its own size and floor plan display (the tool settings are not changed). Requires Archicad 29 or later.

### SetOpeningDetails

Changes the details of Opening elements: the parent element, the cut elements, the polygon, a transformation of the geometry and the extrusion parameters (constraint, limit type, linked status, shape type, size, anchor, offsets, surface overrides) returned by GetOpeningDetails. Available from Archicad 29.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetOpeningDetails

Parameters:

- `openingsWithDetails` (array of object, required): The Opening elements (made with the Opening tool) to change, each with the details to set. A detail that is left out stays as it is.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `parentElementId` (ElementId): The new element the opening belongs to.
  - `addCutElements` (array of ElementIdArrayItem): Elements the opening should cut as well.
  - `removeCutElements` (array of ElementIdArrayItem): Elements the opening should no longer cut.
  - `polygon` (array of Coordinate2D): The new polygon of the opening, in the plane of the xAxis and yAxis returned by GetOpeningDetails.
  - `transformation` (array of number): A transformation applied to the opening's geometry: a 3x4 matrix of 12 numbers, row by row, the 4th, 8th and 12th numbers being the translation along X, Y and Z. For example [1,0,0,1, 0,1,0,0, 0,0,1,0] moves the opening by 1 along X.
  - `extrusionParameters` (object): The size and extrusion settings to change, with the names GetOpeningDetails returns. The ones left out are not changed.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `SetOpeningDetailsComponent`

### CreateMorphs

Creates Morph elements from simple box definitions.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.4.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateMorphs

Parameters:

- `morphsData` (array of object, required)

  - `size` (Dimensions3D): Builds a simple axis-aligned box of this size. Mutually exclusive with `body` - give exactly one of the two.
  - `body` (MorphBody): Builds arbitrary geometry instead of a simple box. Mutually exclusive with `size` - give exactly one of the two.
  - `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId)
  - `xAxis` (Coordinate3D)
  - `yAxis` (Coordinate3D)
  - `zAxis` (Coordinate3D)
  - `surfaceId` (AttributeId)
  - `topExpansion` (number): Only used with `size` (box) morphs. Expands the top rectangle outwards on all four sides by this amount, creating a frustum (e.g. sloped excavation shape). 0 creates a cuboid.
  - `castShadow` (boolean)
  - `receiveShadow` (boolean)
  - `isAutoOnStoryVisibility` (boolean)
  - `showContour` (StoryVisibility)
  - `showFill` (StoryVisibility)
  - `linkToSettings` (LinkToSettings)
  - `displayOption` (DisplayOption)
  - `viewDepthLimitation` (ViewDepthLimitation)
  - `cutFillPen` (integer)
  - `cutFillBackgroundPen` (integer)
  - `cutLineType` (AttributeId)
  - `cutLinePen` (integer)
  - `uncutLineType` (AttributeId)
  - `uncutLinePen` (integer)
  - `overheadLineType` (AttributeId)
  - `overheadLinePen` (integer)
  - `useCoverFillType` (boolean)
  - `outlineContourDisplay` (boolean)
  - `coverFillType` (AttributeId)
  - `coverFillPen` (integer)
  - `coverFillBGPen` (integer)
  - `use3DHatching` (boolean)
  - `coverFillOrientation` (CoverFillOrientation)
  - `useDistortedCoverFill` (boolean)
  - `textureProjectionType` (TextureProjectionType)
  - `textureProjectionCoords` (array of Coordinate3D)
  - `level` (number)
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the basePoint's z value.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateMorphsComponent`, `MorphsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateMorphs.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateMorphs.py): Creates a 2 m box morph and a tetrahedron morph from vertices and faces with CreateMorphs. A body's vertices are local to the morph's basePoint; each face lists vertex indices counterclockwise as seen from outside. An item may also name a Morph favorite to start from (favoriteName), a layer (layerIndex) and an Element ID (id), as the box does with its id.

### CreateRoofs

Creates Roof elements based on footprint, level and roof profile data. Creates a multi-plane roof by default; pass 'pivotLine' (and optionally 'angle') to create a single-plane roof instead.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.4.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateRoofs

Parameters:

- `roofsData` (array of object, required)
  - `level` (number, required)
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from level.
  - `thickness` (number): Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) roof - a Composite roof takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Without structureType the new roof keeps the structure of the roof tool default (or the favorite), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.
  - `polygonCoordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required)
  - `polygonArcs` (array of PolyArc)
  - `holes` (Holes2D)
  - `pivotLine` (RoofPivotLine): If given, creates a single-plane roof instead of a multi-plane roof, tilted along this pivot line.
  - `angle` (number): Slope angle of the single-plane roof in radians. Only valid together with 'pivotLine'.
  - `eavesOverhang` (number)
  - `levels` (array of RoofLevel)
  - `structureType` (RoofStructureType)
  - `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId)
  - `compositeId` (AttributeId)

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateRoofsComponent`, `RoofsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateRoofs.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateRoofs.py): Creates a multi-plane roof and a single-plane roof with CreateRoofs. A pivotLine makes a single-plane roof that rises on the left of the line; angles are in radians.

### CreateRailings

Creates Railing elements along a reference polyline. Posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters come from the favorite or from the Railing tool defaults; Archicad generates one node per vertex and one segment per pair of consecutive vertices.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateRailings

Parameters:

- `railingsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Railings.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The 2D coordinates of the reference line of the railing on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates becomes one straight segment.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index (home story) of the railing. The story is made active in the floor plan while the railing is created and the previously active story is restored afterwards. When omitted, the current story.
  - `bottomOffset` (number): Optional base height of the railing relative to the floor level. When omitted, the value of the favorite (or of the Railing tool defaults) is kept.
  - `height` (number): Optional height of the railing segments. When omitted, the segment height of the favorite (or of the Railing tool defaults) is kept.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `RailingsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateRailings.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateRailings.py): Creates a 1.1 m high railing along three edges of a balcony with CreateRailings. The posts, rails, handrails and infill come from the Railing tool defaults, or from favoriteName.

### CreateCurtainWalls

Creates Curtain Wall elements along a reference polyline with a column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern. The frame and panel classes come from the favorite or from the Curtain Wall tool defaults; the pattern cells can assign them to the grid.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateCurtainWalls

Parameters:

- `curtainWallsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Curtain Walls.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The 2D coordinates of the reference line of the curtain wall on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates becomes one straight segment, so two coordinates give a single-segment curtain wall.
  - `zCoordinate` (number): Optional Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the bottom of the curtain wall. When omitted, the base level of the favorite (or of the Curtain Wall tool defaults) relative to the floor is kept.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index. When omitted, derived from zCoordinate if that is given, otherwise the current story.
  - `height` (number): Optional height of the curtain wall. When omitted, the height of the favorite (or of the Curtain Wall tool defaults) is kept.
  - `primaryPattern` (CurtainWallPattern): Optional column pattern: the sizes of the columns along the segment (the primary grid). When omitted, the pattern of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) is kept.
  - `secondaryPattern` (CurtainWallPattern): Optional row pattern: the sizes of the rows from the bottom up (the secondary grid). When omitted, the pattern of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) is kept.
  - `cells` (array of CurtainWallPatternCell): Optional assignment of panel and frame classes to the cells of the pattern unit. The unit repeats along and up the segment, so an assignment applies to every repetition of that cell. A cell not listed here keeps the assignment of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) when the pattern is unchanged, otherwise the assignment of the first default cell.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateCurtainWallsComponent`, `CurtainWallsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateCurtainWalls.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateCurtainWalls.py): Creates a 6 m long, 3 m high curtain wall with 1.5 m wide columns and two rows with CreateCurtainWalls. The frame and panel classes come from the Curtain Wall tool defaults, or from favoriteName.

### CreateAssociativeDimensions

Creates associative linear dimensions from explicit witness point references. A witness point can also be static, given by its coordinate instead of an element.

Its settings are applied first, then the command sets the geometry and its usual text placement. The favorite's text size, text pen and text frame are not applied (tested in Archicad 28): use textHeight and textPen for the texts. The Dimension tool defaults are left as they were.

  - `textPen` (integer): Optional pen index of the dimension texts, applied to every witness point after favoriteName.

  - `direction` (Coordinate2D, required)

The dimension follows the wall: inIndex 1 and 2 are the end points of the wall's reference line. A witness point given only by a coordinate is static. direction is the direction of the dimension line.

Parameters:

- `dimensionsData` (array of object, required)
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a Dimension favorite to base the new dimension on, e.g. for its layer, line pen and markers. Its settings are applied first, then the command sets the geometry and its usual text placement. The favorite's text size, text pen and text frame are not applied (tested in Archicad 28): use textHeight and textPen for the texts. The Dimension tool defaults are left as they were.
  - `textHeight` (number): Optional height of the dimension texts in millimeters (paper size), applied to every witness point after favoriteName.
  - `textPen` (integer): Optional pen index of the dimension texts, applied to every witness point after favoriteName.
  - `wallId` (ElementId, required)
  - `referencePoint` (Coordinate2D, required)
  - `direction` (Coordinate2D, required)

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateWallThicknessDimensionsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateWallThicknessDimensions.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateWallThicknessDimensions.py): Creates a wall and dimensions its thickness with CreateWallThicknessDimensions. The dimension line runs across the wall (direction) through referencePoint.

### GetOpeningTransformations

Gets the placement of Opening elements, Windows, Doors and Skylights without changing them: a global-to-local transformation matrix, its inverse, and the origin and axes in world coordinates derived from the inverse. For Windows, Doors and Skylights the local-to-global matrix is the one Archicad returns, and mirrored ones give a left-handed matrix (isMirrored). For Opening elements it is built from the opening geometry (Archicad 29 and later): origin at the anchor point, the X and Y axes of the opening and Z = X × Y, which points against the extrusion direction. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetOpeningTransformations

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `openingTransformations` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The transformation of each given Opening, or an error, in the order of the input elements.

Grasshopper: `GetOpeningTransformationsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetOpeningTransformations.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetOpeningTransformations.py): Prints the placement (transformation matrices, origin and axes) of every window with GetOpeningTransformations. Needs at least one Window; Doors, Skylights and Openings work the same way (Openings from Archicad 29). Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### CreateZones

Creates Zone elements based on the given parameters.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.8. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateZones

Parameters:

- `zonesData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Zones.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `floorIndex` (number): Optional story index of the new zone. An automatic zone (geometry.referencePosition) is found around its reference point on this story, which is made active in the floor plan while the zone is created; the previously active story is restored afterwards.
  - `name` (string, required): Name of the zone.
  - `numberStr` (string, required): Zone number.
  - `categoryAttributeId` (AttributeId): The identifier of the zone category attribute.
  - `stampPosition` (Coordinate2D): Position of the origin of the zone stamp.
  - `stampAngle` (number): Optional zone stamp rotation angle in radians.
  - `fixedStampAngle` (boolean): If true, the zone stamp angle remains fixed when the element is rotated.
  - `contourLine` (ZoneContourLine): Optional contour line of the zone. Fields that are left out keep the value of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults.
  - `coverFill` (ZoneCoverFill): Optional cover fill of the zone. Fields that are left out keep the value of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults.
  - `height` (number): Optional height of the zone from its bottom. Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height); when omitted, the height and top link of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults are kept. Do not combine with relativeTopStory.
  - `bottomOffset` (number): Optional base level of the zone relative to its home story level.
  - `topOffset` (number): Optional offset of the top of the zone from the linked top story level. Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.
  - `relativeTopStory` (number): Optional top link: non-zero links the top of the zone to another story, relative to its home story (1 is the story above), instead of an explicit height. Do not combine with height.
  - `floorThickness` (number): Optional thickness of the floor finish (subfloor thickness) of the zone.
  - `geometry` (ZoneCreationGeometry, required)

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateZonesComponent`, `ZonesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateZones.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateZones.py): Creates a 6 m x 5 m zone named Office from its outline with CreateZones. A zone that would overlap an existing zone on the same story fails with an error instead (unless allowOverlap is true). Give 'geometry': {'referencePosition': {'x': ..., 'y': ...}} instead to create an automatic zone in the room around that point.

### CreateHatches

Creates Hatch elements based on the given parameters. A hatch can have holes, in the same format SetDetailsOfElements accepts for hatches.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateHatches

Parameters:

- `hatchesData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Hatches.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `floorInd` (number): The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Layer attribute index to place the hatch on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.
  - `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The 2D coordinates of the hatch outline. Do not repeat the first point at the end.
  - `arcs` (array of PolyArc): The arcs of the hatch outline.
  - `holes` (Holes2D): Optional holes of the hatch, each with its polygonOutline and optional polygonArcs (arc indices are relative to the hole's own outline). The same format SetDetailsOfElements accepts and GetDetailsOfElements returns for hatches.
  - `contourPenIndex` (integer): Optional pen index for the contour. By default the current pen is used.
  - `fillPenIndex` (integer): Optional pen index for the fill. By default the current pen is used.
  - `fillBackgroundPenIndex` (integer)
  - `foregroundColor` (ColorRGB): Optional RGB color (components between 0.0 and 1.0) of the fill foreground, used instead of fillPenIndex. Takes precedence over fillPenIndex when both are given. The same format as the colors returned by GetZoneCategories and GetPenTables.
  - `backgroundColor` (ColorRGB): Optional RGB color (components between 0.0 and 1.0) of the fill background, used instead of fillBackgroundPenIndex. Takes precedence over fillBackgroundPenIndex when both are given.
  - `fillId` (AttributeId): Optional fill attribute. By default the current fill is used.
  - `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId)
  - `roomSpecial` (integer): Special area percent in a room (negative means OFF).
  - `showArea` (boolean)

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateHatchesComponent`, `FillsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateHatches.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateHatches.py): Creates a 4 m x 4 m hatch with a 1 m x 1 m hole and a red foreground with CreateHatches. Don't repeat the first point at the end of the outline. Colors are RGB values between 0 and 1.

### GetGridElementDefaults

Returns the Grid Tool defaults: library part, size and GDL parameters of a new grid element. Needs Archicad 26 or later.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetGridElementDefaults

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `elementId` (ElementId): The grid element. The zero GUID for the tool defaults.
- `variation` (string, required): Four-character variation of the object: 'GREL' for a grid element.
- `floorIndex` (integer, required): Home story index.
- `layerIndex` (integer, required): Layer attribute index.
- `pos` (Coordinate2D, required): Insertion point: the start of the grid line.
- `angle` (number, required): Direction of the grid line in radians.
- `length` (number, required): Length of the grid line: the GDL parameter AC_Length of the Grid Tool's grid marker, or the object's A size for a library part without it.
- `xRatio` (number, required): The object's xRatio as stored: its A size with useXYFixSize on, otherwise the A size divided by the library part's own A.
- `yRatio` (number, required): The object's yRatio as stored, like xRatio for the B size.
- `useXYFixSize` (boolean, required): Whether xRatio and yRatio hold the sizes themselves.
- `level` (number, required): Elevation of the object from its home story.
- `libInd` (integer, required): Library part index.
- `libraryPartName` (string, required): Localized name of the library part.
- `parameters` (array of object, required): GDL parameters, separators left out. Only when requested.
  - `name` (string, required)
  - `displayName` (string, required)
  - `type` (string, required): Integer, Length, Angle, RealNum, LightSwitch, ColorRGB, Intensity, LineType, Material, FillPattern, PenColor, String, Boolean, Title, BuildingMaterial, Profile, Dictionary or Unknown.
  - `value` (any): Number for numeric and boolean types, string for String and Title. Not given for arrays.
  - `dimension1` (integer): First dimension of an array parameter.
  - `dimension2` (integer): Second dimension of an array parameter.

Grasshopper: `GetGridElementDefaultsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetGridElementDefaults.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetGridElementDefaults.py): Prints the library part, size and GDL parameters a new grid element gets from the Grid Tool defaults, with GetGridElementDefaults. Requires Archicad 26 or later.

- `gridElements` (array of object, required)

  - `variation` (string, required): Four-character variation of the object: 'GREL' for a grid element.
  - `floorIndex` (integer, required): Home story index.
  - `layerIndex` (integer, required): Layer attribute index.
  - `pos` (Coordinate2D, required): Insertion point: the start of the grid line.
  - `angle` (number, required): Direction of the grid line in radians.
  - `length` (number, required): Length of the grid line: the GDL parameter AC_Length of the Grid Tool's grid marker, or the object's A size for a library part without it.
  - `xRatio` (number, required): The object's xRatio as stored: its A size with useXYFixSize on, otherwise the A size divided by the library part's own A.
  - `yRatio` (number, required): The object's yRatio as stored, like xRatio for the B size.
  - `useXYFixSize` (boolean, required): Whether xRatio and yRatio hold the sizes themselves.
  - `level` (number, required): Elevation of the object from its home story.
  - `libInd` (integer, required): Library part index.
  - `libraryPartName` (string, required): Localized name of the library part.
  - `parameters` (array of object): GDL parameters, separators left out. Only when requested.

Grasshopper: `GetGridElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetGridElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetGridElements.py): Prints the position, direction, length and library part of every grid element with GetGridElements. Set includeParameters to True to get their GDL parameters as well. Requires Archicad 26 or later.

### CreateGridElements

Creates grid elements, the elements the Grid Tool places, from begin and end coordinates, with optional story, layer and GDL parameters. Needs Archicad 26 or later.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateGridElements

Parameters:

- `gridElements` (array of object, required)
  - `begCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required): Start point of the grid line (the object's insertion point).
  - `endCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required): End point of the grid line. Sets the direction and, unless lengthMode is 'none', the length.
  - `lengthMode` (string ("length", "none")): How the line length is applied. length (default): to the GDL parameter AC_Length when the library part has it, as the Grid Tool's grid marker does; otherwise to the object's A size, converted to xRatio as CreateObjects does. none: the length is left to 'parameters'.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Home story index. Default: the tool default.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Layer attribute index. Only a positive index takes effect. Default: the tool default.
  - `parameters` (array of object): GDL parameters to set by name (read the names with GetGridElementDefaults). The value is a number, a boolean or a string. Unknown names and wrong value types are reported in warnings and skipped. The tool defaults can look different from a grid drawn with the Grid Tool (for example a short line with a leader to the bubble); to get the same look, copy the parameters of such a grid (GetGridElements with includeParameters).

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)
- `warnings` (array of string, required): Parameters that were not set, prefixed with the index of the grid element.

Grasshopper: `CreateGridElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateGridElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateGridElements.py): Creates two crossing 20 m long grid lines with CreateGridElements. The library part comes from the Grid Tool defaults; parameters sets GDL parameters by name (see GetGridElementDefaults). Requires Archicad 26 or later.

### CreateLabels

Creates Label elements based on the given parameters.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.2.5. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateLabels

Parameters:

- `labelsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Labels.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `parentElementId` (ElementId): The parent element if the label is an associative label.
  - `labelClass` (LabelClass): Optional; if omitted, inherits the current Label tool default (which may silently resolve to either class - explicitly setting this avoids ambiguity). 'Symbol' needs a symbol library part, which only the Label tool default or the favorite given in favoriteName can provide: when those are a Text label, the item fails instead of placing a label without content.
  - `text` (string): The text content if the label is a text label. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF. Ignored if 'runs' is also given.
  - `runs` (array of TextRunDetails): Multi-style text content for a text label: an array of styled runs, concatenated in order. Takes precedence over 'text' if both are given.
  - `style` (TextStyleSettableDetails): Ignored for symbol labels.
  - `symbolStyle` (LabelSymbolStyleSettableDetails): Ignored for text labels.
  - `leaderLine` (LabelLeaderLineSettableDetails)
  - `begCoordinate` (Coordinate2D): The begin coordinate of leader line. Optional parameter, but either begCoordinate or parentElementId must be provided. Unless midCoordinate and endCoordinate are both given too, the label is created at its default position relative to the parent element (Archicad's 'createAtDefaultPosition'), so the label may not end up at begCoordinate - read it back with GetDetailsOfElements after creation.
  - `midCoordinate` (Coordinate2D): The mid coordinate of leader line. Optional parameter; give it together with endCoordinate to place the label exactly where the coordinates say.
  - `endCoordinate` (Coordinate2D): The end coordinate of leader line. Optional parameter; give it together with midCoordinate to place the label exactly where the coordinates say.
  - `floorInd` (number): The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor or the floor of the parent element is used.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `LabelElementsComponent`, `LabelsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateLabels.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateLabels.py): Labels the first wall with a text label with CreateLabels. Needs at least one Wall. Without parentElementId the label stands on its own at begCoordinate.

### CreateTexts

Creates standalone Text elements based on the given parameters.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateTexts

Parameters:

- `textsData` (array of any or any, required): Array of data to create Texts.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `coordinate` (Coordinate3D, required): The placement position of the text. The z value is used to determine the floor when floorIndex is omitted.
  - `text` (string): The text content. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF. Ignored if 'runs' is also given.
  - `runs` (array of TextRunDetails): Multi-style text content: an array of styled runs, concatenated in order. Takes precedence over 'text' if both are given.
  - `height` (number): The character height in millimeters. Optional; defaults to the Text tool default. Equivalent to style.height.
  - `pen` (integer): Optional pen attribute index. Equivalent to style.penIndex.
  - `angle` (number): Optional rotation angle in radians. Equivalent to style.angle.
  - `justification` (Justification): Optional; equivalent to style.justification.
  - `style` (TextStyleSettableDetails): height/pen/angle/justification above take precedence over the same fields here if both are given.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the coordinate's z value.

### CreateLevelDimensions

Creates Level Dimension elements (the Level Dimension tool) based on the given parameters. With a parentElementId the dimension is associative: it shows the height of the parent element (Mesh, Slab, Roof ...) at its position and follows the element when it changes.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateLevelDimensions

Parameters:

- `levelDimensionsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Level Dimensions (the Level Dimension tool of the floor plan).
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a Level Dimension favorite to base the new element on. Its settings (marker, format, text style, layer, pen) are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `position` (Coordinate2D, required): The location of the marker on the floor plan. With a parentElementId it must lie on that element, the measured level is the parent's height at this point. Outside the parent's outline Archicad still creates the dimension, but without a height (GetDetailsOfElements reads a level of -110000000).
  - `parentElementId` (ElementId): Optional element the level dimension is associated with (Mesh, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Beam, Column, Wall, Object, Stair ...). The dimension then shows the element's height at the position and follows the element when it changes. Without it the dimension measures the floor level, or the given static level.
  - `level` (number): Optional fixed level value in meters (absolute, from the project zero). Only used without parentElementId; the dimension then shows this value instead of the floor level.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): The index of the floor to place the dimension on. Optional parameter, by default the floor of the parent element, otherwise the current floor is used.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Layer attribute index to place the dimension on. Optional parameter, by default the layer of the favorite or the Level Dimension tool default is used.
  - `pen` (integer): Pen index of the marker. Optional parameter.
  - `textHeight` (number): Height of the dimension text in millimeters (paper size). Optional parameter.
  - `textPen` (integer): Pen index of the dimension text. Optional parameter.
  - `dimForm` (integer): Marker type of the Level Dimension tool, 0-19 as Archicad stores it (read it back with GetDetailsOfElements from an existing level dimension or one placed with a favorite). Optional parameter.
  - `needPlus` (boolean): Show a plus sign for positive values. Optional parameter.
  - `markerSize` (number): Size of the marker in millimeters (paper size). Optional parameter.
  - `angle` (number): Rotation angle of the marker in radians. Optional parameter.
  - `origin` (DimensionOrigin): The origin the level is measured from. Optional parameter.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `LevelDimensionsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateLevelDimensions.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateLevelDimensions.py): Creates a slab and puts an associative level dimension on it with CreateLevelDimensions, plus one showing a fixed level. The associative one shows the slab's level at its position and follows the slab when it changes; level (in meters, from the project zero) is only used without parentElementId.

### ModifyWalls

Modifies Wall elements based on the given parameters.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.4.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyWalls

Parameters:

- `wallsWithDetails` (array of object, required)
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `geometryType` (WallModificationGeometryType): Polygonal is not settable here; it is read-only via GetDetailsOfElements. This is unrelated to slantAlpha/slantBeta - see profileType for the cross section shape those depend on.
  - `begCoordinate` (Coordinate2D)
  - `endCoordinate` (Coordinate2D)
  - `arcAngle` (number): Arc angle in radians; non-zero makes the wall curved (begCoordinate/endCoordinate are the chord endpoints).
  - `height` (number): Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height). Do not combine with relativeTopStory in the same call - whichever is applied last wins, and Archicad recomputes the actual height from the story elevations once relativeTopStory is non-zero.
  - `thickness` (number): Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) wall - a Composite or Profile wall takes its thickness from the composite or profile attribute. Send structureType 'Basic' in the same call to switch such a wall first.
  - `bottomOffset` (number)
  - `offset` (number)
  - `structureType` (WallStructureType)
  - `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId)
  - `compositeId` (AttributeId)
  - `profileId` (AttributeId)
  - `referenceLineLocation` (WallReferenceLineLocation)
  - `flipped` (boolean): True mirrors the wall to its reference line (the side GetDetailsOfElements reports as flipped).
  - `profileType` (WallModificationProfileType): slantAlpha/slantBeta only have an effect once this is set to Slanted.
  - `slantAlpha` (number): Only has an effect once profileType is set to Slanted or Trapez.
  - `slantBeta` (number): Only has an effect once profileType is set to Slanted or Trapez.
  - `topOffset` (number): Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.
  - `relativeTopStory` (number): Non-zero links the wall's top to another story instead of an explicit height - do not set together with 'height' in the same call, see the note on 'height' above.
  - `zoneRel` (WallZoneRelation)
  - `visibility` (StoryVisibility): Confirmed live on Archicad 29 (#852): a wall there knows only 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories' (Wall Settings offers no Custom option), and Archicad silently drops every other combination written here although the command reports success - showAllAbove, showAllBelow, showRelAbove and showRelBelow (any value, 0 included) and showOnHome true -> false all read back unchanged. 'All relevant stories' is isAutoOnStoryVisibility true. 'Home story only' takes two calls: first isAutoOnStoryVisibility true (Archicad resets the custom fields to 0), then isAutoOnStoryVisibility false with visibility { showOnHome: true }. Archicad 30 adds a Custom option for walls; whether the other fields become writable there is untested.
  - `isAutoOnStoryVisibility` (boolean): When true (the default on a new wall), Archicad recomputes 'visibility' automatically from the wall's vertical extent and ignores any value set for it. Setting 'visibility' without also setting this field turns it off automatically. See the note on 'visibility' for which combinations a wall accepts.
  - `referenceMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial)
  - `oppositeMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial)
  - `sideMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial)
  - `cutFillPen` (OverriddenPen)
  - `cutFillBackgroundPen` (OverriddenPen)
  - `contourPen` (integer): Pen of the wall's own contour/reference outline (API_WallType::contPen) - distinct from cutFillPen, which is the cut fill pattern's pen. Not inheritable/overridable like cutFillPen, it is the wall's own pen index directly, the same field regardless of structureType.
  - `contourPen3D` (integer): Pen of the wall's contour in 3D views (API_WallType::contPen3D).
  - `contourLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the wall's own contour (API_WallType::contLtype) - pairs with contourPen, which only sets the pen, not the line type.
  - `belowViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type used when "OutLines Only" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup (API_WallType::belowViewLineType).
  - `aboveViewLinePen` (integer): Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup.
  - `aboveViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.
  - `displayOption` (DisplayOption)
  - `viewDepthLimitation` (ViewDepthLimitation): Only has an effect on a multi-story wall (relativeTopStory/topOffset making it span more than one story).
  - `useCompositePriority` (boolean): When true, the Composite's own priority is used at junctions instead of connectionPriority.
  - `linkToSettings` (LinkToSettings)
  - `inheritEndSurface` (boolean): The end surface of the wall is inherited from the adjoining wall.
  - `alignTexture` (boolean): Align texture mapping to the wall's edges.
  - `polyCanChange` (boolean): The polygonal wall's corners can be changed in case of L and T connections. Only meaningful for a Polygonal wall (geometryType).
  - `materialsChained` (boolean): Whether the surface materials are chained.
  - `logHeight` (number): Height of the log for log walls. 0 means a normal (non-log) wall.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ModifyWallsComponent`, `WallsApiComponent`, `WallsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyWalls.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyWalls.py): Creates a wall, then makes it longer, higher and thicker with ModifyWalls. Only the given fields change. A new thickness only takes effect on a Basic wall.

### ModifyTexts

Modifies standalone Text elements based on the given parameters.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.9. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyTexts

Parameters:

- `textsWithDetails` (array of object, required): Array of Text elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is. A change of the text, the runs, or a run-level style field (pen, font, faces, height, effects) rebuilds the content as one paragraph, which makes the element auto-width (word wrap off), as SetDetailsOfElements does, and on a multi-run text applies that style to every run; the other style fields leave the content as it is.

  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional. Moves the text to this floor; when omitted and a coordinate is given, the floor is derived from its z value.
  - `text` (string): The new text content. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF.
  - `runs` (array of TextRunDetails)
  - `style` (TextStyleSettableDetails)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

### ModifyCurtainWalls

Modifies Curtain Wall elements in place, keeping their GUID, properties and classifications: the height, the bottom elevation and story, the reference line (with the same number of segments), and the column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern with its cell assignments, in the fields of CreateCurtainWalls.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyCurtainWalls

Parameters:

- `curtainWallsWithDetails` (array of object, required): Array of Curtain Wall elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed; the others, and the frames and panels not affected by them, are left as they are. The fields are those of CreateCurtainWalls, so a curtain wall can be changed in place instead of being deleted and recreated, keeping its GUID, properties and classifications.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D): The new 2D coordinates of the reference line of the curtain wall on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates is one straight segment, so the number of coordinates must be the current number of segments plus one: the segments can be moved and resized, but not added or removed (a curved segment becomes straight).
  - `zCoordinate` (number): The new Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the bottom of the curtain wall. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given too.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): The new home story index. On its own it moves the curtain wall to that story, keeping its bottom offset from the story; with zCoordinate it pins the story the bottom elevation is measured from.
  - `height` (number): The new height of the curtain wall.
  - `primaryPattern` (CurtainWallPattern): The new column pattern: the sizes of the columns along the segments (the primary grid). Applied to every segment of the curtain wall; the frames and panels are regenerated from it.
  - `secondaryPattern` (CurtainWallPattern): The new row pattern: the sizes of the rows from the bottom up (the secondary grid). Applied to every segment of the curtain wall; the frames and panels are regenerated from it.
  - `cells` (array of CurtainWallPatternCell): Assignment of panel and frame classes to the cells of the pattern unit of every segment, as in CreateCurtainWalls. Without a pattern change, a cell not listed here keeps its current assignment; with one, it takes the assignment of the first current cell.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `CurtainWallsComponent`, `ModifyCurtainWallsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyCurtainWalls.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyCurtainWalls.py): Creates a curtain wall, then makes it 4 m high with 1 m wide columns with ModifyCurtainWalls. The curtain wall keeps its GUID, properties and classifications.

### ChangeTextContent

Replaces a range of the content of Text elements and text Labels, keeping the styles of the runs and the autotexts in the rest of the content.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ChangeTextContent

Parameters:

- `contentChanges` (array of object, required): The content changes, applied in order (several changes of one element see the content as the previous one left it). Unlike ModifyTexts/ModifyLabels, the rest of the content is not rebuilt: the other runs, their styles and any autotext in them stay as they are, and the inserted piece takes the style of the character at 'from'.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required): A Text element or a Label of the Text class.
  - `from` (integer, required): The position in the content where the replaced range starts.
  - `range` (integer, required): The number of characters to replace; 0 inserts the content at 'from'. The range may not reach over a line end into another paragraph.
  - `content` (string, required): The new content of the range; an empty string deletes the range. It must not contain line ends.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ChangeTextContentComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ChangeTextContent.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ChangeTextContent.py): Creates the text 'Hello World', then replaces 'World' with 'Tapir' with ChangeTextContent. from is the character position, range the number of characters replaced (0 inserts). The styles of the rest of the content and the autotexts in it are kept. A range must stay within one line.

### ModifyZones

Modifies Zone elements: name, number, category, zone stamp, height, base offset, top link and floor thickness. Only the given fields are changed; the polygon is kept.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyZones

Parameters:

- `zonesWithDetails` (array of object, required): Array of Zone elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed; the polygon and the omitted fields are kept. The same fields as the ZoneSettings of SetDetailsOfElements.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `name` (string): Name of the zone.
  - `numberStr` (string): Zone number.
  - `categoryAttributeId` (AttributeId): The identifier of the zone category attribute.
  - `stampPosition` (Coordinate2D): Position of the origin of the zone stamp.
  - `stampAngle` (number): Rotation angle of the zone stamp in radians.
  - `fixedStampAngle` (boolean): If true, the zone stamp angle remains fixed when the element is rotated.
  - `height` (number): Height of the zone from its bottom. Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height), so do not combine it with relativeTopStory in the same call: whichever is applied last wins.
  - `bottomOffset` (number): Base level of the zone relative to its home story level.
  - `topOffset` (number): Offset of the top of the zone from the linked top story level. Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.
  - `relativeTopStory` (number): Non-zero links the top of the zone to another story, relative to its home story (1 is the story above), instead of an explicit height. Do not set together with height in the same call, see the note on height.
  - `floorThickness` (number): Thickness of the floor finish (subfloor thickness) of the zone.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ModifyZonesComponent`, `ZonesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyZones.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyZones.py): Renames and renumbers the first zone with ModifyZones, reads it back, then restores its name and number. Needs at least one Zone. Only the given fields change; the polygon is kept.

### MeasureTexts

Measures texts before placing them: the length of every line for a given font, style and height, on paper in millimetres or in the model at the current drawing scale, and the font's capital size factor. Creates nothing.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#MeasureTexts

Parameters:

- `texts` (array of any or any, required): The texts to measure, each with the font, style and height it would be placed with. Nothing is created.
  - `text` (string, required): The text to measure. Newlines separate lines, each measured on its own; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are treated as LF.
  - `fontIndex` (integer): The index of the font, as GetDetailsOfElements and GetFontsByName report it in fontIndex. One of fontName and fontIndex is required.
  - `fontName` (string): Name of the font as Archicad's font list carries it (GetDetailsOfElements reports it in fontName), which is not always the operating system's font name; GetFontsByName tells whether a name is found. Resolved to the font's index (exact match first, then case-insensitive); the text fails when no loaded font has the name. Takes precedence over fontIndex if both are given. One of fontName and fontIndex is required.
  - `height` (number, required): The character height in millimetres, as a Text's height.
  - `bold` (boolean): Bold style. Optional, default false.
  - `italic` (boolean): Italic style. Optional, default false.
  - `underline` (boolean): Underline style. Optional, default false.
  - `slant` (number): The slant angle of the characters in radians; pi/2 (the default) is upright text.
  - `inModelUnits` (boolean): When true, Archicad applies the drawing scale correction and the lengths are model distances at the current drawing scale; when false (the default), they are lengths on paper in millimetres.

Returns:

- `measurements` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): One item per input text, in the same order. The measurement takes no width factor or character spacing into account.

Grasshopper: `MeasureTextsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/MeasureTexts.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/MeasureTexts.py): Measures the length of each line of a two-line text in Arial 2.5 mm, on paper and in the model, with MeasureTexts. Creates nothing. Model lengths use the drawing scale of the current window.

### SetElementNotificationClient

Sets up a new notification client to receive element events.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.2.8. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetElementNotificationClient

Parameters:

- `host` (string): The host address of the notification client. If not provided, localhost is used.
- `port` (integer, required): The port number of the notification client.
- `notifyOnNewElement` (boolean): Notify on creation of a new element. Optional parameter, by default true.
- `notifyOnModificationOfAnElement` (boolean): Notify on modification/deletion of an element. Optional parameter, by default true.
- `notifyOnReservationChanges` (boolean): Notify on reservation changes of an element. Optional parameter, by default true.


Grasshopper: `SetElementNotificationClientComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetElementNotificationClient.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetElementNotificationClient.py): Prints the element events Archicad sends to a local HTTP server registered with SetElementNotificationClient. Creates a column to trigger a notification, then removes the client again. Archicad posts each event as JSON to http://<host>:<port>/element_notification. Modifications are observed only for columns here (elementTypesToObserve): attaching an observer to every element blocks Archicad for minutes on a project with thousands of elements.

### RemoveElementNotificationClient

Removes an element notification client.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.2.8. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RemoveElementNotificationClient

Parameters:

- `host` (string): The host address of the notification client. If not provided, localhost is used.
- `port` (integer, required): The port number of the notification client.


Grasshopper: `RemoveElementNotificationClientComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RemoveElementNotificationClient.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RemoveElementNotificationClient.py): Registers an element notification client and removes it again with RemoveElementNotificationClient. host and port name the client given to SetElementNotificationClient.

### RegularizePolygons

Regularizes polygons with Archicad's own polygon regularization, before they are used to create slabs, zones or fills: removes duplicate points, fixes the orientation, resolves self-intersections and touching holes. Each input polygon gives 0, 1 or more valid polygons in the format of CreateSlabs, optionally with the input vertex and edge each result vertex and edge came from. Changes nothing in the project.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RegularizePolygons

Parameters:

- `polygons` (array of object, required): The polygons to regularize, in the format of CreateSlabs (polygonCoordinates, polygonArcs, holes). For CreateHatches, pass the outline of a result as its coordinates and arcs.
  - `polygonCoordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The 2D coordinates of the outline. A last coordinate equal to the first is ignored.
  - `polygonArcs` (array of PolyArc): Arcs of the outline.
  - `holes` (Holes2D)
- `withAncestry` (boolean): Also return for every vertex and edge of the results which input vertex or edge it came from. Optional, false by default.

Returns:

- `results` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): One item per input polygon, in the order of the request.

Grasshopper: `RegularizePolygonsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RegularizePolygons.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RegularizePolygons.py): Regularizes a self-intersecting (bow tie) outline with a repeated point with RegularizePolygons. The results are in the format of CreateSlabs; nothing is created.

### RegularizePolylines

Regularizes polylines with Archicad's own polyline regularization: removes repeated consecutive points. The result is in the format of CreatePolylines and may be empty, optionally with the input point and segment each result point and segment came from. Changes nothing in the project.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RegularizePolylines

Parameters:

- `polylines` (array of object, required): The polylines to regularize, in the format of CreatePolylines.
  - `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The 2D coordinates of the polyline.
  - `arcs` (array of PolyArc): The arcs of the polyline.
- `withAncestry` (boolean): Also return for every point and segment of the results which input point or segment it came from. Optional, false by default.

Returns:

- `results` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): One item per input polyline, in the order of the request.

Grasshopper: `RegularizePolylinesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RegularizePolylines.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RegularizePolylines.py): Removes the repeated points of a polyline with RegularizePolylines, and reports which input point each result point came from. The result is in the format of CreatePolylines; nothing is created.

A group without user data gets an error item. Needs at least one grouped Wall.

### SetUserDataOfGroups

Stores string values under keys in the user data of groups, for scripts to keep their own state on a group. The given pairs are merged into what each group already holds: a key that exists gets the new value, other keys are left as they are, and the keys listed in keysToDelete are removed. Prefix the keys with the script's name so that scripts do not overwrite each other's data. User data in another layout is left unchanged and reported as an error. One undo step per call.

Group: Element grouping Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetUserDataOfGroups

Parameters:

- `groups` (array of GroupIdArrayItem, required): The groups to store the pairs on.
- `pairs` (UserDataPairs): The key-value pairs to store on each group. A key the group already holds gets the new value; other keys are left as they are.
- `keysToDelete` (UserDataKeysToDelete)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required): One result per group, in the input order.

Grasshopper: `SetUserDataOfGroupsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/ElementGrouping/SetUserDataOfGroups.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/ElementGrouping/SetUserDataOfGroups.py): Groups the first two Walls, stores a key-value pair on the group with SetUserDataOfGroups and reads it back. The script ungroups the walls again at the end. Needs at least two Walls that are not grouped yet.
