### ImportFavorites

Import Favorites from a .prefs file or folder into the current project. From Archicad 29 they can also be imported from a folder of Favorite files (xml format, all of them or the given fileNames) or from a legacy .prf file (legacyPRF format), with the conflict policies Error, Skip, OverwriteExisting and RenameNew.

Group: Favorites Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ImportFavorites

Parameters:

- `path` (string, required): Absolute path on the AC host. With the prefs format: a Favorites file (.prefs) or folder. With the xml format: the folder of Favorite files, as ExportFavorites writes it. With the legacyPRF format: the .prf file.
- `format` (string ("prefs", "xml", "legacyPRF")): The format to import from, the counterpart of the format of ExportFavorites. prefs (the default) works in every Archicad version. xml imports Favorite files from a folder, and legacyPRF a Favorites file of earlier Archicad versions; these two require Archicad 29 or newer.
- `fileNames` (array of string): Only with the xml format: the names of the Favorite files in the folder to import. Default: every Favorite file of the folder.
- `targetFolder` (array of string): Folder hierarchy under which to import. Empty = root. With the xml and legacyPRF formats the folder must exist, and omitting it keeps the folders stored with the Favorites.
- `importFolders` (boolean): Only with the prefs format: if true and `path` is a folder, the folder structure is preserved.
- `conflictPolicy` (string ("Error", "Skip", "Overwrite", "Append", "OverwriteExisting", "RenameNew")): How to resolve name conflicts. The prefs format takes Error, Skip, Overwrite or Append, default Overwrite. The xml and legacyPRF formats take Error, Skip, OverwriteExisting or RenameNew, default Error.

Returns:

- `firstConflictName` (string): Set when conflictPolicy=Error and a name collided; absent otherwise.

Grasshopper: `ImportFavoritesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Favorites/ImportFavorites.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Favorites/ImportFavorites.py): Imports a Favorite from a .prefs file with ImportFavorites. Needs at least one Wall. The script creates the Favorite 'Tapir Example Wall' from the first wall, exports it to a temporary file, deletes it, imports it again from the file and finally deletes it.

### ExportFavorites

Export the project's Favorites to a .prefs file or folder. From Archicad 29 they can also be exported to a folder of Favorite files (xml format) or to a legacy .prf file (legacyPRF format).

Group: Favorites Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ExportFavorites

Parameters:

- `path` (string, required): Absolute path on the AC host. With the prefs format: if extension matches the Favorite binary format (.prefs), writes a single file; otherwise treats as folder. With the xml format: the folder to write the Favorite files to. With the legacyPRF format: the .prf file to write.
- `names` (array of string): Optional subset of Favorites to export. Default: export all.
- `format` (string ("prefs", "xml", "legacyPRF")): The format to export to. prefs (the default) works in every Archicad version. xml exports each Favorite to its own file in the folder, and legacyPRF exports to a Favorites file of earlier Archicad versions; these two require Archicad 29 or newer.


Grasshopper: `ExportFavoritesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Favorites/ExportFavorites.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Favorites/ExportFavorites.py): Exports the Wall Favorites of the project to a .prefs file with ExportFavorites. Needs a Wall Favorite. The file is written into a new temporary folder.

### ApplyFavoritesToElements

Apply the given favorites to existing elements. Only settings-type parameters are changed - geometry (position, floor, and dimensions such as a Wall's height) is left untouched, so applying a Favorite never moves the target element. A Window or Door keeps its wall, marker and placement, and takes the Favorite's library part and parameters, size included. For the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own geometry. By default settings, classifications, categories and properties are all applied; each can be opted out of individually. keepFields lists fields of the target (its ID, layer, an opening's width, height and sill height, a Wall's reference line location, height and top link) that are copied back after the Favorite has been applied, so that e.g. only the library part or the wall type changes.

Group: Favorites Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.4. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ApplyFavoritesToElements

Parameters:

- `favoritesToApply` (array of object, required)
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `favorite` (string, required)
- `applySettings` (boolean): Whether to apply the Favorite's settings-type parameters (structure, materials, pens, etc.). Geometry (position, floor, and dimensions such as a Wall's height) is never applied - the element stays on its own home story - except that a Window or Door takes the Favorite's library part and parameters, size included, while keeping its wall, marker and placement. For the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own geometry. A Dimension's text size, text pen and text frame are not changed (tested in Archicad 28): the dimension creation commands take textHeight and textPen for them. Default is true.
- `applyClassifications` (boolean): Whether to apply the Favorite's classifications. Default is true.
- `applyCategories` (boolean): Whether to apply the Favorite's element categories (e.g. IFC categories). Default is true.
- `applyProperties` (boolean): Whether to apply the Favorite's property values. Default is true.
- `keepFields` (array of string ("id", "layerIndex", "width", "height", "sillHeight", "referenceLineLocation", "topOffset", "relativeTopStory")): Fields of the target element to keep: after the Favorite has been applied, they are copied back from the target as it was before, so only the Favorite's other settings (e.g. its library part or wall type) take effect. 'id' and 'layerIndex' apply to every element type; 'width', 'height' and 'sillHeight' to a Window or Door ('width' and 'height' also to a Skylight); 'height', 'topOffset' and 'relativeTopStory' to a Wall or Column; 'referenceLineLocation' to a Wall. A field the target's type does not have is ignored. To keep a Wall's or Column's top exactly as it was, keep 'height', 'relativeTopStory' and 'topOffset' together - a kept 'height' alone is recomputed by Archicad while the Favorite's relativeTopStory links the top to a story. Default: nothing is kept.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ApplyFavoritesToElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Favorites/ApplyFavoritesToElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Favorites/ApplyFavoritesToElements.py): Applies the first Wall Favorite to a new wall with ApplyFavoritesToElements, keeping the wall's height. Needs a Wall Favorite. The wall is created by the script and deleted at the end.

### CreateFavorite

Creates a Favorite in the given folder from the settings of another Favorite or of the current Opening tool default. conflictPolicy says what happens when the name is taken: fail, skip, overwrite the existing Favorite's settings or create the new one under a free name. Available from Archicad 29.

Group: Favorites Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateFavorite

Parameters:

- `name` (string, required): The name of the new Favorite.
- `folder` (array of string): The folder of the Favorites palette to create the Favorite in, as the folder names from the root down. The folder must exist. Empty or omitted = root.
- `source` (object, required): Where the settings of the new Favorite come from: exactly one of favoriteName and toolDefault.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Take the settings of this Favorite.
  - `toolDefault` (string ("Opening")): Take the current settings of this tool.
- `conflictPolicy` (string ("Error", "Skip", "OverwriteExisting", "RenameNew")): What to do when a Favorite with this name already exists: Error fails, Skip leaves the existing Favorite unchanged, OverwriteExisting gives the existing Favorite the new settings (its folder does not change), RenameNew creates the Favorite with ' (2)', ' (3)', ... appended to the name. Default Error.

Returns:

- `name` (string, required): The name of the Favorite: the given name, or the new name with RenameNew.
- `folder` (array of string): The folder of the Favorite, as the folder names from the root down. Empty for the root. Missing when Archicad cannot read it.
- `outcome` (string ("Created", "Skipped", "Overwritten"), required): Created for a new Favorite (also with RenameNew), Skipped or Overwritten when a Favorite with the name already existed.

Grasshopper: `CreateFavoriteComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Favorites/CreateFavorite.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Favorites/CreateFavorite.py): Creates a copy of the first Favorite of the project with CreateFavorite, then deletes it. Needs a Favorite. RenameNew picks a free name when the name is taken. Requires Archicad 29 or later.

## Property Commands

### GetAllProperties

Returns all user defined and built-in properties. Optionally only the given properties or property types, and without the availability lists.

Group: Property Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetAllProperties

Parameters:

- `properties` (PropertyIds): Returns only the definitions of these properties. Identifiers not found in the project are left out of the response. All properties are returned when omitted.
- `propertyTypes` (array of string ("StaticBuiltIn", "DynamicBuiltIn", "Custom")): Returns only the properties of these types. All types are returned when omitted.
- `includeAvailability` (boolean): Adds the availability list (the classification items a custom property is available for) to each custom property. Default is true.

Returns:

- `properties` (array of PropertyDetails, required): A list of property identifiers.
- `propertyGroups` (array of PropertyGroupDetails): Every property group, including empty ones.

Grasshopper: `ElementMetadata`, `FindPropertyByGuidComponent`, `FindPropertyByName`, `GetAllPropertiesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Property/GetAllProperties.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Property/GetAllProperties.py): Lists the group and name of every custom property of the project with GetAllProperties.

### GetPropertyValuesOfElements

- `properties` (PropertyIds, required)

Returns:

### AddPropertyToAttributes

Makes an existing custom property available for the given attributes (for example Building Materials), in one undo step. Available in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 only.

Group: Property Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#AddPropertyToAttributes

Parameters:

- `propertyId` (PropertyId, required): An existing custom property. Create it first with CreatePropertyDefinitions if needed.
- `attributeIds` (AttributeIds, required): The attributes (for example Building Materials) to make the property available for.


Grasshopper: `AddPropertyToAttributesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Property/AddPropertyToAttributes.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Property/AddPropertyToAttributes.py): Makes a custom property available for the first Building Material with AddPropertyToAttributes, then removes it again. Needs a custom property that the Building Material does not have yet. Requires Archicad 25, 26 or 27.

### RemovePropertyFromAttributes

Makes a custom property unavailable for the given attributes (for example Building Materials), in one undo step. Available in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 only.

Group: Property Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RemovePropertyFromAttributes

Parameters:

- `propertyId` (PropertyId, required)
- `attributeIds` (AttributeIds, required): The attributes (for example Building Materials) to make the property unavailable for.


Grasshopper: `RemovePropertyFromAttributesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Property/RemovePropertyFromAttributes.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Property/RemovePropertyFromAttributes.py): Makes a custom property unavailable for the first Building Material with RemovePropertyFromAttributes. The script first makes a property available that the Building Material does not have yet, so the project ends as it was. Requires Archicad 25, 26 or 27.

### CreatePropertyGroups

Creates Property Groups based on the given parameters.

### DeletePropertyGroups

### CreatePropertyDefinitions

Creates Custom Property Definitions based on the given parameters.

Group: Property Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.9. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreatePropertyDefinitions

Deletes the given Custom Property Definitions.

### UpdatePropertyDefinitions

Updates existing Custom Property Definitions in place, keeping their guid: name, description, group, default value or expressions, availability, and enum options (add, rename, remove, reorder).

Group: Property Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.4. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#UpdatePropertyDefinitions

Parameters:

- `propertyDefinitions` (array of PropertyDefinitionUpdate, required): The property definitions to update. Only the fields given change; the definition keeps its guid, so element values survive.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `UpdatePropertyDefinitionsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Property/UpdatePropertyDefinitions.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Property/UpdatePropertyDefinitions.py): Creates a temporary custom property and changes its name, description, default value and editability with UpdatePropertyDefinitions. The property keeps its guid. The script deletes the property and its group again at the end.

### UpdatePropertyGroups

Updates the name and/or description of existing Custom Property Groups, keeping their guid.

Group: Property Commands. Added in Tapir 1.6.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#UpdatePropertyGroups

Returns:

Grasshopper: `UpdatePropertyGroupsComponent`

### ImportPropertiesXml

Imports a Property Manager XML export, with the given policy for names that already exist. Returns the property definitions it created and removed.

Group: Property Commands. Added in Tapir 1.6.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ImportPropertiesXml

Parameters:

- `xml` (string, required): A Property Manager export (XML) to import.
- `conflictPolicy` (PropertyImportConflictPolicy, required)

Returns:

- `executionResult` (ExecutionResult, required)
- `created` (array of GuidId, required)
- `removed` (array of GuidId, required)

Grasshopper: `ImportPropertiesXmlComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Property/ImportPropertiesXml.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Property/ImportPropertiesXml.py): Imports a group with one text property from Property Manager XML with ImportPropertiesXml, then deletes them. conflictPolicy 'skip' keeps a property whose name already exists in its group.

### ModifyPropertyValueOfElements

Sets one property value on all the given elements in a single step. If the property is not available for any of the elements, none of them is changed. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Property Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyPropertyValueOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): The elements to set the value on. The property must be available for every one of them.
- `propertyId` (PropertyId, required)
- `propertyValue` (PropertyValue, required)


Grasshopper: `ModifyPropertyValueOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Property/ModifyPropertyValueOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Property/ModifyPropertyValueOfElements.py): Sets the same Element ID on the first three Walls in one step with ModifyPropertyValueOfElements, then restores their values. Needs at least one Wall.

### GetPropertyAvailabilityOfDefaults

Tells whether the given properties are available and whether they are visible in the current tool default of an element type, before creating new elements. It checks the native tool default only, not a Favorite that is not applied. Unknown properties are reported as errors, not as unavailable. Available from Archicad 26.

Group: Property Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetPropertyAvailabilityOfDefaults

Parameters:

- `elementType` (ElementType, required): The element type whose current tool default is checked. This is the native tool default, a Favorite counts only after it was applied.
- `properties` (PropertyIds, required)

Returns:

- `propertyAvailabilities` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The order is that of the given properties.

Grasshopper: `GetPropertyAvailabilityOfDefaultsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Property/GetPropertyAvailabilityOfDefaults.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Property/GetPropertyAvailabilityOfDefaults.py): Tells whether the custom properties of the project are available and visible in the Wall tool default with GetPropertyAvailabilityOfDefaults. Requires Archicad 26 or later.

### MakePropertyAvailableForElements

Makes a property definition available for all the given elements. Available only in Archicad 27.

Group: Property Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#MakePropertyAvailableForElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): The elements to make the property available for.
- `propertyId` (PropertyId, required)


Grasshopper: `MakePropertyAvailableForElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Property/MakePropertyAvailableForElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Property/MakePropertyAvailableForElements.py): Makes a custom property available for the first Wall with MakePropertyAvailableForElements, then unavailable again. Needs a Wall and a custom property that is not available for it. Requires Archicad 25, 26 or 27.

### MakePropertyUnavailableForElements

Makes a property definition unavailable for all the given elements. Available only in Archicad 27.

Group: Property Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#MakePropertyUnavailableForElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): The elements to make the property unavailable for.
- `propertyId` (PropertyId, required)


Grasshopper: `MakePropertyUnavailableForElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Property/MakePropertyUnavailableForElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Property/MakePropertyUnavailableForElements.py): Makes a custom property unavailable for the first Wall with MakePropertyUnavailableForElements. The script first makes a property available that is not available for the wall, so the project ends as it was. Requires Archicad 25, 26 or 27.


## Classification Commands

### GetClassificationsOfElements

Returns the classification of the given elements in the given classification systems. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also.

Group: Classification Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetClassificationsOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `classificationSystemIds` (ClassificationSystemIds, required)

Returns:

- `elementClassifications` (ElementClassificationsOrErrors, required): Order of the ids are the same as in the input. Non-existing elements or non-existing classification systems are represented by error objects.

Grasshopper: `GetClassificationsOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/GetClassificationsOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/GetClassificationsOfElements.py): Reads the classification of the first three Walls in every classification system with GetClassificationsOfElements. Needs at least one Wall.

### GetElementsByClassification

Returns the elements classified with the given classification items, one list per item, so elements can be filtered by classification in a single call.

Group: Classification Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementsByClassification

Parameters:

- `classificationItemIds` (ClassificationItemIds, required)

Returns:

- `elementsOfClassificationItems` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The elements classified with each classification item, aligned with the input, or an error for a non-existing classification item.

Grasshopper: `GetElementsByClassificationComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/GetElementsByClassification.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/GetElementsByClassification.py): Lists the elements that are classified like the first Wall with GetElementsByClassification. Needs a classified Wall.

### SetClassificationsOfElements

Sets the classifications of elements. In order to set the classification of an element to unclassified, omit the classificationItemId field. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also.

Group: Classification Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetClassificationsOfElements

Parameters:

- `elementClassifications` (ElementClassifications, required)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `SetClassificationsOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/SetClassificationsOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/SetClassificationsOfElements.py): Classifies the first Wall with the first item of the first classification system with SetClassificationsOfElements, then restores its classification. Needs at least one Wall and a classification system with an item.

### GetClassificationsOfAttributes

Returns the classifications of the given attributes (building materials, composites, surfaces, etc.) in every classification system they are classified in.

Group: Classification Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetClassificationsOfAttributes

Parameters:

- `attributeIds` (AttributeIds, required)

Returns:

- `attributeClassifications` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The classifications of the attributes, in the order of the input. A non-existing attribute is represented by an error object.

Grasshopper: `GetClassificationsOfAttributesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/GetClassificationsOfAttributes.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/GetClassificationsOfAttributes.py): Reads the classifications of the first three Building Materials in every classification system with GetClassificationsOfAttributes.

### SetClassificationsOfAttributes

Sets the classifications of attributes (building materials, composites, surfaces, etc.). The given item replaces the attribute's current item in the same classification system. In order to set the classification of an attribute to unclassified in a system, omit the classificationItemId field.

Group: Classification Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetClassificationsOfAttributes

Parameters:

- `attributeClassifications` (array of object, required): The classifications to set, one per attribute and classification system.
  - `attributeId` (AttributeId, required)
  - `classificationId` (ClassificationId, required): The classification to set. The item replaces the attribute's current item in the same classification system. If the classificationItemId field is omitted, the attribute becomes unclassified in the given system.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `SetClassificationsOfAttributesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/SetClassificationsOfAttributes.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/SetClassificationsOfAttributes.py): Classifies the first Building Material with the first item of the first classification system with SetClassificationsOfAttributes, then restores it. Needs a classification system with an item.

### GetClassificationOfAttributesInSystem

Returns the classification of the given attributes (for example Building Materials) in the given classification system. classificationItemId is omitted for an unclassified attribute.

Group: Classification Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetClassificationOfAttributesInSystem

Parameters:

- `attributeIds` (AttributeIds, required)
- `classificationSystemId` (ClassificationSystemId, required)

Returns:

- `attributeClassifications` (ClassificationIdsOrErrors, required): Order of the items is the same as in the input. classificationItemId is omitted when the attribute is unclassified in the system. Non-existing attributes or a non-existing classification system are represented by error objects.

Grasshopper: `GetClassificationOfAttributesInSystemComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/GetClassificationOfAttributesInSystem.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/GetClassificationOfAttributesInSystem.py): Reads the classification of the first three Building Materials in the first classification system with GetClassificationOfAttributesInSystem.

### GetClassificationsOfElementDefaults

Returns the classification of the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of the given element types in the given classification systems.

Group: Classification Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetClassificationsOfElementDefaults

Parameters:

- `elementTypes` (array of ElementType, required): The element types whose tool defaults (the settings new elements get) are read.
- `classificationSystemIds` (ClassificationSystemIds, required)

Returns:

- `elementDefaultClassifications` (ElementClassificationsOrErrors, required): Order of the outer list is that of the given element types, the inner list that of the given classification systems. Invalid element types or non-existing classification systems are represented by error objects.

Grasshopper: `GetClassificationsOfElementDefaultsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/GetClassificationsOfElementDefaults.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/GetClassificationsOfElementDefaults.py): Reads the classification of the Wall and Slab tool defaults in every classification system with GetClassificationsOfElementDefaults.

### SetClassificationsOfElementDefaults

Sets the classifications of the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of the given element types. In order to set a default to unclassified, omit the classificationItemId field.

Group: Classification Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetClassificationsOfElementDefaults

Parameters:

- `elementDefaultClassifications` (array of object, required): The classifications to set on the tool defaults (the settings new elements get).
  - `elementType` (ElementType, required)
  - `classificationId` (ClassificationId, required)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `SetClassificationsOfElementDefaultsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/SetClassificationsOfElementDefaults.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/SetClassificationsOfElementDefaults.py): Classifies the Wall tool default with the first item of the first classification system with SetClassificationsOfElementDefaults, then restores it. New walls get the tool default's classification. Needs a classification system with an item.

### GetClassificationsOfToolDefaults

Returns every classification of the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of the given element types, in all classification systems at once. Unlike GetClassificationsOfElementDefaults it needs no list of classification systems; systems in which a default is unclassified are left out.

Group: Classification Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetClassificationsOfToolDefaults

Parameters:

- `elementTypes` (array of ElementType, required): The element types whose tool defaults (the settings new elements get) are read.

Returns:

- `classificationsOfToolDefaults` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The classifications of the tool defaults of each element type, in the order of the given element types. Invalid element types are represented by error objects.

Grasshopper: `GetClassificationsOfToolDefaultsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/GetClassificationsOfToolDefaults.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/GetClassificationsOfToolDefaults.py): Reads every classification of the Wall, Slab and Column tool defaults in one call with GetClassificationsOfToolDefaults.

### GetAllClassificationSystems

Returns the classification systems of the project with their guid, name, description, source, version and date. Same output as the official GetAllClassificationSystems command, so scripts can rely on Tapir commands only.

Group: Classification Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetAllClassificationSystems

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `classificationSystems` (array of object, required): The classification systems of the project.
  - `classificationSystemId` (ClassificationSystemId, required)
  - `name` (string, required): The display name of the classification system.
  - `description` (string, required): The description of the classification system.
  - `source` (string, required): The source of the classification system (e.g. URL to a classification system standard).
  - `version` (string, required): The version of the classification system.
  - `date` (Date, required): The release date of the classification system's current version.

Grasshopper: `GetClassificationSystemsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/GetAllClassificationSystems.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/GetAllClassificationSystems.py): Lists the name, version and date of every classification system of the project with GetAllClassificationSystems.

### GetClassificationItemVisibility

Tells whether the given classification items are visible (offered) for the given elements, element tool defaults and attributes, such as building materials. Non-existing targets and classification items are reported as errors. Visibility does not tell whether the target is classified with the item, and an item can be visible even if its parent item is not.

Group: Classification Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetClassificationItemVisibility

Parameters:

- `targets` (array of object or object or object, required): The elements, element tool defaults and attributes to check the classification items for.
- `classificationItemIds` (ClassificationItemIds, required)

Returns:

- `classificationItemVisibilities` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): One entry per target, in the order of the input. A non-existing element or attribute, or an invalid element type, is represented by an error object.

Grasshopper: `GetClassificationItemVisibilityComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/GetClassificationItemVisibility.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Classification/GetClassificationItemVisibility.py): Tells whether the first item of the first classification system is offered for the first Wall, the Wall tool default and the first Building Material with GetClassificationItemVisibility. Needs at least one Wall.


## Attribute Commands

### GetAttributesByType

Returns the details of every attribute of the given type. From Archicad 30 an attribute that Archicad keeps a creation record of also carries creationInfo: how (method), from where (source), by whom and when it was created.

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetAttributesByType

Parameters:

- `attributeType` (AttributeType, required)

### GetAttributesFromProject

Reads the attributes of the given types from another project or template file without opening it, for example to compare them with the attributes of the open project. Nothing is imported into the open project. The names are the legacy 8-bit names, so non-ASCII characters may not come through. Archicad does not read Layer, Surface, BuildingMaterial and MEPSystem attributes from a file that is not open: these types get an error item instead of an empty list. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetAttributesFromProject

Parameters:

- `projectFilePath` (string, required): The absolute path of the project or template file (for example .pln or .tpl) to read the attributes from.
- `attributeTypes` (array of AttributeType, required): The attribute types to read. Layer, Surface, BuildingMaterial and MEPSystem cannot be read from a file that is not open; they get an error item.


Grasshopper: `GetAttributesFromProjectComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/GetAttributesFromProject.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/GetAttributesFromProject.py): Reads the line types and fills of another project or template file with GetAttributesFromProject, without opening it. Set the TAPIR_ATTRIBUTE_SOURCE environment variable to the absolute path of a .pln or .tpl file. Nothing is imported into the open project. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

Gets the attributes in use, as Archicad reports them for the usedAttributes JSON query: parsed into usedAttributes when the report is a JSON object, otherwise as text in raw. Helps to find the attributes DeleteAttributes can remove before a handover. Available from Archicad 27.

### MoveAttributesAndFolders

Moves attributes and attribute folders (with their contents) into the target folder, which must be of the same attribute type; an empty target path is the root folder. Returns one execution result per attribute and per folder. Available from Archicad 26.

### CreateLayers

Creates or overwrites Layer attributes based on the given parameters.

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateLayers

- `layerDataArray` (array of object, required): Array of data to create new Layers.
  - `attributeId` (AttributeId): Indentifier of the existing Layer to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.
  - `index` (string): Index of the existing Layer to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.
  - `name` (string, required): Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Layer with the given name will be overwritten.
  - `isHidden` (boolean): Hide/Show.
  - `isLocked` (boolean): Lock/Unlock.
  - `isWireframe` (boolean): Force the model to wireframe.
  - `intersectionGroupNr` (integer): Intersection group. Elements on layers having the same group will be intersected.
- `overwriteExisting` (boolean): Overwrite the Layer if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

Returns:

- `attributeIds` (AttributeIdsOrErrors, required)

Overwrites the layer of the same name when the script is run again.

### CreateLayerCombinations

Creates or overwrites Layer Combination attributes based on the given parameters.

  - `layers` (LayersOfLayerCombination): Layer states to set. Layers not listed keep their current state when overwriting an existing Layer Combination (or get the default visible/unlocked state for a new one), so this can be omitted to e.g. only rename an existing Layer Combination.

Overwrites the layer combination of the same name when the script is run again.

### CreateLines

Creates or overwrites Line attributes based on the given parameters.

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.4. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateLines

Parameters:

- `lineDataArray` (array of object, required): Array of data to create new Lines.
  - `attributeId` (AttributeId): Indentifier of the existing Line to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.
  - `index` (string): Index of the existing Line to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.
  - `name` (string, required): Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Line with the given name will be overwritten.
  - `scaleWithPlan` (boolean): If true, the line type parameters are defined in meters at the given defineScale and scale on printout with the actual plan scale. If false (default), the parameters are fixed values in millimeters as the line will appear on the printout.
  - `defineScale` (number): The floor plan scale the line type is defined with. Only used if scaleWithPlan is true.
  - `lineType` (string): Solid, Dashed, or Symbol. Defaults to Solid.
  - `period` (number): The length of one period (Dashed and Symbol line types).
  - `height` (number): The height of the symbol line (Symbol line type only).
  - `dashItems` (array of LineDashItem): Dash-gap pairs describing one period (Dashed line type only).
  - `lineItems` (array of LineSymbolItemData): Symbol items describing one period (Symbol line type only).
- `overwriteExisting` (boolean): Overwrite the Line if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

Returns:

- `attributeIds` (AttributeIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateLinesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/CreateLines.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/CreateLines.py): Creates a dashed Line type (3 mm dash, 1.5 mm gap on the printout) with CreateLines. Overwrites the line type of the same name when the script is run again.

### CreateFills

Creates or overwrites Fill attributes based on the given parameters.

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.4. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateFills

Parameters:

- `fillDataArray` (array of object, required): Array of data to create new Fills.
  - `attributeId` (AttributeId): Indentifier of the existing Fill to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.
  - `index` (string): Index of the existing Fill to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.
  - `name` (string, required): Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Fill with the given name will be overwritten.
  - `subType` (string): Vector, Solid, Empty, Symbol, LinearGradient, RadialGradient, or Image. Defaults to Vector. Only one Solid and one Empty fill may exist. Image fills use the texture field's name to reference the image library part.
  - `scaleWithPlan` (boolean): The fill is scale dependent.
  - `useForWalls` (boolean): This fill can be used for cut fills.
  - `useForDraft` (boolean): This fill can be used for drafting fills.
  - `useForCover` (boolean): This fill can be used for cover fills.
  - `horizontalSpacing` (number): The fill's spacing factor in the X direction (Vector fills).
  - `verticalSpacing` (number): The fill's spacing factor in the Y direction (Vector fills).
  - `angle` (number): The angle of the fill in radians (Vector, Symbol, and gradient fills).
  - `bitPattern` (string): 16 hex characters (8 bytes) describing the fill's bitmap pattern, one line of the pattern per byte, matching the Pattern field of the Attribute Manager XML export.
  - `gradientStart` (Coordinate2D): Gradient start point (LinearGradient/RadialGradient fills only).
  - `gradientEnd` (Coordinate2D): Gradient end point (LinearGradient/RadialGradient fills only).
  - `symbolOffset1` (Coordinate2D): First offset vector of the repeating symbol motif, X1/Y1 in the Fill Types dialog (Symbol fills only).
  - `symbolOffset2` (Coordinate2D): Second offset vector of the repeating symbol motif, X2/Y2 in the Fill Types dialog (Symbol fills only).
  - `percent` (number): Translucency percentage [0..1] (gradient and some Solid fills).
  - `texture` (Texture): Used for Image and gradient fills. Only name, rotationAngle, xSize, ySize, mirrorX, and mirrorY are used for Fills.
  - `lineItems` (array of FillLineItem): Vectorial fill line items (Vector fills only).
  - `symbolLines` (array of FillSymbolLine): Line items of the fill's repeating symbol pattern (Symbol fills only).
  - `symbolArcs` (array of FillSymbolArc): Arc items of the fill's repeating symbol pattern (Symbol fills only).
  - `symbolHotspots` (array of Coordinate2D): Hotspot coordinates of the fill's repeating symbol pattern (Symbol fills only).
- `overwriteExisting` (boolean): Overwrite the Fill if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

Returns:

- `attributeIds` (AttributeIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateFillsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/CreateFills.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/CreateFills.py): Creates a vectorial hatching Fill of parallel lines at 45 degrees with CreateFills. Overwrites the fill of the same name when the script is run again.

### CreatePenTables

Creates or overwrites Pen Table attributes based on the given parameters.

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.4. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreatePenTables

Parameters:

- `penTableDataArray` (array of object, required): Array of data to create new Pen Tables.
  - `attributeId` (AttributeId): Indentifier of the existing Pen Table to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.
  - `index` (string): Index of the existing Pen Table to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.
  - `name` (string, required): Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Pen Table with the given name will be overwritten.
  - `isActiveForModel` (boolean): Make this the active Pen Table for the model window. Defaults to false for a new Pen Table, or to the current value when overwriting an existing one.
  - `isActiveForLayout` (boolean): Make this the active Pen Table for layouts. Defaults to false for a new Pen Table, or to the current value when overwriting an existing one.
  - `sourceAttributeId` (AttributeIdArrayItem): Identifier of the Pen Table whose 255 pens are used as the starting point, before the pens listed in the pens array are applied on top. Defaults to the Pen Table being overwritten itself (so unlisted pens keep their current color/width/description), or an arbitrary existing Pen Table in the project when creating a brand new one (or a plain black, 0.1 mm pen for all 255 if the project has no Pen Table at all yet).
  - `pens` (array of PenData): The pens to set in the Pen Table, on top of the 255 pens copied from sourceAttributeId (or the current Pen Table, or an arbitrary existing one - see sourceAttributeId). Only list the pens you actually want to change.
- `overwriteExisting` (boolean): Overwrite the Pen Table if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

Returns:

- `attributeIds` (AttributeIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreatePenTablesComponent`

Only the given fields of a listed pen are changed. In a Teamwork project the PenTables lockable object set must be reserved first (see ReserveLockableObjectSet).

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyPens

Parameters:

- `pens` (array of PenData, required): The pens to change in the active Pen Table. Only the given fields (color, width, description) of a listed pen are changed; every other pen of the table is left as it is.
- `target` (string ("model", "layout")): Which active Pen Table to change: the one in effect for the model views (the default) or the one in effect for the layouts. The two can be the same Pen Table.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

In a Teamwork project the PenTables lockable object set must be reserved first.

### CreateProfiles

Creates or overwrites Profile attributes as a copy of an existing Profile's geometry, based on the given parameters.

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.4. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateProfiles

Parameters:

- `profileDataArray` (array of object, required): Array of data to create new Profiles.
  - `attributeId` (AttributeId): Indentifier of the existing Profile to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.
  - `index` (string): Index of the existing Profile to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.
  - `name` (string, required): Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Profile with the given name will be overwritten.
  - `sourceAttributeId` (AttributeIdArrayItem): Identifier of an existing Profile whose geometry (cross-section shape) will be copied as the starting point. Optional if newSkins is given: omit it to build the Profile's geometry entirely from newSkins instead of copying anything (AC27+ only).
  - `wallType` (boolean): Profile available for walls. Defaults to the source Profile's value.
  - `beamType` (boolean): Profile available for beams. Defaults to the source Profile's value.
  - `coluType` (boolean): Profile available for columns. Defaults to the source Profile's value.
  - `handrailType` (boolean): Profile available for handrails. Defaults to the source Profile's value.
  - `otherGDLObjectType` (boolean): Profile available for other GDL based objects. Defaults to the source Profile's value.
  - `skinOverrides` (array of object): Modifications to apply to specific skins of the copied geometry, e.g. to change a skin's building material without rebuilding the profile's shape. Each skinId comes from a prior GetProfiles call's skins[].skinId on the source Profile (or, when overwriteExisting is true, on the Profile being overwritten).
  - `newSkins` (array of ProfileSkinData): AC27+ only. Adds brand-new skins built from caller-supplied polygon geometry, instead of (or in addition to) whatever was copied from sourceAttributeId. Combine with sourceAttributeId to add skins to a copied Profile, or omit sourceAttributeId to build a Profile's geometry entirely from newSkins.
  - `replaceSkins` (boolean): AC27+ only. When overwriteExisting targets an existing Profile, discard every one of its existing skins (and any sourceAttributeId geometry given alongside it) before applying newSkins, instead of adding newSkins on top of the preserved existing geometry. Use this to fully replace a Profile's cross-section with a caller-authored shape while keeping its guid and scalar fields (wallType etc.) - e.g. to sync a Profile's geometry from another project, where sourceAttributeId can't be used because it only resolves within the same file. Also discards any existing profileModifiers, since those are tied to the specific geometry being replaced. Ignored when creating a brand-new Profile (there is nothing to discard yet).
- `overwriteExisting` (boolean): Overwrite the Profile if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

Returns:

- `attributeIds` (AttributeIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateProfilesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/CreateProfiles.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/CreateProfiles.py): Creates a Profile as a copy of the first Profile of the project, usable for walls and beams, with CreateProfiles. Overwrites the Profile of the same name when the script is run again.

### CreateBuildingMaterials

Creates or overwrites Building Material attributes based on the given parameters.

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateBuildingMaterials

Parameters:

- `buildingMaterialDataArray` (array of object, required): Array of data to create new Building Materials.
  - `attributeId` (AttributeId): Indentifier of the existing Building Material to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.
  - `index` (string): Index of the existing Building Material to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.
  - `name` (string, required): Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Building Material with the given name will be overwritten.
  - `id` (string): Identifier.
  - `manufacturer` (string): Manufacturer.
  - `description` (string): Decription.
  - `connPriority` (integer): Intersection priority.
  - `cutFillIndex` (integer): Index of the Cut Fill.
  - `cutFillPen` (integer): Cut Fill Foreground Pen.
  - `cutFillBackgroundPen` (integer): Cut Fill Background Pen.
  - `cutSurfaceIndex` (integer): Index of the Cut Surface.
  - `thermalConductivity` (number): Thermal Conductivity.
  - `density` (number): Density.
  - `heatCapacity` (number): Heat Capacity.
  - `embodiedEnergy` (number): Embodied Energy.
  - `embodiedCarbon` (number): Embodied Carbon.
  - `showUncutLines` (boolean): Show Contours in Model Views.
  - `collisionDetection` (boolean): Whether the Building Material participates in collision detection.
  - `cutFillOrientation` (string): ProjectOrigin, ElementOrigin, or FitToSkin. Orientation of the cut fill.
- `overwriteExisting` (boolean): Overwrite the Building Material if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

Returns:

- `attributeIds` (AttributeIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateBuildingMaterialsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/CreateBuildingMaterials.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/CreateBuildingMaterials.py): Creates a Building Material with its cut fill, cut surface and physical properties with CreateBuildingMaterials. Overwrites the Building Material of the same name when the script is run again.

### CreateComposites

Creates or overwrites Composite attributes based on the given parameters.

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateComposites

Parameters:

- `compositeDataArray` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Composites.
  - `attributeId` (AttributeId): Indentifier of the existing Composite to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.
  - `index` (string): Index of the existing Composite to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.
  - `name` (string, required): Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Composite with the given name will be overwritten.
  - `useWith` (array of string): Array of types the composite can used with. If omitted when overwriting an existing Composite, its current setting is kept.
  - `skins` (array of object): Array of skin data. Required when creating a new Composite. If omitted when overwriting an existing Composite, its current skins are kept.
  - `separators` (array of object): Array of skin separator data. The number of items must be the number of skins plus one. Required when creating a new Composite. If omitted when overwriting an existing Composite, its current separators are kept (only possible if the number of skins does not change).
- `overwriteExisting` (boolean): Overwrite the Composite if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

Returns:

- `attributeIds` (AttributeIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateCompositesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/CreateComposites.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/CreateComposites.py): Creates a two-skin wall Composite (core and finish) with CreateComposites. Uses the first two Building Materials and the first line type of the project. Overwrites the Composite of the same name when the script is run again.

### CreateSurfaces

Creates or overwrites Surface attributes based on the given parameters.

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.2.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateSurfaces

Parameters:

- `surfaceDataArray` (array of object, required): Array of data to create new surfaces.
  - `attributeId` (AttributeId): Indentifier of the existing Surface to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.
  - `index` (string): Index of the existing surface to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.
  - `name` (string, required): Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing surface with the given name will be overwritten.
  - `materialType` (SurfaceType)
  - `ambientReflection` (number): Ambient percentage [0..100].
  - `diffuseReflection` (number): Diffuse percentage [0..100].
  - `specularReflection` (number): Specular percentage [0..100].
  - `transparency` (number): Transparency percentage [0..100].
  - `shine` (number): The shininess factor multiplied by 100 [0..10000].
  - `transparencyAttenuation` (number): Transparency attenuation multiplied by 100 [0..10000].
  - `emissionAttenuation` (number): Emission attenuation multiplied by 100 [0..10000].
  - `surfaceColor` (ColorRGB)
  - `specularColor` (ColorRGB)
  - `emissionColor` (ColorRGB)
  - `fillId` (AttributeIdArrayItem)
  - `texture` (Texture)
- `overwriteExisting` (boolean): Overwrite the Surface if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.

Returns:

- `attributeIds` (AttributeIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateSurfacesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/CreateSurfaces.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/CreateSurfaces.py): Creates a green, matte Surface with CreateSurfaces. Overwrites the Surface of the same name when the script is run again.

Gets graphic override rules by name, with their rule group, criterion and style. The rule group narrows the search; without it the rule is searched in every rule group. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetGraphicOverrideRulesByName

Parameters:

- `graphicOverrideRules` (array of object, required): The graphic override rules to get, by name.
  - `name` (string, required): The name of the rule. Rule names are unique within the project.
  - `ruleGroupName` (string): The name of the rule group to search the rule in. Left out: every rule group is searched.

Returns:

- `graphicOverrideRules` (array of GraphicOverrideRuleOrError, required): The rules, or errors, in the order of the input.

Grasshopper: `GetGraphicOverrideRulesByNameComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/GetGraphicOverrideRulesByName.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/GetGraphicOverrideRulesByName.py): Gets the first graphic override rule of the project by its name with GetGraphicOverrideRulesByName. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### CreateGraphicOverrideRules

Creates graphic override rules. The criterion is given as Archicad's criterion XML or as structured conditions. The rule group is created when no rule group has the given name. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateGraphicOverrideRules

Parameters:

- `graphicOverrideRules` (array of object, required): The graphic override rules to create.
  - `name` (string, required): The name of the rule, unique within the project.
  - `ruleGroupName` (string, required): The name of the rule group to put the rule in. Created when it does not exist.
  - `criterionXML` (string): The criterion of the rule, in the XML format Archicad saves override rules in. Take it from GetGraphicOverrideRules and change its values: Archicad drops XML written from scratch without an error, and the rule then applies to all elements. Left out together with 'criterion': Archicad's default criterion for new rules.
  - `criterion` (GraphicOverrideCriterion): The criterion of the rule as structured conditions, turned into Archicad's criterion XML. Use it instead of criterionXML, not with it.
  - `style` (GraphicOverrideStyle)

Returns:

- `graphicOverrideRuleIds` (array of GraphicOverrideRuleIdOrError, required): The identifiers of the created rules, or errors, in the order of the input.

Grasshopper: `CreateGraphicOverrideRulesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/CreateGraphicOverrideRules.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/CreateGraphicOverrideRules.py): Creates a graphic override rule that paints walls higher than 2.5 m red with CreateGraphicOverrideRules. The rule is given by structured conditions; the script deletes it again at the end. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### ModifyGraphicOverrideRules

Modifies the name, criterion or style of graphic override rules. The criterion is given as Archicad's criterion XML or as structured conditions. A given style replaces the whole style of the rule. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyGraphicOverrideRules

Parameters:

- `graphicOverrideRules` (array of object, required): The graphic override rules to modify.
  - `graphicOverrideRuleId` (GraphicOverrideRuleId, required)
  - `name` (string): The new name of the rule.
  - `criterionXML` (string): The new criterion of the rule, in the XML format Archicad saves override rules in. Take it from GetGraphicOverrideRules and change its values: Archicad drops XML written from scratch without an error, and the rule then applies to all elements.
  - `criterion` (GraphicOverrideCriterion): The new criterion of the rule as structured conditions, turned into Archicad's criterion XML. Use it instead of criterionXML, not with it.
  - `style` (GraphicOverrideStyle)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ModifyGraphicOverrideRulesComponent`

### GetUserDataOfAttributes

Reads the key-value pairs stored on attributes by SetUserDataOfAttributes. An attribute without user data returns no pairs; one holding user data in another layout returns an error.

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetUserDataOfAttributes

Parameters:

- `attributeIds` (AttributeIds, required)

Returns:

- `userDataOfAttributes` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): One item per attribute, in the input order: the pairs stored on the attribute (none when it holds no user data), or an error when the attribute was not found or holds user data in another layout.

Grasshopper: `GetUserDataOfAttributesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/GetUserDataOfAttributes.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/GetUserDataOfAttributes.py): Reads the key-value pairs scripts stored on the first three Layers with GetUserDataOfAttributes.

### SetUserDataOfAttributes

Stores string values under keys in the user data of attributes, for scripts to keep their own state on an attribute. The given pairs are merged into what each attribute already holds: a key that exists gets the new value, other keys are left as they are, and the keys listed in keysToDelete are removed. Prefix the keys with the script's name so that scripts do not overwrite each other's data. User data in another layout is left unchanged and reported as an error. Archicad does not record this change as an undo step, so Undo does not revert it.

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetUserDataOfAttributes

Parameters:

- `attributeIds` (AttributeIds, required)
- `pairs` (UserDataPairs): The key-value pairs to store on each attribute. A key the attribute already holds gets the new value; other keys are left as they are.
- `keysToDelete` (UserDataKeysToDelete)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required): One result per attribute, in the input order.

Grasshopper: `SetUserDataOfAttributesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/SetUserDataOfAttributes.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/SetUserDataOfAttributes.py): Stores a key-value pair on the first Layer with SetUserDataOfAttributes, reads it back, then removes the key. Undo does not revert user data changes.

### DeleteUserDataOfAttributes

Removes the user data of attributes, every key at once. Archicad does not record this change as an undo step, so Undo does not revert it.

Group: Attribute Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteUserDataOfAttributes

Parameters:

- `attributeIds` (AttributeIds, required)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required): One result per attribute, in the input order.

Grasshopper: `DeleteUserDataOfAttributesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/DeleteUserDataOfAttributes.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/DeleteUserDataOfAttributes.py): Creates a temporary Layer with user data and removes all its user data with DeleteUserDataOfAttributes. DeleteUserDataOfAttributes removes every key, also those of other scripts, and Undo does not revert it, so the script works on a layer it creates and deletes.


## IFC Commands

### IFCFileOperation

Executes an IFC file operation: opens or merges an IFC file, or saves the project as an IFC file. A save can name the export translator to use.

Group: IFC Commands. Added in Tapir 1.2.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#IFCFileOperation

Parameters:

- `method` (string ("save", "merge", "open"), required): The file operation method to use.
- `ifcFilePath` (string, required): The target IFC file to use.
- `fileType` (string ("ifc", "ifcxml", "ifczip", "ifcxmlzip")): The type of the IFC file. The default is 'ifc'.
- `translatorName` (string): Only for the save method: the name of the IFC export translator to save with, as GetIFCExportTranslators lists them. Without it the save runs with the translator Archicad would offer in its own Save dialog. Needs a fileType of ifc or ifczip (ifc or ifcxml on Archicad 25 and 26).
- `elementsToExport` (IFCElementsToExport): Only for the save method, and only together with translatorName. The default is VisibleElementsOnAllStories.


Grasshopper: `IFCFileOperationComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/IFC/IFCFileOperation.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/IFC/IFCFileOperation.py): Saves the project as an IFC file with IFCFileOperation, using the first IFC export translator of the project. The file is written into a new temporary folder. The open and merge methods take the same ifcFilePath; open replaces the open project.

### GetIFCExportTranslators

Lists the IFC export translators of the project, the preview translator first. Pass one of the names to IFCFileOperation as translatorName.

Group: IFC Commands. Added in Tapir 1.6.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetIFCExportTranslators

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `translators` (array of IFCExportTranslator, required): The IFC export translators of the project, the preview translator first.

Grasshopper: `GetIFCExportTranslatorsComponent`

Needs at least one Wall. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27.

### SetIFCPropertiesOfElements

Sets local IFC properties on elements by creating or modifying single value (IfcPropertySingleValue) properties in the given property sets. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now.

Group: IFC Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetIFCPropertiesOfElements

Parameters:

- `elementIFCPropertyValues` (array of object, required): The IFC property values to set. Only single value (IfcPropertySingleValue) properties are supported.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `propertySetName` (string, required): The name of the property set, for example Pset_DoorCommon. Custom property set names are also accepted.
  - `propertyName` (string, required): The name of the property, for example FireRating.
  - `type` (string, required): The IFC type of the value, for example IfcLabel, IfcText, IfcIdentifier, IfcBoolean, IfcLogical, IfcInteger, IfcReal or a measure type like IfcThermalTransmittanceMeasure. A type Archicad does not know is rejected.
  - `value` (any, required): The new value of the property. Provide a boolean for IfcBoolean and IfcLogical (IfcLogical also accepts the string Unknown), a number for the numeric types and a string for every other type.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `SetIFCPropertiesOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/IFC/SetIFCPropertiesOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/IFC/SetIFCPropertiesOfElements.py): Sets a local IFC property of the first wall with SetIFCPropertiesOfElements and reads it back. Needs at least one Wall. The property 'Tapir_Example / Note' is removed again at the end. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27.

### GetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements

Retrieves the IFC classification references of the given elements, subelements included: identification, name, location, description (from Archicad 29), the referenced classification (name, source, edition) and whether the reference comes from the preview translator or is stored locally. On Archicad 25, 26 and 27 the source is not given, the referenced classification also has its edition date, description and location, and storedOnly returns only the references stored on the elements.

Group: IFC Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `storedOnly` (boolean): Return only the classification references stored on the elements, not the ones Archicad would generate on IFC export. Used only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27. Default: false.

Returns:

- `elementIFCClassificationReferences` (ElementIFCClassificationReferencesOrErrors, required)

Needs at least one Wall.

### SetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements

Stores IFC classification references (identification, name, location and the referenced classification with its name, edition, edition date, description and location) on elements. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now.

  - `name` (string): The name of the classification reference. Default: empty.

Needs at least one Wall. The reference is removed again at the end. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27.

### RemoveIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements

Removes IFC classification references stored on elements, given by the name of their classification and optionally their identification; without identification every stored reference of that classification is removed. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now.

  - `referencedSource` (object, required): The classification (IfcClassification) the reference belongs to.
  - `identification` (string): The identification of the classification reference to remove. When it is not given, every stored reference of the classification is removed from the element.

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Needs at least one Wall. The removed reference is stored by the script first. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27.

### ReloadLibraries

Executes the reload libraries command.

Group: Library Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ReloadLibraries

Parameters: none.


Grasshopper: `ReloadLibrariesComponent`

### AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary

Adds the given files into the embedded library. With the overwriteExisting flag an embedded library item already existing on an outputPath is replaced (Archicad 27 or newer).

Group: Library Commands. Added in Tapir 1.2.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary

Parameters:

- `files` (LibraryFileAdditions, required)
- `overwriteExisting` (boolean): Optional. When true, an embedded library item already existing on an outputPath is deleted first, so the newly added file replaces the loaded library part. By default false: the existing loaded part stays in use. Requires Archicad 27 or newer.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `AddFilesToEmbeddedLibraryComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Library/AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Library/AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary.py): Adds a small PNG file to the embedded library with AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary. The image is written to a temporary folder first and deleted from the embedded library at the end (the deletion requires Archicad 27 or later).

### DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems

Deletes the given items from the embedded library. The path of an item is the same relative path that AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary takes as outputPath. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Library Commands. Added in Tapir 1.6.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems

Parameters:

- `embeddedLibraryItems` (array of object, required): A list of embedded library items to delete.
  - `path` (string, required): The relative path of the library item inside the embedded library, the same path AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary takes as outputPath.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItemsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Library/DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Library/DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems.py): Adds a small PNG file to the embedded library, then deletes it again with DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### CreateLibraryParts

Creates GDL library parts in the embedded library from their scripts (master, 2D, 3D, parameter, interface, properties) and parameter definitions, under the given parent subtype. The new parts are placeable right away, e.g. with CreateObjects. With the overwriteExisting flag an embedded library item already existing on the path of a new part is replaced (Archicad 27 or newer).

Group: Library Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateLibraryParts

Parameters:

- `libraryParts` (array of object, required): The library parts to create in the embedded library.
  - `name` (string, required): The name of the new library part, as shown in the library and used by CreateObjects as libraryPartName.
  - `parentId` (string): The parent subtype of the new library part: its unique ID ('{main}-{revision}') or its main GUID, as GetAvailableLibraryParts reports it. Either parentId or parentName is required.
  - `parentName` (string): The document name of the parent subtype, e.g. 'General Object' or 'General Label' from the Archicad Library; used when parentId is not given.
  - `type` (LibraryPartType): Optional. The type of the new library part. By default the type of the parent found by parentName or by a parentId GUID, and Object otherwise.
  - `path` (string): Optional. The relative path of the .gsm file inside the embedded library, the same kind of path AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary takes as outputPath. By default '<name>.gsm'.
  - `a` (number): Optional. The default value of the A (X size) parameter. 1.0 by default.
  - `b` (number): Optional. The default value of the B (Y size) parameter. 1.0 by default.
  - `masterScript` (string): Optional. The GDL master script.
  - `script2D` (string): Optional. The GDL 2D script.
  - `script3D` (string): Optional. The GDL 3D script.
  - `parameterScript` (string): Optional. The GDL parameter script (value lists, locks, hiding).
  - `uiScript` (string): Optional. The GDL user interface script.
  - `propertiesScript` (string): Optional. The GDL properties (component listing) script.
  - `parameters` (array of object): Optional. The parameters of the library part besides A and B, in the order they appear in the settings dialog. Only simple (non-array) parameters can be defined.
- `overwriteExisting` (boolean): Optional. When true, an embedded library item already existing on the path of a new library part is deleted first, so the new one replaces the loaded library part. By default false: creating on an existing path fails. Requires Archicad 27 or newer.

Returns:

- `libraryParts` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The created library parts, in the order of the input, or the error of each one that could not be created.

Grasshopper: `CreateLibraryPartsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Library/CreateLibraryParts.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Library/CreateLibraryParts.py): Creates a GDL box object in the embedded library with CreateLibraryParts, then deletes it again. The parent subtype is the 'General GDL Object' of the loaded Archicad Library. Deleting the part at the end requires Archicad 27 or later.

### CreateFolderInEmbeddedLibrary

Creates a folder, with any missing parent folders, inside the embedded library. The folderPath is relative to the embedded library, like the outputPath of AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary.

Group: Library Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateFolderInEmbeddedLibrary

Parameters:

- `folderPath` (string, required): The path of the folder relative to the embedded library, for example 'Office/Doors'. Missing parent folders are created too; folders that already exist are kept.


Grasshopper: `CreateFolderInEmbeddedLibraryComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Library/CreateFolderInEmbeddedLibrary.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Library/CreateFolderInEmbeddedLibrary.py): Creates the folder 'TapirExamples/Created Folder' in the embedded library with CreateFolderInEmbeddedLibrary. Missing parent folders are created too. The empty folder stays in the embedded library.

### CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary

Copies the given files, keeping their names, into a folder of the embedded library with one library operation. The target folder is created when it is missing. With overwriteIfExists an item of the same name in that folder is replaced.

Group: Library Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary

Parameters:

- `files` (array of object, required): The files to copy. Each keeps its file name inside the target folder.
  - `path` (string, required): The absolute path of the file to copy.
- `targetFolder` (string): Optional. The folder relative to the embedded library to copy the files into, for example 'Office/Doors'. Missing folders are created. By default the root of the embedded library.
- `overwriteIfExists` (boolean): Optional. When true, an item with the same name in the target folder is replaced. By default false.


Grasshopper: `CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibraryComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Library/CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Library/CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary.py): Copies two PNG files into a folder of the embedded library with CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary. The files are written to a temporary folder first; the copies are deleted from the embedded library at the end (the deletion requires Archicad 27 or later).

### SetLibraries

Makes the given folders the project's local libraries; built-in, embedded, server and web libraries are kept. Set the libraries before opening a file that needs them and the missing-library dialog does not appear.

The original list of local libraries is set back at the end. Built-in, embedded, server and web libraries are not touched.

Adds the given folders to the project's local libraries, skipping any already loaded.

Group: Library Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.9. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#AddLibraries
