### SetLibraryPartScripts

Sets and deletes the master, parameter, 2D, 3D, properties, interface and forward and backward migration scripts of loaded library parts. Only the given scripts are changed; an empty script makes the section empty, deleteScripts removes it. A library part that is not editable (e.g. a part of a library package or a read-only library) is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: Library Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetLibraryPartScripts

Parameters:

- `libraryParts` (array of any or any, required): The library parts to modify, with the scripts to set and to delete in each.
  - `name` (string, required): The name of the loaded library part file with its extension, as returned in the fileName field of GetAvailableLibraryParts (e.g. 'My Door.gsm').
  - `scripts` (object): Optional. The scripts to set. Only the scripts given here are changed, the others are kept. An empty string makes that script section empty, it does not delete it; use deleteScripts for that.
  - `deleteScripts` (array of string ("master", "parameter", "2d", "3d", "properties", "interface", "forwardMigration", "backwardMigration")): Optional. The script sections to delete from the library part. A script cannot be both set in scripts and deleted here.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `SetLibraryPartScriptsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Library/SetLibraryPartScripts.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Library/SetLibraryPartScripts.py): Sets the 2D and 3D scripts of a library part with SetLibraryPartScripts and reads them back. The library part is created in the embedded library by the script and deleted at the end. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### SetLibraryPartPictures

Deletes the preview picture, the GDL pictures (and from Archicad 29 their dark variants) or the 2D symbol of a loaded library part, or copies the 2D symbol from another library part. A library part that is not editable is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28.

- `deleteDarkPreviewPicture` (boolean): Optional. When true, the preview picture for the dark user interface is deleted. Requires Archicad 29 or newer.
- `deleteGdlPictures` (boolean): Optional. When true, all GDL pictures are deleted.
- `deleteDarkGdlPictures` (boolean): Optional. When true, all GDL pictures for the dark user interface are deleted. Requires Archicad 29 or newer.
- `copy2DSymbolFrom` (string): Optional. The name of another loaded library part (fileName with extension); its 2D symbol (the drawn 2D vector image) replaces this part's 2D symbol.

The library part is created in the embedded library by the script and deleted at the end. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### GetLibraryPartCustomSection

Gets a custom section of a loaded library part by its section identifier and index: whether it exists, its data version and its content as base64. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: Library Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetLibraryPartCustomSection

Most library parts have no such section, so the response usually says it does not exist. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### SetLibraryPartCustomSection

Creates, replaces or deletes a custom section of a loaded library part. The content is given as base64. A library part that is not editable is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: Library Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetLibraryPartCustomSection

Parameters:

- `name` (string, required): The name of the loaded library part file with its extension, as returned in the fileName field of GetAvailableLibraryParts (e.g. 'My Door.gsm').
- `sectionId` (integer, required): The type identifier of the custom section. A four-character code is given as its integer value, the first character in the highest byte (e.g. 'ABCD' is 1094861636).
- `index` (integer): Optional. The index of the section among the sections with the same identifier. By default 0.
- `dataVersion` (integer): Optional. The data version stored with the section. By default 0. Only used with data.
- `data` (string): The new content of the section, base64 encoded. The section is created when it does not exist, otherwise replaced. Give either data or delete.
- `delete` (boolean): When true, the section is deleted. Give either data or delete.


Grasshopper: `SetLibraryPartCustomSectionComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Library/SetLibraryPartCustomSection.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Library/SetLibraryPartCustomSection.py): Writes a custom section into a library part with SetLibraryPartCustomSection, reads it back and deletes it. The library part is created in the embedded library by the script and deleted at the end. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### CreateLibraryPart

Creates a new library part file (.gsm) of the given loaded subtype, inheriting its parameters, and reports whether it is loaded with its index and names. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: Library Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateLibraryPart

Parameters:

- `path` (string, required): The full path of the new library part file. It must end with .gsm, must not exist yet, and its folder must exist.
- `ancestorSubtype` (string, required): The name of a loaded library part that is a subtype, with its extension, as returned in the fileName field of GetAvailableLibraryParts. The new object is of this subtype and inherits its parameters.

Returns:

- `isLoaded` (boolean, required): Whether the new library part is loaded in the project. It is only loaded when its folder is in a loaded library; otherwise only the file was created.
- `libraryPart` (object): The new library part, in the same form as in GetAvailableLibraryParts. Left out when it is not loaded.
  - `guid` (string, required)
  - `index` (integer, required)
  - `documentName` (string, required)
  - `fileName` (string, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateLibraryPartComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Library/CreateLibraryPart.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Library/CreateLibraryPart.py): Creates a new .gsm file of the 'General GDL Object' subtype with CreateLibraryPart. The file is created in a temporary folder that is added to the library list for the time of the script, so the new part is loaded; the folder is removed from the list at the end. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### OpenLibraryPartInEditor

Opens a loaded library part, given by its fileName or documentName as returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts, in Archicad's library part editor. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Library Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#OpenLibraryPartInEditor

Parameters:

- `name` (string, required): The name of the loaded library part to open: its fileName (with extension, e.g. 'My Object.gsm') or its documentName, as returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts.


Grasshopper: `OpenLibraryPartInEditorComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Library/OpenLibraryPartInEditor.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Library/OpenLibraryPartInEditor.py): Opens the first loaded door library part in Archicad's library part editor with OpenLibraryPartInEditor. Opens a new window in Archicad. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### ReserveLockableObjectSet

Reserves a non-element lockable object set (attributes, favorites, project info, project preferences, etc.) in Teamwork mode. The object set is given by its Archicad API name, e.g. 'Composites', 'LayerSettingsDialog' or 'ProjectInfo'.

Group: Teamwork Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ReserveLockableObjectSet

Parameters:

- `objectSetName` (string, required): The name of the lockable object set, as the Archicad API documents it: BuildingMaterials, Cities, Composites, Favorites, FillTypes, LayerSettingsDialog (layers and layer combinations), LineTypes, MarkupStyles, MEPSystems, ModelViewOptions, OperationProfiles, PenTables, Profiles, ProjectInfo, GeoLocation (project location), PreferencesDialog (project preferences and dimension standards), GraphicOverrides (renovation override styles), Surfaces or ZoneCategories. Other names the Archicad API accepts work too.

Returns:

- `executionResult` (ExecutionResult, required)
- `conflicts` (array of User): The users whose reservation prevented reserving the object set.

Grasshopper: `ReserveLockableObjectSetComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Teamwork/ReserveLockableObjectSet.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Teamwork/ReserveLockableObjectSet.py): Reserves the Favorites of a Teamwork project with ReserveLockableObjectSet. Needs an open Teamwork project. Favorites that were free before are released again at the end.

### ReleaseLockableObjectSet

Releases a non-element lockable object set reserved with ReserveLockableObjectSet in Teamwork mode.

Group: Teamwork Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ReleaseLockableObjectSet

Parameters:

- `objectSetName` (string, required): The name of the lockable object set, as the Archicad API documents it: BuildingMaterials, Cities, Composites, Favorites, FillTypes, LayerSettingsDialog (layers and layer combinations), LineTypes, MarkupStyles, MEPSystems, ModelViewOptions, OperationProfiles, PenTables, Profiles, ProjectInfo, GeoLocation (project location), PreferencesDialog (project preferences and dimension standards), GraphicOverrides (renovation override styles), Surfaces or ZoneCategories. Other names the Archicad API accepts work too.


Grasshopper: `ReleaseLockableObjectSetComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Teamwork/ReleaseLockableObjectSet.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Teamwork/ReleaseLockableObjectSet.py): Reserves the Composites of a Teamwork project and releases them again with ReleaseLockableObjectSet. Needs an open Teamwork project.

### GetLockableObjectSetStatus

Returns the Teamwork reservation status of a non-element lockable object set and the users who hold it.

Group: Teamwork Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetLockableObjectSetStatus

Parameters:

- `objectSetName` (string, required): The name of the lockable object set, as the Archicad API documents it: BuildingMaterials, Cities, Composites, Favorites, FillTypes, LayerSettingsDialog (layers and layer combinations), LineTypes, MarkupStyles, MEPSystems, ModelViewOptions, OperationProfiles, PenTables, Profiles, ProjectInfo, GeoLocation (project location), PreferencesDialog (project preferences and dimension standards), GraphicOverrides (renovation override styles), Surfaces or ZoneCategories. Other names the Archicad API accepts work too.

Returns:

- `status` (string ("Free", "Editable", "Locked", "NotAvailable", "NotExist"), required): Free: nobody has reserved it. Editable: the current user has reserved it. Locked: another user has reserved it (see conflicts). NotAvailable: the Teamwork server is offline or not available. NotExist: there is no Teamwork connection, for example the project is not a Teamwork project. An unknown object set name is reported as an error, not as a status.
- `conflicts` (array of User): The users who hold a reservation on the object set.

Grasshopper: `GetLockableObjectSetStatusComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Teamwork/GetLockableObjectSetStatus.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Teamwork/GetLockableObjectSetStatus.py): Gets the Teamwork reservation status of a few lockable object sets with GetLockableObjectSetStatus, and who holds them.

In a solo project isShared and isOnline are false.

### CreateLayout

Creates Layouts and their backing master layouts. Archicad inserts a new layout at the first place of its subset, renumbering the sheets after it; previousNavigatorItemId or position 'last' places it after an existing sheet or at the end instead. A custom layout number does not leave the layout out of the numbering; layoutParameters.doNotIncludeInNumbering does.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.4.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateLayout

Parameters:

- `layoutsData` (array of object, required)
  - `masterLayoutName` (string)
  - `masterNavigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId)
  - `layoutName` (string, required)
  - `parentNavigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId)
  - `previousNavigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId): The sibling after which the new layout is placed, as in MoveNavigatorItem. It must be a child of parentNavigatorItemId (or of the Layout Book root when that is omitted). Cannot be combined with position.
  - `position` (string ("first", "last")): Where to place the new layout under its parent. Archicad inserts new layouts at the first place, which renumbers the sheets after them; "last" appends it after the existing children instead. Cannot be combined with previousNavigatorItemId.
  - `paperWidth` (number): Optional paper width in mm, used together with paperHeight. Sets the size of the new layout, and of the master layout when this command creates it from masterLayoutName: a new master starts with the template's default size, which layoutParameters cannot change. An existing master keeps its size. Wins over layoutParameters.horizontalSize.
  - `paperHeight` (number): Optional paper height in mm, used together with paperWidth. See paperWidth. Wins over layoutParameters.verticalSize.
  - `layoutParameters` (object)

Returns:

- `databases` (DatabaseIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateLayoutComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateLayout.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateLayout.py): Creates a layout at the end of the Layout Book with CreateLayout, then deletes it again. Needs at least one master layout.

### CreateDrawings

Creates Drawing elements on the specified or active layout from navigator items.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.4.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateDrawings

Parameters:

- `drawingsData` (array of object, required)
  - `navigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required)
  - `layoutDatabaseId` (DatabaseId)
  - `name` (string): Custom title name of the new Drawing. Giving a name implies nameType CustomName unless nameType is set explicitly.
  - `nameType` (DrawingNameType): Defaults to CustomName when name is given, otherwise to the Drawing tool's current default.
  - `position` (Coordinate2D, required)
  - `scale` (number): Scale ratio applied to the drawing relative to its source view (API_DrawingType::ratio). Defaults to 1.0.
  - `angle` (number): Rotation angle of the drawing in radians. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.
  - `drawingScale` (number): The nominal scale of the drawing. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.
  - `modelOffset` (Coordinate2D): Offset of the model origin within the drawing. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.
  - `clipPolygon` (array of Coordinate2D): Optional polygon to clip the drawing with, in layout coordinates (meters on the layout, the same coordinate system as position) - not the coordinates of the source view's model. Stored as given: position, angle, scale and modelOffset are not applied to it.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateDrawingsComponent`, `DrawingsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateDrawings.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateDrawings.py): Places the first story of the project as a Drawing on the first layout with CreateDrawings. Needs at least one layout. Deletes the new Drawing at the end.

### ChangeDrawingLink

Relinks a Drawing to a different source navigator item. Archicad has no in-place relink API, so this recreates the Drawing against the new source and deletes the original - the returned elementId is a NEW guid, not the input one. The Drawing Title marker's own position is not preserved (undocumented Archicad limitation). The new source view is made current before the Drawing is created (Archicad 27 or later), and the window and story that were active when the command started are restored afterwards; the view settings (zoom, layers, scale) shown in that window are not restored.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ChangeDrawingLink

Parameters:

- `drawingsWithNewLinks` (array of object, required)
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `navigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required)
  - `layoutDatabaseId` (DatabaseId, required)

Returns:

- `elements` (array of ElementIdOrError, required): One result per input item. On success, elementId is the NEW Drawing's identifier - relinking necessarily replaces the element, it cannot keep the original guid.

Grasshopper: `ChangeDrawingLinkComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/ChangeDrawingLink.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/ChangeDrawingLink.py): Places a Drawing of the first story on a layout, then links it to the second story with ChangeDrawingLink. Needs at least two stories and a layout. ChangeDrawingLink recreates the Drawing, so it returns a new element id. Deletes the Drawing at the end.

### CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap

Clones Project Map viewpoints into a specified View Map folder.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap

Parameters:

- `viewsData` (array of object, required): Array of views to clone from the Project Map to the View Map.
  - `navigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required): Navigator item ID of the Project Map viewpoint to clone.
  - `parentNavigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required): Navigator item ID of the View Map folder to place the clone in. Required - Archicad's CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap API leaves a clone created directly at the View Map root in a broken state (it cannot be deleted or moved afterwards, by API or by hand), so Tapir refuses to fall back to the root on your behalf. Create a View Map folder (CreateViewMapFolder) first if you don't already have one to target.

Returns:

- `navigatorItems` (array of NavigatorItemIdOrError, required)

Deletes the clone and the folder at the end.

Creates independent (non-clone) navigator views in a specified View Map folder, by copying database and settings from source items.

  - `parentNavigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required): View Map folder to place the new view in. Create a View Map folder (CreateViewMapFolder) first if you don't already have one to target.

### Set3DCutPlanes

Sets the 3D cut planes. An empty cutPlanes array switches the 3D cut off.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.3.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#Set3DCutPlanes

Parameters:

- `cutPlanes` (array of object): The cut planes. An empty array switches the 3D cut off. The side of a plane its normal vector points to is cut away and the other side is kept (to be confirmed in Archicad). pd is in meters.
  - `pa` (number, required): Coefficient of x in the plane equation. The x coordinate of the normal vector of the plane.
  - `pb` (number, required): Coefficient of y in the plane equation. The y coordinate of the normal vector of the plane.
  - `pc` (number, required): Coefficient of z in the plane equation. The z coordinate of the normal vector of the plane.
  - `pd` (number, required): Constant term in the plane equation, in meters. The distance of the plane from the origin along the normal vector.

An empty cutPlanes array switches the 3D cut off.

### Create3DStyles

Creates 3D styles. Each new style starts from the current 3D style and differs from it only in the given fields. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#Create3DStyles

Parameters:

- `styles` (array of object, required): The 3D styles to create. Each starts from the current 3D style; only the given fields differ from it.
  - `name` (string, required): The name of the 3D style, unique within the project.
  - `engineId` (integer): The id of the 3D rendering engine (API_3DStyle.engineId).
  - `model3D` (integer): The 3D model type: Block, Wireframe, Hidden Line or Shading, as the integer value of API_3DModelTypeID.
  - `transparency` (boolean): Transparency in shading.
  - `monochromeEnabled` (boolean): The model is shown in monochrome colors.
  - `monochromeSurfaceColor` (ColorRGB): The surface color of the monochrome model.
  - `monochromeContourColor` (ColorRGB): The contour color of the monochrome model.
  - `backgroundAsInRendering` (boolean): The background is the same as in the rendering settings.
  - `chainBackgroundColors` (boolean): The sky and the ground background colors are chained.
  - `backgroundSkyColor` (ColorRGB): The sky color of the background (API_3DStyle.bkgSkyColor).
  - `backgroundColor` (ColorRGB): The (ground) color of the background (API_3DStyle.backGroundRGB).
  - `shadingContours` (integer): The contours in shaded mode, as the integer value of API_ShadingContoursID.
  - `vectorialSunShadow` (integer): The vectorial sun shadow options, as the integer value of API_VectorShadowID.
  - `vectorialHatching` (boolean): Vectorial 3D hatching is on.
  - `contourThickness` (integer): The thickness of the contours, in pixels.
  - `silhouetteThickness` (integer): The thickness of the silhouettes, in pixels.
  - `vectorialHatchingThickness` (integer): The thickness of the vectorial hatching, in pixels.
  - `shadowContourThickness` (integer): The thickness of the shadow contours, in pixels.
  - `castShadowPercent` (integer): The intensity of the cast shadows, in percent.
  - `shadingPercent` (integer): The intensity of the shading, in percent.
  - `shadowElevation` (number): The elevation of the shadow plane, used by the one level vectorial sun shadow options.
  - `show3DHotSpotsOnly` (boolean): Only the 3D hotspots are shown.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `Create3DStylesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/Create3DStyles.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/Create3DStyles.py): Creates a white monochrome 3D style with black contours, based on the current style, with Create3DStyles. ### Get3DProjectionSettings

Gets the 3D projection settings of the 3D window: whether it is perspective or axonometric, the camera and target position, view cone, roll angle, distance and azimuth of a perspective, or the transformation matrix of an axonometry.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#Get3DProjectionSettings

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `isPersp` (boolean, required): True for a perspective projection, false for an axonometric one.
- `cameraElementId` (ElementId): The Camera element the projection was set from. Missing when the projection does not come from a camera.
- `activeCameraSetElementId` (ElementId): The active Camera Set element. Missing when there is none.
- `perspective` (PerspectiveProjectionParameters): The perspective parameters. Present only when isPersp is true.
- `axonometric` (object): The parameters of an axonometric projection. Present only when isPersp is false.
  - `transformationMatrix` (array of number, required): The 3x4 transformation matrix of the axonometric projection, row by row (12 numbers).

- `settings` (object, required): The settings to change, in the form Get3DFilterAndCutSettings returns. Only the given keys are changed.
  - `firstStory3D` (integer): The first story shown.
  - `lastStory3D` (integer): The last story shown.
  - `allStories` (boolean): Whether all stories are shown; if false, firstStory3D to lastStory3D.
  - `trimToStoryRange` (boolean)
  - `filterMode` (string ("FilterByRules", "FilterBySelection", "FilterByMarqueeAndRules"))
  - `elemTypeFilter` (array of object): Whether each element type is shown. On Set only the listed element types are changed.
- `rebuild` (boolean): If true, Archicad drops the partial conversion data, so the next rebuild of the 3D window is a full one. Default: false.


Grasshopper: `Set3DFilterAndCutSettingsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/Set3DFilterAndCutSettings.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/Set3DFilterAndCutSettings.py): Hides the walls in the 3D window with Set3DFilterAndCutSettings, then restores the original filter. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### GetGridSettings

Gets the grid and snap grid settings of the database of the current window, and which database that is. Each database has its own grid settings. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetGridSettings

Parameters: none.


Grasshopper: `GetGridSettingsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/GetGridSettings.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/GetGridSettings.py): Prints the grid and snap grid settings of the current window's database with GetGridSettings. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### SetGridSettings

Changes the grid and snap grid settings of the database of the current window; only the given fields change. Returns the settings read back after the change. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetGridSettings

Parameters:

- `settings` (object, required): The grid settings to change, in the form GetGridSettings returns. Only the given keys are changed; a color may give only some of its components.
  - `spaceMainX` (number): The horizontal spacing of the main grid, in meters.
  - `spaceMainY` (number): The vertical spacing of the main grid, in meters.
  - `nLineMainX` (integer): The number of main horizontal grid lines.
  - `nLineMainY` (integer): The number of main vertical grid lines.
  - `gridSwitch` (boolean): Whether the grid is visible.
  - `spaceAuxX` (number): The horizontal spacing of the auxiliary grid, in meters.
  - `spaceAuxY` (number): The vertical spacing of the auxiliary grid, in meters.
  - `nLineAuxX` (integer): The number of horizontal auxiliary grid lines.
  - `nLineAuxY` (integer): The number of vertical auxiliary grid lines.
  - `gridMode` (integer): 0: none, 1: grid, 2: snap.
  - `snapOffsX` (number): The horizontal offset of the snap grid, in meters.
  - `snapOffsY` (number): The vertical offset of the snap grid, in meters.
  - `snapStepX` (number): The horizontal spacing of the snap grid, in meters.
  - `snapStepY` (number): The vertical spacing of the snap grid, in meters.
  - `status` (integer): The status of the grid, as Archicad stores it.
  - `gridAngle` (number): The rotation angle of the grid.
  - `gridOffsX` (number): The X offset of the grid.
  - `gridOffsY` (number): The Y offset of the grid.
  - `gridOffsZ` (number): The Z offset of the grid.
  - `backColor` (object): A color with transparency, each component from 0 to 1.
  - `gridColor` (object): A color with transparency, each component from 0 to 1.


Grasshopper: `SetGridSettingsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/SetGridSettings.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/SetGridSettings.py): Shows the grid with a 1 m main spacing in the current window with SetGridSettings, then restores the original grid. Each database has its own grid settings. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### ZoomToElements

Zooms the current window, 2D or 3D, to the given elements: selects them, zooms to the selection and restores the previous selection unless keepSelection is false. Fails when none of the elements could be selected, e.g. all of them are on another story or on a hidden layer.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ZoomToElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `keepSelection` (boolean): Restore the selection the window had before the command (default). With false the given elements stay selected.

Needs at least one Wall on the current story.

### CreateSections

Creates Section elements on the floor plan. A section looks to the left of its start to end direction, with its depth line that far on that side. GetDetailsOfElements reads the geometry of existing sections back.

  - `endCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
  - `depth` (number): The distance of the depth line from the section line, on the left of the start to end direction, which is the direction the section looks in. Default is 1.

The section looks to the left of its start to end direction, here to the north.

Every pair of consecutive points becomes one segment with its own viewpoint; repeating the first point at the end closes the chain.

### MoveNavigatorItem

Moves a navigator item to a new parent in the navigator tree, or to a new position within its current parent. Fails when Archicad does not put the item where it was asked to.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#MoveNavigatorItem

Parameters:

- `navigatorItemIdToMove` (NavigatorItemId, required)
- `parentNavigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required): The new parent of the item. It can be the item's current parent, to change the order of the items in it.
- `previousNavigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId): Optional child of parentNavigatorItemId that the item is placed right after. Without it an item moved within its own parent goes to the end of it.


Grasshopper: `CreateViewMapFolderComponent`, `MoveNavigatorItem`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/MoveNavigatorItem.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/MoveNavigatorItem.py): Creates two View Map folders and moves the second into the first with MoveNavigatorItem. Deletes both folders at the end.

### RenameNavigatorItem

Renames a navigator item or changes its ID. newId sets the custom layout number of a layout and the custom ID of any other item. For a Project Map section, elevation, detail or worksheet the name and ID of the element behind the viewpoint are changed, for an interior elevation those of the segment the item stands for; the change is undone when the item does not show the new name. The name and ID of other Project Map items (stories, schedules, ...) cannot be changed. Fails when Archicad refuses the change or does not apply the new name or ID. With customName false the item drops its custom name and follows its Project Map source again.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RenameNavigatorItem

Parameters:

- `navigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required)
- `newName` (string)
- `newId` (string): The new ID of the item. On a layout it is the custom layout number (customLayoutNumbering is switched on); on a Project Map section, elevation, interior elevation, detail or worksheet it is the reference ID of the element behind the item; on any other item it is the custom ID of the navigator item (customUiId becomes true).
- `customName` (boolean): Set to false to drop the custom name of the item, so that it follows the name of its Project Map source again. Cannot be combined with newName.


Grasshopper: `RenameNavigatorItem`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/RenameNavigatorItem.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/RenameNavigatorItem.py): Creates a View Map folder and renames it with RenameNavigatorItem. Deletes the folder at the end.

### DeleteNavigatorItems

Deletes navigator items from the navigator tree: views and folders of the View Map, layouts and master layouts of the Layout Book, and independent worksheets and details of the Project Map. Layout subsets and marker-linked worksheets and details cannot be deleted. An item that Archicad refuses to delete (in a Teamwork project: it is not reserved or the user has no right to delete it) is reported as a failed execution result.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteNavigatorItems

Parameters:

Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### CreateAddOnViewpoints

Creates add-on viewpoint roots, groups and leaf nodes in the Project Map, with their ID, name, view settings flags (leaf nodes only) and attached data (base64 encoded). A group or a leaf node is created in the given parent root or group. Returns the identifier of each new item, or an error for an item that could not be created. Roots and groups can't be created in a Teamwork project. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateAddOnViewpoints

Parameters:

- `viewpoints` (array of object, required): The add-on viewpoint items to create. The identifier of a new root or group is only known from the response, so create the parents in an earlier call.
  - `itemType` (string ("Root", "Group", "Leaf"), required): Whether to create a root, a group or a leaf node. Roots and groups can't be created in a Teamwork project.
  - `parentViewpointId` (object): The root or group to create the item in. Required for a group or a leaf node, ignored for a root.
  - `displayId` (string): The ID shown for the item in the Project Map.
  - `displayName` (string): The name shown for the item in the Project Map.
  - `viewSettingsFlags` (integer): The view settings flags of a leaf node, as Archicad stores them (a bit field). Ignored for a root or a group.
  - `data` (string): Data to attach to the item, base64 encoded.

Returns:

- `viewpoints` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The identifier of each created item, in the order of the input, or an error for an item that could not be created.

Grasshopper: `CreateAddOnViewpointsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateAddOnViewpoints.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateAddOnViewpoints.py): Creates an add-on viewpoint root with a leaf node in it, using CreateAddOnViewpoints. The new items stay in the Project Map. Roots can't be created in a Teamwork project. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

Needs an add-on viewpoint. Roots can't be changed in a Teamwork project. Requires Archicad 27 or later.


## Graphic Override Commands

### CreateGraphicalOverrideRule

Creates or overwrites a graphic override rule in a rule group: name, criterion XML, surface color and line pen. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

Group: Graphic Override Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateGraphicalOverrideRule

Parameters:

- `name` (string, required): Name of the override rule. Rule names are unique in the project: an existing rule with this name is overwritten, in whichever rule group it is.
- `ruleGroupName` (string): Rule group of a new rule, created when it does not exist. Default: 'Tapir'. An overwritten rule stays in its own group.
- `criterionXML` (string): Optional criterion XML. Archicad only takes XML in its own format: read it from a rule made in the GUI with GetGraphicalOverrideRules and change the values. XML written from scratch is dropped without an error, and so is an empty one: the rule then applies to all elements.
- `surfaceRGB` (object): Optional color override of the cut and uncut surfaces. Components are in the 0..1 range.
  - `red` (number, required)
  - `green` (number, required)
  - `blue` (number, required)
- `linePenIndex` (integer): Optional pen index override for lines, markers and texts. Only a positive index takes effect.
- `overrideContours` (boolean): Optional. If true, the contours of the overridden surfaces are recolored too.

Returns:

- `ruleId` (GuidId, required): The created or overwritten override rule.

Grasshopper: `CreateGraphicalOverrideRuleComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/GraphicOverride/CreateGraphicalOverrideRule.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/GraphicOverride/CreateGraphicalOverrideRule.py): Creates a graphic override rule that colors surfaces red with CreateGraphicalOverrideRule. The rule is created in the rule group 'Tapir Examples', which is deleted with it at the end. Without criterionXML the rule applies to every element. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### GetGraphicalOverrideRules

Returns every graphic override rule with its criterion XML. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

Group: Graphic Override Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetGraphicalOverrideRules

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `rules` (array of object, required)
  - `ruleId` (GuidId, required)
  - `name` (string, required)
  - `ruleGroupName` (string, required): Name of the rule group the rule belongs to.
  - `criterionXML` (string, required): The criterion in Archicad's own XML format. Change its values and pass it to CreateGraphicalOverrideRule to make similar rules.

Grasshopper: `GetGraphicalOverrideRulesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/GraphicOverride/GetGraphicalOverrideRules.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/GraphicOverride/GetGraphicalOverrideRules.py): Lists every graphic override rule of the project with its rule group and criterion XML with GetGraphicalOverrideRules. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination

Creates a graphic override combination from rule names, or replaces the rules of an existing one. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

Group: Graphic Override Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination

Parameters:

- `name` (string, required): Name of the override combination. When a combination with this name exists, its rule list is replaced.
- `ruleNames` (array of string, required): Names of the override rules in the combination, in order. Rule names are unique in the project, whatever the rule group. An empty list makes a combination without rules.

Returns:

- `combinationId` (GuidId, required): The created or changed override combination.

Grasshopper: `CreateGraphicalOverrideCombinationComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/GraphicOverride/CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/GraphicOverride/CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination.py): Creates a graphic override combination from a rule with CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination. The rule and the combination are created by the script and deleted at the end. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### GetGraphicalOverrideStyleOfElements

Returns the graphic override style each element is drawn with in the current window: for every overridable member (line type, pens, fill types, surfaces, ...) whether the active graphic override combination replaces it, and with what. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

Group: Graphic Override Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetGraphicalOverrideStyleOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

## Revision Management Commands

### GetRevisionIssues

Retrieves all issues.

Group: Revision Management Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.9. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetRevisionIssues

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `revisionIssues` (array of RevisionIssue, required)
- `customScheme` (array of object): The custom scheme fields of the revision issues (key and name). Present only when the project defines any.
  - `customSchemeKey` (Guid, required)
  - `customSchemeName` (string, required)

Grasshopper: `GetRevisionIssuesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/RevisionManagement/GetRevisionIssues.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/RevisionManagement/GetRevisionIssues.py): Lists the revision issues of the project with GetRevisionIssues.

### ModifyRevisionIssues

Modifies the ID, the short description and the custom scheme data of the given revision issues. Only the given fields are changed. Issued revision issues may refuse the change.

Group: Revision Management Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyRevisionIssues

Parameters:

- `revisionIssues` (array of object, required): The revision issues to modify. Only the given fields are changed.
  - `revisionIssueId` (RevisionIssueId, required)
  - `id` (string): The new ID of the revision issue.
  - `description` (string): The new short description of the revision issue.
  - `customSchemeData` (array of object): The custom scheme fields to set. A field is addressed by its key (as GetRevisionIssues returns it) or by its name; the fields not listed keep their values.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ModifyRevisionIssuesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/RevisionManagement/ModifyRevisionIssues.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/RevisionManagement/ModifyRevisionIssues.py): Changes the description of the first revision issue that is not issued yet with ModifyRevisionIssues, then restores it. Needs a revision issue that is not issued.

### GetRevisionChanges

Retrieves all changes.

Group: Revision Management Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.9. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetRevisionChanges

### GetRevisionChangeCustomScheme

Retrieves the custom fields of changes (the change custom scheme): the key and the name of each field. The keys are the customSchemeKey values in the customSchemeData of changes.

Group: Revision Management Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetRevisionChangeCustomScheme

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `customScheme` (array of object, required)
  - `customSchemeKey` (string, required): The identifier of the custom field. The same key is used in the customSchemeData of the revision changes.

Grasshopper: `GetRevisionChangeCustomSchemeComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/RevisionManagement/GetRevisionChangeCustomScheme.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/RevisionManagement/GetRevisionChangeCustomScheme.py): Lists the custom fields of revision changes with GetRevisionChangeCustomScheme.

### GetDocumentRevisions

## Project Data Commands

### GetProjectDataKeys

Lists the project data stored by Tapir in the project: the names, the identifiers of the add-on objects that store them, whether they are kept on this client only and the Teamwork user who has reserved them. Project data is text (for example JSON) saved in the project file by scripts and Grasshopper definitions, such as their settings or the mapping of elements to an external system.

Group: Project Data Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetProjectDataKeys

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `keys` (array of object, required): The project data stored by Tapir in the project.
  - `name` (string, required): The name of the project data.
  - `guid` (string, required): The identifier of the add-on object that stores the project data.
  - `clientOnly` (boolean, required): True when the project data is kept on this client only and is not shared in Teamwork.
  - `teamworkOwner` (User): The Teamwork user who has reserved the project data. Omitted when nobody has reserved it or the project is not a Teamwork project.

Grasshopper: `GetProjectDataKeysComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectData/GetProjectDataKeys.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectData/GetProjectDataKeys.py): Prints the names of the project data stored by Tapir, with their Teamwork owners, with GetProjectDataKeys.

### GetProjectData

Gets the content of the project data with the given names.

Group: Project Data Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetProjectData

Parameters:

- `names` (array of string, required): The names of the project data to get.

Returns:

- `values` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The project data in the order of the given names, or an error for a name that has no project data.

Grasshopper: `GetProjectDataComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectData/GetProjectData.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectData/GetProjectData.py): Prints the content of every project data stored by Tapir with GetProjectData.

### SetProjectData

Creates or overwrites project data: text (for example JSON) saved in the project under a name. New project data can be kept on this client only, or created as unique so that in Teamwork only one can exist with its name. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so scripts do not overwrite each other's data.

Group: Project Data Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetProjectData

Parameters:

- `values` (array of object, required): The project data to create or to overwrite. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so different scripts do not overwrite each other's data.
  - `name` (string, required): The name of the project data.
  - `content` (string, required): The content of the project data, for example a JSON string.
  - `clientOnly` (boolean): Creates the project data on this client only, it is not shared in Teamwork. Used only when the project data is created. The default is false.
  - `unique` (boolean): Creates the project data as a unique add-on object: in Teamwork only one can exist with its name, even when several users create it at the same time. Used only when the project data is created, and cannot be combined with clientOnly. The default is false.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `SetProjectDataComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectData/SetProjectData.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectData/SetProjectData.py): Saves a JSON text in the project under a name with SetProjectData, reads it back, then deletes it.

### DeleteProjectData

Deletes the project data with the given names.

Group: Project Data Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteProjectData

Parameters:

- `names` (array of string, required): The names of the project data to delete.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `DeleteProjectDataComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectData/DeleteProjectData.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectData/DeleteProjectData.py): Saves a project data and deletes it again with DeleteProjectData.

### ReserveProjectData

Reserves the project data with the given names in Teamwork, so that other users cannot change it. Returns the users who have already reserved some of it.

Group: Project Data Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ReserveProjectData

Parameters:

- `names` (array of string, required): The names of the project data to reserve.

Returns:

- `executionResult` (ExecutionResult, required)
- `conflicts` (array of object): The project data that could not be reserved because another user has reserved it.
  - `name` (string, required): The name of the project data.
  - `user` (User, required)

Grasshopper: `ReserveProjectDataComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectData/ReserveProjectData.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectData/ReserveProjectData.py): Saves a project data, reserves it in Teamwork with ReserveProjectData, then releases and deletes it. Needs a Teamwork project; in a solo project the reservation fails.

### ReleaseProjectData

Releases the project data with the given names in Teamwork.

Group: Project Data Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ReleaseProjectData

Parameters:

- `names` (array of string, required): The names of the project data to release.


Grasshopper: `ReleaseProjectDataComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectData/ReleaseProjectData.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectData/ReleaseProjectData.py): Saves and reserves a project data, then releases it in Teamwork with ReleaseProjectData and deletes it. Needs a Teamwork project; in a solo project the reservation and the release fail.

### RequestProjectData

Requests the project data with the given names in Teamwork from the users who have reserved it, with an optional message.

Group: Project Data Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RequestProjectData

Parameters:

- `names` (array of string, required): The names of the project data to request from the users who have reserved them.
- `mailText` (string): The message sent with the request. The default is empty.


Grasshopper: `RequestProjectDataComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectData/RequestProjectData.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectData/RequestProjectData.py): Requests the project data reserved by other Teamwork users from them, with a message, with RequestProjectData. Needs a Teamwork project. Sends the request to the users who reserved the data.

### GrantProjectData

Grants the project data with the given names, reserved by the current user, to another Teamwork user.

Group: Project Data Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GrantProjectData

Parameters:

- `names` (array of string, required): The names of the project data, reserved by the current user, to grant.
- `toUserId` (integer, required): The Teamwork user id of the user who gets the project data, for example the userId of a user returned by GetProjectDataKeys or ReserveProjectData.


Grasshopper: `GrantProjectDataComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectData/GrantProjectData.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/ProjectData/GrantProjectData.py): Saves and reserves a project data, then grants it to another Teamwork user with GrantProjectData. Needs a Teamwork project. Set toUserId to the user to grant to, e.g. the userId of a teamworkOwner that GetProjectDataKeys lists.


## MEP Commands

### GetMEPElements

Retrieves the MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) elements of the project, optionally filtered by type and domain. MEP elements are ordinary elements, so the generic element commands work on them as well (for example they can be deleted with the DeleteElements command). Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPElements

Parameters:

- `elementTypes` (array of MEPElementType): Optional filter for the MEP element types.
- `domains` (array of MEPDomain): Optional filter for the MEP domains.

Returns:

- `elements` (array of MEPElement, required): The MEP elements.

Grasshopper: `GetMEPElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPElements.py): Lists the duct and pipe routes and terminals of the project with GetMEPElements. Leave out both filters to list every MEP element. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### GetMEPRoutingElements

Retrieves the details of the given MEP routing elements: domain, MEP system, offset from the home story, branch preference table, the ports logically connected at the route's beginning and end, the floor plan display settings (cut plane position, floor plan display option, show projection and on-story visibility, from Archicad 29), route polyline, segments with cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), begin and end nodes, anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size, connection style and rigid segments, and nodes with their incoming and outgoing segments, preferred transition placement, elbows and transitions. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPRoutingElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `routingElements` (MEPRoutingElementDetailsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `GetMEPRoutingElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPRoutingElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPRoutingElements.py): Prints the polyline, segments and nodes of the first MEP routes of the project with GetMEPRoutingElements. Needs at least one MEP route (duct, pipe or cable carrier). Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### GetMEPPorts

Retrieves the ports of the given MEP elements including position, shape, size, connection status and connection style (from Archicad 30), the flow direction of piping and ventilation ports, the nominal size of piping ports (from Archicad 30), and the outer diameter, wall thickness and flange size (Archicad 30) of piping and ventilation ports. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPPorts

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `elementPorts` (MEPElementPortsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `GetMEPPortsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPorts.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPorts.py): Prints the ports of the first MEP elements of the project with GetMEPPorts. Needs at least one MEP element. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### GetMEPDistributionSystems

Retrieves the MEP distribution systems of the project with their domain, MEP system attribute and member elements. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPDistributionSystems

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `distributionSystems` (array of MEPDistributionSystem, required): The distribution systems of the project.
- `ports` (array of Guid): The ports in the distribution systems graph (see GetMEPPorts).

Grasshopper: `GetMEPDistributionSystemsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPDistributionSystems.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPDistributionSystems.py): Prints the MEP distribution systems of the project and their element trees with GetMEPDistributionSystems. The physical systems of a distribution system are returned from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### CreateMEPRoutingElements

Creates MEP routing elements (duct, pipe or cable carrier routes) along the given polylines with optional cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), MEP system and layer (also set on the segments, elbows and transitions), and optional elbow and transition defaults (preference tables and elbow radius factor, from Archicad 29) that apply only to what is placed. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateMEPRoutingElements

Parameters:

- `routingElementsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create MEP routing elements.
  - `domain` (MEPDomain, required)
  - `nodeCoordinates` (array of Coordinate3D, required): The corner points of the route polyline.
  - `crossSectionWidth` (number): Optional cross section width applied to all segments.
  - `crossSectionHeight` (number): Optional cross section height applied to all segments.
  - `crossSectionShape` (MEPCrossSectionShape): Optional; applied to all segments.
  - `crossSectionReferenceId` (integer): Optional cross section reference id of the segment preference table (used for circular cross sections). Resolved against preferenceTableId if given, otherwise against the table of the current routing tool default.
  - `preferenceTableId` (Guid): Optional guid of the segment preference table (see GetMEPPreferenceTables) applied to all segments. Not applicable to the CableCarrier domain.
  - `mepSystemId` (AttributeId): Optional MEP system attribute.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index of the routing element and all its parts (routing segments, rigid segments, elbows and transitions). Only a positive index takes effect; otherwise the routing tool default layer is used. A layer that does not exist or is locked gives an error for the item, and nothing is placed.
  - `defaults` (object): Optional changes to the routing tool default of the domain before the route is placed. Only what is placed changes, not the routing tool's settings. A value that cannot be set gives an error for the item, and nothing is placed.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateMEPRoutingElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/CreateMEPRoutingElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/CreateMEPRoutingElements.py): Creates a rectangular duct route with one corner and a circular pipe route with CreateMEPRoutingElements. Coordinates are in meters. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### CreateMEPElements

Creates MEP elements (Terminal, Accessory, Equipment or Fitting) at the given positions, optionally with a changed insulation that applies only to what is placed. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateMEPElements

Parameters:

- `elementsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create MEP elements.
  - `type` (MEPComponentType, required)
  - `domain` (MEPDomain): Required for all types except Equipment.
  - `position` (Coordinate3D, required)
  - `orientationDirection` (Coordinate3D): Optional direction vector of the orientation. Defaults to (1, 0, 0).
  - `orientationRotation` (Coordinate3D): Optional rotation vector of the orientation. Defaults to (0, 1, 0).
  - `defaults` (object): Optional changes to the tool default before the element is placed. Only what is placed changes, not the tool's settings. A value that cannot be set gives an error for the item, and nothing is placed.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateMEPElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/CreateMEPElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/CreateMEPElements.py): Places a duct terminal and a pipe accessory with the current tool settings using CreateMEPElements. Coordinates are in meters. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### ModifyMEPRoutingElements

Modifies the given MEP routing elements: MEP system, branch preference table, floor plan display settings (cut plane position, floor plan display option, show projection and on-story visibility, from Archicad 29), cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size and connection style of all segments, preferred transition placement of all nodes, and node positions. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyMEPRoutingElements

Parameters:

- `routingElementsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to modify MEP routing elements. Only provided fields are changed.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `mepSystemId` (AttributeId)
  - `crossSectionWidth` (number): New cross section width applied to all segments.
  - `crossSectionHeight` (number): New cross section height applied to all segments.
  - `crossSectionShape` (MEPCrossSectionShape): The new shape is applied to all segments.
  - `crossSectionReferenceId` (integer): New cross section reference id of the segment preference table applied to all segments (used for circular cross sections). Resolved against preferenceTableId if given, otherwise against the table the segments already use.
  - `preferenceTableId` (Guid): New segment preference table (guid as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables) applied to all segments. Not applicable to the CableCarrier domain.
  - `branchPreferenceTableId` (Guid): New branch preference table (guid as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables) of the routing element.
  - `anchor` (string ("TopLeft", "TopCenter", "TopRight", "MiddleLeft", "Center", "MiddleRight", "BottomLeft", "BottomCenter", "BottomRight")): New anchor point of the cross section, on a 3x3 grid, applied to all segments.
  - `referenceLineOffsetX` (number): New horizontal offset of the reference line from the anchor point, applied to all segments.
  - `referenceLineOffsetY` (number): New vertical offset of the reference line from the anchor point, applied to all segments.
  - `wallThickness` (number): New wall thickness applied to all segments.
  - `flangeSize` (number): New flange size applied to all segments.
  - `connectionStyle` (MEPConnectionStyle): New connection style applied to all segments.
  - `preferredTransitionPlacement` (MEPPreferredTransitionPlacement): New preferred transition placement applied to all nodes.
  - `cutPlanePosition` (MEPCutPlanePosition): New cut plane position of the routing element. Available from Archicad 29.
  - `floorPlanDisplayOption` (MEPFloorPlanDisplayOption): New floor plan display option of the routing element. Available from Archicad 29.
  - `showProjection` (MEPShowProjection): New show projection setting of the routing element. Available from Archicad 29.
  - `onStoryVisibility` (MEPOnStoryVisibility): New on-story visibility of the routing element. Available from Archicad 29.
  - `nodePositions` (array of Coordinate3D): New positions of the routing nodes. The size must match the number of nodes of the route.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ModifyMEPRoutingElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/ModifyMEPRoutingElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/ModifyMEPRoutingElements.py): Changes the cross section and insulation of a duct route with ModifyMEPRoutingElements. Creates a temporary duct route, modifies it, reads it back and deletes it. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### ModifyMEPPorts

Modifies the given MEP ports (as returned by GetMEPPorts): shape, connection style (from Archicad 30), the flow direction of piping and ventilation ports, and the outer diameter and nominal size (from Archicad 30) of piping ports. Only the given fields are changed. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyMEPPorts

Parameters:

- `portsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to modify MEP ports. Only provided fields are changed.
  - `portId` (Guid, required): The port to modify, as returned by GetMEPPorts.
  - `shape` (MEPCrossSectionShape): New shape of the port.
  - `connectionStyle` (MEPConnectionStyle): New connection style of the port. Available from Archicad 30.
  - `flowDirection` (MEPFlowDirection): New flow direction of a piping or ventilation port.
  - `outerDiameter` (number): New outer diameter of a piping port.
  - `nominalSize` (string): New nominal size of a piping port. Available from Archicad 30.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ModifyMEPPortsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/ModifyMEPPorts.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/ModifyMEPPorts.py): Changes the flow direction and outer diameter of a pipe port with ModifyMEPPorts. Creates a temporary pipe route, modifies the port at its start, reads it back and deletes the route. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

Connects MEP routing elements to other MEP elements or routes. Merges routes, splits routes or creates branch elements as needed. Archicad 27 does not report the merged, split or created elements. Available from Archicad 27.

Creates the two duct routes; the branch starts on the main route, as the command needs. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### CheckMEPPortConnectability

Checks whether MEP ports can be connected to other ports, for the given pairs of ports. Archicad 28 and later check the physical connection. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CheckMEPPortConnectability

Parameters:

- `portPairs` (array of object, required): The pairs of ports to check.
  - `portId` (Guid, required): The port to check, as returned by GetMEPPorts.
  - `otherPortId` (Guid, required): The port to connect it to, as returned by GetMEPPorts.

Returns:

- `results` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The result for each pair of ports, in the order of the input.

Grasshopper: `CheckMEPPortConnectabilityComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/CheckMEPPortConnectability.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/CheckMEPPortConnectability.py): Checks with CheckMEPPortConnectability whether the end port of one duct can be connected to the ports of another. Creates two temporary duct routes that meet at one point and deletes them at the end. The command itself works from Archicad 27; creating the routes requires Archicad 28 or later.

### GetMEPPreferenceTables

Gets the circular cross section preference tables (referenceId, diameter, wall thickness, description) and the reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, optionally with the elbow, branch and transition preference tables, plus the rectangular duct tables of the Ventilation domain or the segment tables of the CableCarrier domain. Each table has its name and whether it is editable; the segment tables also have their segmentation lengths from Archicad 29. The rows of the circular, elbow, branch and transition tables say whether they are valid, and the reference set and the angle set say which of their reference ids and angles are defined. The angle set and the transition tables are available from Archicad 29. Every row has its index in the table, as ModifyMEPPreferenceTables expects it. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPPreferenceTables

Parameters:

- `domain` (MEPPreferenceTableDomain, required)
- `includeFittingTables` (boolean): Also return the elbow, branch and transition preference tables. Defaults to false. Ignored for the CableCarrier domain.

Returns:

- `tables` (array of MEPPreferenceTable, required): The circular segment preference tables of the domain. Empty for the CableCarrier domain.
- `rectangularTables` (array of MEPValuePreferenceTable): The rectangular segment preference tables of the Ventilation domain.
- `cableCarrierTables` (array of MEPValuePreferenceTable): The segment preference tables of the CableCarrier domain.
- `referenceSet` (MEPReferenceSet): The reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain. Not returned for the CableCarrier domain.
- `angleSet` (MEPAngleSet): Available from Archicad 29.
- `elbowTables` (array of MEPElbowPreferenceTable): The elbow preference tables of the domain. Only when includeFittingTables is true.
- `branchTables` (array of MEPBranchPreferenceTable): The branch preference tables of the domain. Only when includeFittingTables is true.
- `transitionTables` (array of MEPTransitionPreferenceTable): The transition preference tables of the domain. Only when includeFittingTables is true, available from Archicad 29.

Grasshopper: `GetMEPPreferenceTablesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPreferenceTables.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPreferenceTables.py): Prints the pipe preference tables of the project, with the elbow, branch and transition tables, using GetMEPPreferenceTables. The angle set and the transition tables are returned from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### ModifyMEPPreferenceTables

Modifies the MEP preference tables of a domain, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them: adds tables, changes their names, segmentation lengths (from Archicad 29) and row values and descriptions, deletes or empties rows, adds rows to the rectangular duct and cable carrier tables, deletes tables, and deletes reference ids from the reference set and angles from the angle set (from Archicad 29). Each table is changed in one undoable step. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyMEPPreferenceTables

Parameters:

- `domain` (MEPPreferenceTableDomain, required)
- `tablesToAdd` (array of object): New tables to add to the domain, before the other changes.
  - `type` (MEPPreferenceTableType, required)
  - `name` (string, required)
- `tables` (array of MEPPreferenceTableChange): The tables of the domain to change, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them. Each table is changed in one undoable step.
- `tablesToDelete` (array of string): The guids of the tables of the domain to delete, after the other table changes.
- `referenceIdsToDelete` (array of integer): Reference ids to delete from the reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain.
- `anglesToDelete` (array of number): Angles to delete from the angle set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, as GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them. Available from Archicad 29.

Returns:

- `addedTables` (array of object or FailedExecutionResult, required): One item for each item of tablesToAdd: the guid of the new table, or the error.
- `tables` (ExecutionResults, required): One result for each item of tables.
- `deletedTables` (ExecutionResults, required): One result for each item of tablesToDelete.
- `referenceSet` (ExecutionResult): Only when referenceIdsToDelete is given.
- `angleSet` (ExecutionResult): Only when anglesToDelete is given.

Grasshopper: `ModifyMEPPreferenceTablesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/ModifyMEPPreferenceTables.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/ModifyMEPPreferenceTables.py): Adds a cable carrier segment table, renames it and fills it with rows using ModifyMEPPreferenceTables, then deletes it. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### GetMEPRoutingParameters

Gets the routing parameters of placed MEP elements: of a routing element its routing node parameters (preferred transition placement, elbow from Archicad 29, transition) and routing segment parameters (cross section, preference table, anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size, connection style); of a routing node its elbow (from Archicad 29) and transition parameters; of a routing segment its rigid segment parameters (Archicad 28 only). Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPRoutingParameters

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): MEP routing elements, routing nodes or routing segments.

Returns:

- `routingParameters` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The routing parameters of the given elements, in their order.

Grasshopper: `GetMEPRoutingParametersComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPRoutingParameters.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPRoutingParameters.py): Prints the routing parameters of the first MEP route of the project and of its nodes and segments with GetMEPRoutingParameters. Needs at least one MEP route. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### SetMEPRoutingParameters

Sets the routing parameters of placed MEP elements: the routing segment parameters (cross section and preference table) and, from Archicad 29, the routing node parameters (elbow radius factor and preference table, transition preference table) of routing elements, and the elbow and transition parameters of routing nodes (from Archicad 29). Only the given keys are changed, in one undo step with one execution result per element. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetMEPRoutingParameters

Parameters:

- `elements` (array of object, required): The routing parameters to change. Only the given keys are changed. An item gives either routingNodeParameters and/or routingSegmentParameters for a routing element, or elbowParameters and/or transitionParameters for a routing node.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `routingNodeParameters` (object): The routing node default parameters of a routing element (RoutingElement::Modifier::SetRoutingNodeDefaultParameters). Archicad 29 or newer.
  - `routingSegmentParameters` (object): The routing segment default parameters of a routing element (RoutingElement::Modifier::SetRoutingSegmentDefaultParameters).
  - `elbowParameters` (object): The elbow parameters of a routing node (RoutingNode::Modifier::SetElbowDefaultParameters). Archicad 29 or newer.
  - `transitionParameters` (object): The transition parameters of a routing node (RoutingNode::Modifier::SetTransitionDefaultParameters). Archicad 29 or newer.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `SetMEPRoutingParametersComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/SetMEPRoutingParameters.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/SetMEPRoutingParameters.py): Makes a pipe route circular and changes the elbow radius factor of its nodes with SetMEPRoutingParameters. Creates a temporary pipe route with one corner, changes it, reads the parameters back and deletes it. The elbow parameters can be set from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
