## MEP Commands (extended)

### GetMEPPreferenceTableRows

Gets rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle): whether the row is valid and its values (diameters, wall thickness, radius, length, angle, branch offset, connection length, description), and whether the table exists. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables only give whether they exist, as their rows have no key. On Archicad 27, which has one kind of preference table, a row is found by its shape and index and has a value and a description; the table's name and number of rows per shape are returned too. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: MEP Commands (extended). Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPPreferenceTableRows

Parameters:

- `tableId` (object, required): The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.
  - `guid` (Guid, required)
- `keys` (array of object, required): The keys of the rows to get.
  - `shape` (string ("Circular", "Rectangular")): Archicad 27 only: the shape whose list of values the row is in.
  - `index` (integer): Archicad 27 only: the index of the row in the list of its shape, from 0.
  - `referenceId` (integer)
  - `angle` (number)
  - `mainAxisReferenceId` (integer)
  - `branchAxisReferenceId` (integer)
  - `branchAxisAngle` (number)
  - `beginReferenceId` (integer)
  - `endReferenceId` (integer)

Returns:

- `exists` (boolean, required): Whether the table exists.
- `name` (string): Archicad 27 only: the name of the table.
- `sizes` (object): Archicad 27 only: the number of rows of each shape.
  - `Circular` (integer)
  - `Rectangular` (integer)
- `rows` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The rows in the order of the keys.

Grasshopper: `GetMEPPreferenceTableRowsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPreferenceTableRows.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPreferenceTableRows.py): Reads the first two rows of the first pipe segment preference table by their reference id with GetMEPPreferenceTableRows. Requires Archicad 28 or later (on Archicad 27 the keys are a shape and an index).

### SetMEPPreferenceTableRows

Sets the given values of rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table, found by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle). Only the given values are changed, in one undo step. On Archicad 27 a row is found by its shape and index, its value and description are set, and its index after the call is returned; the keys give the indices before the call. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: MEP Commands (extended). Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetMEPPreferenceTableRows

Parameters:

- `tableId` (object, required): The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.
  - `guid` (Guid, required)
- `rows` (array of object, required): The rows to change. Only the given values are set.
  - `key` (object, required): The key of a row. Segment tables: referenceId. Elbow tables: referenceId and angle. Branch tables: mainAxisReferenceId, branchAxisReferenceId and branchAxisAngle. Transition tables: beginReferenceId and endReferenceId. The angles are as GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them; Archicad 28 finds the rows by their reference ids only and rejects a key with an angle. Archicad 27: shape and index (AddMEPPreferenceTableRows: shape only).
  - `values` (object, required): The values of a row, lengths in meters. Segment tables: diameter, wallThickness and description. Elbow tables: diameter, radius and description. Branch tables: mainAxisDiameter, branchAxisDiameter, length, branchOffset, connectionLength and description. Pipe transition tables: beginDiameter, endDiameter, length and description. Duct transition tables: beginDiameter, endDiameter, angle and description. Archicad 27: value and description.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (array of object or FailedExecutionResult, required): One result per row, in the order of the rows.

Grasshopper: `SetMEPPreferenceTableRowsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/SetMEPPreferenceTableRows.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/SetMEPPreferenceTableRows.py): Changes the description of a row of an editable pipe segment preference table with SetMEPPreferenceTableRows. Reads the row, changes it, reads it back and restores the old description. Requires Archicad 28 or later (on Archicad 27 the key is a shape and an index).

### AddMEPPreferenceTableRows

Adds rows with the given keys and optionally values to a branch, elbow or transition preference table and returns their index, in one undo step. Branch tables from Archicad 28, elbow and transition tables from Archicad 29; segment tables have a row for each reference id. On Archicad 27 a row is added to the list of the given shape of any preference table, and the index of each new row after the call is returned. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: MEP Commands (extended). Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#AddMEPPreferenceTableRows

Parameters:

- `tableId` (object, required): The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.
  - `guid` (Guid, required)
- `rows` (array of object, required): The rows to add, with their key and optionally their values. Branch tables from Archicad 28, elbow and transition tables from Archicad 29. Segment tables have a row for each reference id, so no row can be added to them. Archicad 27: the key has the shape only, the table gives the index.
  - `key` (object, required): The key of a row. Segment tables: referenceId. Elbow tables: referenceId and angle. Branch tables: mainAxisReferenceId, branchAxisReferenceId and branchAxisAngle. Transition tables: beginReferenceId and endReferenceId. The angles are as GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them; Archicad 28 finds the rows by their reference ids only and rejects a key with an angle. Archicad 27: shape and index (AddMEPPreferenceTableRows: shape only).
  - `values` (object): The values of a row, lengths in meters. Segment tables: diameter, wallThickness and description. Elbow tables: diameter, radius and description. Branch tables: mainAxisDiameter, branchAxisDiameter, length, branchOffset, connectionLength and description. Pipe transition tables: beginDiameter, endDiameter, length and description. Duct transition tables: beginDiameter, endDiameter, angle and description. Archicad 27: value and description.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (array of object or FailedExecutionResult, required): One result per row, in the order of the rows.

Grasshopper: `AddMEPPreferenceTableRowsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/AddMEPPreferenceTableRows.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/AddMEPPreferenceTableRows.py): Adds a row to the first editable pipe elbow preference table with AddMEPPreferenceTableRows. The new row gets the reference id of the first row and an angle of the angle set that this reference id has no row for yet; it is deleted again at the end. Elbow rows can be added from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 29 or later.

### DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows

Deletes rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle), in one undo step. The rows of segment tables, and of the elbow tables of Archicad 28, are emptied instead. On Archicad 27 a row is found by its shape and index. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: MEP Commands (extended). Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows

Parameters:

- `tableId` (object, required): The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.
  - `guid` (Guid, required)
- `keys` (array of object, required): The keys of the rows to delete. Segment tables, and the elbow tables of Archicad 28, have a row for each reference id, which is emptied instead. Archicad 27: the indices are those before the call; the rows are deleted from the highest index down.
  - `shape` (string ("Circular", "Rectangular")): Archicad 27 only: the shape whose list of values the row is in.
  - `index` (integer): Archicad 27 only: the index of the row in the list of its shape, from 0.
  - `referenceId` (integer)
  - `angle` (number)
  - `mainAxisReferenceId` (integer)
  - `branchAxisReferenceId` (integer)
  - `branchAxisAngle` (number)
  - `beginReferenceId` (integer)
  - `endReferenceId` (integer)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRowsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows.py): Adds a row to the first editable pipe elbow preference table and deletes it again with DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows. The row gets the reference id of the first row and an angle of the angle set that this reference id has no row for yet. Rows of segment tables are emptied instead of deleted. Requires Archicad 29 or later.

### GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers

Lists the preference tables of the Piping, Ventilation and Cable Carrier preference table containers of Archicad 27: their id, name, whether they exist and their number of rows per shape, and whether the container exists. Only for Archicad 27; from Archicad 28 use GetMEPPreferenceTables.

Group: MEP Commands (extended). Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers

Parameters:

- `domains` (array of string ("Piping", "Ventilation", "CableCarrier")): The domains whose preference tables to list. Defaults to all three.

Returns:

- `containers` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The preference table container of each domain, in the order of the domains.

Grasshopper: `GetMEPPreferenceTableContainersComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.py): Lists the preference tables of the pipe and duct preference table containers with GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers. Only for Archicad 27; from Archicad 28 use GetMEPPreferenceTables.

### CreateMEPPreferenceTables

Adds empty preference tables with the given names to the preference table container of a domain of Archicad 27 and returns their id, in one undo step. Only for Archicad 27.

Group: MEP Commands (extended). Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateMEPPreferenceTables

Parameters:

- `domain` (string ("Piping", "Ventilation", "CableCarrier"), required): The MEP domain of a preference table container.
- `tables` (array of object, required): The tables to add, empty, to the preference table container of the domain.
  - `name` (string, required)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (array of object or FailedExecutionResult, required): One result per table, in the order of the tables.

Grasshopper: `CreateMEPPreferenceTablesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/CreateMEPPreferenceTables.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/CreateMEPPreferenceTables.py): Adds an empty pipe preference table named "Tapir example" with CreateMEPPreferenceTables. Every run adds a new table. Only for Archicad 27; from Archicad 28 use ModifyMEPPreferenceTables.

## Solid Element Operation Commands

### CreateSolidElementLinks

The wall and the slab are created by the script and deleted at the end.

The wall, the slab and the link between them are created by the script first; the elements are deleted at the end.

### GetSolidElementLinks

Returns solid element operation links for each queried element, grouped by role (target or operator).

Group: Solid Element Operation Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.4. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetSolidElementLinks

Needs at least one Wall.

### CreateSolidOperations

Runs a solid operation (subtraction, intersection, addition) on two morphs and returns the resulting morphs, one item per operation. Unlike CreateSolidElementLinks this is not a link: the target and the operator morph are replaced by the result. Morphs only; the operations run in one undo step.

Parameters:

- `operations` (array of object, required): The solid operations to run, each on two morphs. The target and the operator morph are replaced by the resulting morph.
  - `targetId` (ElementId, required): The target morph.
  - `operatorId` (ElementId, required): The operator morph.
  - `operation` (SolidOperationType, required)

Returns:

- `results` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): One item per operation, in the order of the input: the resulting morphs, or an error.

Grasshopper: `CreateSolidOperationsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/SolidElementOperation/CreateSolidOperations.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/SolidElementOperation/CreateSolidOperations.py): Subtracts a small box morph from a bigger one with CreateSolidOperations. Both morphs are created by the script and replaced by the resulting morph, which is deleted at the end.

## Script UI Commands

### ShowScriptUI

Shows the given HTML content in a native Archicad palette (a tkinter alternative for Python scripts).

Group: Script UI Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.4. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ShowScriptUI

Parameters:

- `htmlContent` (string, required): The full HTML document to display in the Script UI palette.
- `width` (integer): Optional palette client width in pixels. Leave unset to keep the current size.
- `height` (integer): Optional palette client height in pixels. Leave unset to keep the current size.
- `title` (string): Optional palette window title. Leave unset to keep the current title.
- `resizable` (boolean): Whether the user can drag-resize the palette. Defaults to true.
- `zoomEnabled` (boolean): Whether Ctrl+scroll/pinch zooming is allowed in the page. Defaults to true.
- `zoomLevel` (number): Optional initial zoom level (1.0 = 100%). Leave unset to keep the current zoom.
- `scrollBarsVisible` (boolean): Whether the browser's own scrollbars are shown. Defaults to true.
- `contextMenuEnabled` (boolean): Whether right-click shows the browser's context menu (e.g. Inspect Element). Defaults to true.
- `navigationDisabled` (boolean): Prevents the page from navigating away (e.g. clicking a link to another site) once it has loaded. Defaults to false.
- `allowSelfSignedCertificates` (boolean): Only relevant if htmlContent links to a remote https:// resource with a self-signed certificate. Defaults to false.
- `clearCookies` (boolean): Deletes all browser cookies before loading htmlContent. Defaults to false.
- `autoHeight` (boolean): Automatically resizes the palette's height to fit the page content as it changes. Defaults to false.


Grasshopper: `ShowScriptUIComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/ScriptUI/ShowScriptUI.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/ScriptUI/ShowScriptUI.py): Shows a small HTML page with a button in an Archicad palette with ShowScriptUI. The page sends its result with window.ACAPI.SubmitResult; read it with GetScriptUIResult.

### GetScriptUIResult

Retrieves and clears the result last submitted from the Script UI palette's page (via window.ACAPI.SubmitResult), if any, and reports whether the palette is still open, so a waiting script can stop when the user closes it.

Group: Script UI Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.4. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetScriptUIResult

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `hasResult` (boolean, required): True if the Script UI page has submitted a result since the last call.
- `result` (string): The submitted content (as passed to window.ACAPI.SubmitResult). Only present when hasResult is true.
- `isOpen` (boolean, required): True while the Script UI palette is open. False before the first ShowScriptUI call and once the user closed the palette with its close box, the page called window.ACAPI.ClosePalette or Archicad closed it; stays true while Archicad only temporarily hides all palettes (e.g. during a modal dialog). Lets a waiting script stop polling when the user closes the palette.

Grasshopper: `GetScriptUIResultComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/ScriptUI/GetScriptUIResult.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/ScriptUI/GetScriptUIResult.py): Shows a palette with two buttons and waits for the user's choice with GetScriptUIResult. Polls until a button is clicked or the palette is closed.

### GenerateDocumentation

Generates files for the documentation. Used by Tapir developers only.

Group: Developer Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GenerateDocumentation

Parameters:

- `destinationFolder` (string, required): Destination folder for the generated documentation files.

### MEPRoutingSegmentDetails

object: The details of an MEP routing segment.
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `routingElementId` (ElementId): The routing element the segment belongs to.
- `crossSectionWidth` (number, required)
- `crossSectionHeight` (number, required)
- `crossSectionShape` (string, required)
- `crossSectionReferenceId` (integer): The cross section reference id of the segment in its preference table (meaningful for circular cross sections).
- `preferenceTableId` (Guid): The guid of the segment preference table used by the segment (see GetMEPPreferenceTables).
- `beginNodeId` (ElementId): The routing node at the beginning of the segment.
- `endNodeId` (ElementId): The routing node at the end of the segment.
- `anchor` (string ("TopLeft", "TopCenter", "TopRight", "MiddleLeft", "Center", "MiddleRight", "BottomLeft", "BottomCenter", "BottomRight")): The anchor point of the cross section, on a 3x3 grid.
- `referenceLineOffsetX` (number): The horizontal offset of the reference line from the anchor point.
- `referenceLineOffsetY` (number): The vertical offset of the reference line from the anchor point.
- `wallThickness` (number): The wall thickness of the segment.
- `flangeSize` (number): The flange size of the segment. Only present when the segment has flanges.
- `connectionStyle` (MEPConnectionStyle)
- `rigidSegments` (Elements): The rigid segments (the straight duct, pipe or cable carrier pieces) of the routing segment.

### MEPRoutingNodeDetails

object: The details of an MEP routing node.
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `routingElementId` (ElementId): The routing element the node belongs to.
- `position` (Coordinate3D, required)
- `incomingSegmentId` (ElementId): The routing segment ending at this node. Not present at the beginning of the route.
- `outgoingSegmentId` (ElementId): The routing segment starting at this node. Not present at the end of the route.
- `preferredTransitionPlacement` (MEPPreferredTransitionPlacement)
- `elbows` (Elements): The elbows (bends in Archicad 28) at this node.
- `transitions` (Elements): The transitions at this node.

### MEPRoutingElementDetails

object: The details of an MEP routing element.
- `domain` (MEPDomainOrUnknown, required)
- `mepSystemId` (AttributeId, required)
- `offsetFromHomeStory` (number): The offset of the routing element from its home story.
- `branchPreferenceTableId` (Guid): The guid of the branch preference table used by the routing element (see GetMEPPreferenceTables). Not present when the routing element has none.
- `logicallyConnectedPortIdAtRouteBegin` (Guid): The port logically connected to the beginning of the route (see GetMEPPorts). Not present when nothing is connected there.
- `logicallyConnectedPortIdAtRouteEnd` (Guid): The port logically connected to the end of the route (see GetMEPPorts). Not present when nothing is connected there.
- `cutPlanePosition` (MEPCutPlanePosition)

object: One skin (hatch) of the profile's cross-section.
- `skinId` (string): Internal identifier of this skin, stable for the lifetime of the profile. Pass it back in CreateProfiles' skinOverrides to target this skin for modification.

- `outlineSubPolyEnds` (array of integer): Index (into outlineCoords) of the last vertex of each contour, for skins whose outline has holes or multiple contours.
- `outlineArcs` (array of object): Marks which consecutive outlineCoords pairs are connected by an arc instead of a straight edge.
  - `begIndex` (integer, required)

  - `arcAngle` (number, required)

### PossibleStringValues

array of string: The possible string values of a GDL parameter.

### PossibleNumericValues

array of object: The possible numeric values of a GDL parameter.

### GDLParameterDetails

object: Details of a GDL parameter.
- `name` (string, required): The name of the parameter.
- `displayName` (string, required): The display name of the parameter.
- `index` (integer, required): The index of the parameter.
- `type` (string, required): The type of the parameter.
- `dimension1` (integer): The 1st dimension of array (in case of array value).
- `dimension2` (integer): The 2nd dimension of array (in case of array value).
- `value` (any, required): The value of the parameter. For an array parameter it is a flat list of all items row by row: dimension1 rows of dimension2 items each. SetGDLParametersOfElements accepts the same flat list back.
- `valueDescription` (string): The value description for numeric parameter.
- `isLocked` (boolean, required): The parameter is locked; i.e. the user cannot modify it
- `flags` (array of string ("Hidden", "HiddenFromScript", "Disabled", "Child", "Unique", "Fixed", "BoldName", "Open"), required): The flags of the parameter.
- `possibleValues` (PossibleStringValues or PossibleNumericValues)
- `canHaveCustomValue` (boolean): The parameter can have a custom value.
- `itemDescriptions` (array of string): Per-item text labels for an array-type parameter (API_AddParType.arrayDescriptions), one per array element in dim1xdim2 order. Only present when the library part defines them.

### SetGDLParameterByNameDetails

object: Details of a GDL parameter.
- `name` (string, required): The name of the parameter.
- `index1` (integer): Optional 1-based first index for changing a single item of an array parameter. Only valid for array parameters and only together with a single (non-list) value.
- `index2` (integer): Optional 1-based second index for changing a single item of a two-dimensional array parameter. Only valid together with index1. Defaults to 1.
- `value` (any, required): The new value of the parameter, in the unit GetGDLParametersOfElements reports it in (Angle parameters in radians). For array parameters provide a list of values for one-dimensional arrays (e.g. [1, 2, 3]) or a list of lists for two-dimensional arrays (e.g. [[11, 12], [21, 22]]); the list must contain exactly as many values as the parameter has items, resizing an array parameter is not supported. A two-dimensional array can also be given as a flat list of all its dimension1 x dimension2 items row by row, the layout GetGDLParametersOfElements returns. Alternatively provide index1 (and optionally index2) together with a single value to change one item of the array. Within one command call whole-array (list) values are applied after all single-value changes.

### SetGDLParameterByIndexDetails

object: Details of a GDL parameter.
- `index` (integer, required): The index of the parameter.
- `index1` (integer): Optional 1-based first index for changing a single item of an array parameter. Only valid for array parameters and only together with a single (non-list) value.
- `index2` (integer): Optional 1-based second index for changing a single item of a two-dimensional array parameter. Only valid together with index1. Defaults to 1.
- `value` (any, required): The new value of the parameter, in the unit GetGDLParametersOfElements reports it in (Angle parameters in radians). For array parameters provide a list of values for one-dimensional arrays (e.g. [1, 2, 3]) or a list of lists for two-dimensional arrays (e.g. [[11, 12], [21, 22]]); the list must contain exactly as many values as the parameter has items, resizing an array parameter is not supported. A two-dimensional array can also be given as a flat list of all its dimension1 x dimension2 items row by row, the layout GetGDLParametersOfElements returns. Alternatively provide index1 (and optionally index2) together with a single value to change one item of the array. Within one command call whole-array (list) values are applied after all single-value changes.

### SetGDLParameterDetails

SetGDLParameterByNameDetails or SetGDLParameterByIndexDetails

### MorphPolygonHole

object
- `vertexIds` (array of integer, required)

### BeamHoleType

string ("Rectangular", "Circular")

### MorphPolygon

object
- `vertexIds` (array of integer, required): Counterclockwise outer-loop vertex indices for this face.
- `filled` (boolean): Defaults to true. Set to false to create only this loop's edges (a wireframe outline, e.g. a bare rectangle with no surface fill) without an actual face - holes/surfaceId are ignored in that case, since there is no fill for them to apply to.
- `holes` (array of MorphPolygonHole): Optional hole loops cut out of this face, each a clockwise list of vertex indices.
- `surfaceId` (AttributeId): Optional per-face surface (render material) override. Uses the Morph's default surface when omitted. Ignored during creation in Archicad 25.

### MeshSubline

object
- `coordinates` (array of Coordinate3D, required): The 3D coordinates of the leveling subline of the mesh.

### CurtainWallPattern

object: The column (primary) or row (secondary) pattern of a curtain wall segment: the sizes of the columns/rows of one pattern unit and how the unit is repeated along the segment.
- `sizes` (array of number, required): The sizes (widths of the columns or heights of the rows) of the pattern unit in meters, in order from the start of the segment or from the bottom. The unit is repeated to fill the segment.
- `logic` (CurtainWallPatternLogic)
- `origin` (CurtainWallPatternOrigin)
- `flexibleIndices` (array of integer): Zero-based indices of the columns/rows of the pattern unit that 'BestDivision' may stretch. When omitted, all of them are flexible. Ignored by 'FixedSizes'.

### CurtainWallPatternCell

object: The panel and frame classes of one cell of the pattern unit of a curtain wall segment. Panel classes are numbered as Archicad numbers them: 0 is no panel (the cell is left empty), 1 is the first panel class of the curtain wall (as listed in the Curtain Wall Settings, from the favorite or the tool defaults), 2 the second and so on. Frame classes: 0 is no frame (the cell is merged with its neighbour), 1 the Division frame, 2 the Corner frame, 3 the Boundary frame, 4 the first custom frame class of the curtain wall, 5 the second and so on. Fields not given keep the default assignment of the cell.
- `columnIndex` (integer, required): Zero-based column of the cell within the pattern unit, counted from the start of the segment.
- `rowIndex` (integer, required): Zero-based row of the cell within the pattern unit, counted from the bottom.
- `panelClassIndex` (integer): The panel class of the cell. 0 leaves the cell without a panel (Archicad keeps a hidden 'deleted panel' subelement there). With a crossing frame it is the class of the left (or lower) half; see rightPanelClassIndex for the other half.
- `rightPanelClassIndex` (integer): The panel class of the right (or upper) half of a cell with a crossing frame. Defaults to panelClassIndex.
- `leftFrameClassIndex` (integer): The frame class of the frame on the left edge of the cell (the grid line at the start of the column).
- `bottomFrameClassIndex` (integer): The frame class of the frame on the bottom edge of the cell (the grid line at the bottom of the row).
- `crossingFrameType` (CurtainWallCrossingFrameType)
- `crossingFrameClassIndex` (integer): The frame class of the diagonal frame of the cell. Only used when crossingFrameType is not 'None'.

### BeamHole

object
- `holeId` (number, required)
- `type` (BeamHoleType, required)
- `showContour` (boolean)
- `centerX` (number, required)
- `centerZ` (number, required)
- `width` (number, required)
- `height` (number)

### BeamHoleModification

object
- `type` (BeamHoleType, required)
- `showContour` (boolean)
- `centerX` (number, required)
- `centerZ` (number, required)
- `width` (number, required)
- `height` (number): Only used for the Rectangular type.

### LinkToSettings

object: Mode of linking an element to its home story.
- `homeStoryDifference` (integer): Difference of the home story from the current story.
- `newCreationMode` (boolean): Controls home-story selection during element creation. If true, homeStoryDifference selects the home story relative to the current story and the element's absolute floor index is ignored. If false, the absolute floor index is used and Archicad fills homeStoryDifference. This is a creation instruction, not a persistent linking mode.

### CoverFillOrientation

object: Orientation/distortion of the floor plan cover fill.
- `type` (HatchOrientationType)
- `origo` (Coordinate2D): Origin of the fill relative to the project origin.
- `matrix00` (number): X component of the primary distortion (direction) vector - the cosine of the fill angle, if not distorted.
- `matrix10` (number): Y component of the primary distortion (direction) vector - the sine of the fill angle, if not distorted.
- `matrix01` (number): X component of the secondary distortion vector - the cosine of the normal vector's angle, if not distorted.
- `matrix11` (number): Y component of the secondary distortion vector - the sine of the normal vector's angle, if not distorted.
- `innerRadius` (number): Radius for circular fill distortion (type Centered only).

### ProfileEdgeOverride

object
- `edgeIndex` (integer, required)
- `pen` (integer)
- `isVisibleLine` (boolean)
- `lineTypeId` (AttributeIdArrayItem)
- `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeIdArrayItem)

### ProfileSkinContour

object
- `polygonCoordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The 2D coordinates of this contour.
- `polygonArcs` (array of PolyArc): Optional arcs along this contour's edges. begIndex/endIndex are 0-based positions within this contour's own polygonCoordinates.

### LineSymbolItemData

object
- `itemType` (string, required): Separator, CenterDot, CenterLine, Dot, RightAngle, Parallel, Line, Circle, or Arc.
- `centerOffset` (number): Vertical distance from the origin. Used for Separator, CenterDot, and CenterLine item types.
- `length` (number): Length of the item. Used for CenterLine, RightAngle, and Parallel item types.
- `begPos` (Coordinate2D): Beginning position. Used for Dot, RightAngle, Parallel, Line, Circle, and Arc item types.
- `endPos` (Coordinate2D): End position. Used for Line item type only.
- `radius` (number): Radius. Used for Circle and Arc item types.
- `beginAngle` (number): Beginning angle in radians, measured from the vertical axis. Used for Arc item type only.
- `endAngle` (number): End angle in radians, measured from the vertical axis. Used for Arc item type only.

### PenData

object
- `index` (integer, required): Index of the pen [1..255].
- `color` (ColorRGB)
- `width` (number): Thickness of the pen defined in paper millimeters.
- `description` (string): Textual description of the pen.

### ProfileSkinData

object: One new skin (hatch). Its shape is one or more closed polygon contours: the first is the outer boundary, any further ones are holes cut out of it - the same polygon+holes convention as e.g. CreateSlabs' polygonCoordinates/polygonArcs/holes, just expressed as a list of contours instead of a separate holes array.
- `contours` (array of ProfileSkinContour, required): Closed polygon contours forming this skin's cross-section, in the Profile's local coordinate system. Each contour is closed automatically - do not repeat its first vertex at the end.
- `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeIdArrayItem)
- `surfaceId` (AttributeIdArrayItem)
- `fillId` (AttributeIdArrayItem)
- `contourPen` (integer)
- `contourLineTypeId` (AttributeIdArrayItem)
- `isCore` (boolean)
- `isFinish` (boolean)
- `visibleCutEndLines` (boolean)
- `cutEndLinePen` (integer)
- `cutEndLineTypeId` (AttributeIdArrayItem)
- `edgeOverrides` (array of ProfileEdgeOverride): Per-edge pen/visibility/line type, targeted by 0-based edge index. Edge indices follow the same order as this skin's contours/polygonCoordinates: the outer contour's edges first (one edge per vertex, wrapping around), then each hole's, in the order the contours were given. Verify exact indices for a created skin via a follow-up GetProfiles call's skins[].edges before relying on them.

### PolyArc

object: Representation of an arc segment of a two dimensional polygon/polyline.
- `begIndex` (integer, required): Node index of one end point of the arc.
- `endIndex` (integer, required): Node index of the other end point of the arc.
- `arcAngle` (number, required): Angle of the arc; it is positive, if the arc is on the right-hand side of the straight segment.

### Coordinate2D

object: 2D coordinate.
- `x` (number, required): X value of the coordinate.
- `y` (number, required): Y value of the coordinate.

### Coordinate3D

object: 3D coordinate.
- `x` (number, required): X value of the coordinate.
- `y` (number, required): Y value of the coordinate.
- `z` (number, required): Z value of the coordinate.

### PerspectiveProjectionParameters

object: The parameters of a perspective projection of the 3D window.
- `cameraPosition` (Coordinate3D, required): The position of the camera.
- `targetPosition` (Coordinate3D, required): The position of the target point the camera looks at.
- `distance` (number, required): The distance between the camera and the target.
- `azimuth` (number, required): The azimuth angle of the camera.
- `viewCone` (number, required): The view cone angle of the camera.
- `rollAngle` (number, required): The roll angle of the camera.
- `isTwoPointPersp` (boolean, required): True for a two-point perspective (vertical edges stay vertical).

### Dimensions3D

object: Dimensions in 3D.
- `x` (number, required): X dimension.
- `y` (number, required): Y dimension.
- `z` (number, required): Z dimension.

### ColorRGB

object: RGB color.
- `red` (number, required): Red value between 0.0 and 1.0
- `green` (number, required): Green value between 0.0 and 1.0
- `blue` (number, required): Blue value between 0.0 and 1.0

### Texture

object: Texture parameters
- `name` (string, required): The filename of the texture in the library (without extension).
- `rotationAngle` (number): Rotation angle in radians.
- `xSize` (number): X size of the picture in model space, by default 1.
- `ySize` (number): Y size of the picture in model space, by default 1.
- `FillRectangle` (boolean): True, if fit the rectangle with the picture in a central position, using the natural aspect ratio of the picture.
- `FitPicture` (boolean): True, if fit the picture in the middle of the rectangle, using the natural aspect ratio of the picture.
- `mirrorX` (boolean): True, if the texture is mirrored in X direction.
- `mirrorY` (boolean): True, if the texture is mirrored in Y direction.
- `useAlphaChannel` (boolean): True, if the alpha channel of the texture is used.
- `alphaChannelChangesTransparency` (boolean): True, if the alpha channel of the texture changes the transparency.
- `alphaChannelChangesSurfaceColor` (boolean): True, if the alpha channel of the texture changes the surface color.
- `alphaChannelChangesAmbientColor` (boolean): True, if the alpha channel of the texture changes the ambient color.
- `alphaChannelChangesSpecularColor` (boolean): True, if the alpha channel of the texture changes the specular color.
- `alphaChannelChangesDiffuseColor` (boolean): True, if the alpha channel of the texture changes the diffuse color.

### Error

object: The details of an error.
- `code` (integer, required): The code of the error.
- `message` (string, required): The error message.

### ErrorItem

object
- `error` (Error, required)

### OverriddenValue

object: A value the active graphic override combination may replace. 'overridden' tells whether it does; only then the value is given: 'attributeId' for line types, fills and surfaces, 'penIndex' for pens, 'color' for background pens and surfaces set to a color.
- `overridden` (boolean, required)
- `attributeId` (AttributeId)
- `penIndex` (integer)
- `color` (object)
  - `red` (number, required)
  - `green` (number, required)
  - `blue` (number, required)

### SuccessfulExecutionResult

object: The result of a successful execution.
- `success` (boolean (true), required)

### FailedExecutionResult

object: The result of a failed execution.
- `success` (boolean (false), required)
- `error` (Error, required)

### ExecutionResult

SuccessfulExecutionResult or FailedExecutionResult: The result of the execution.

### ExecutionResults

array of ExecutionResult: A list of execution results.

string ("AllSharp", "AllSmooth", "UserDefined"): How ridges between mesh facets are displayed in 3D: 'AllSharp' shows all ridges, 'AllSmooth' hides them, 'UserDefined' shows only ridges along user-defined level lines (the drawing-set look for contour-line topography).

### CurtainWallPatternLogic

string ("FixedSizes", "BestDivision"): How the pattern unit fills the segment: 'FixedSizes' keeps the given sizes and repeats the unit, which may leave a partial unit at the end (Archicad: Fixed Size); 'BestDivision' stretches the flexible columns/rows so that whole units fill the segment with the least stretching (Archicad: Best Division).

### CurtainWallPatternOrigin

string ("StartWithPattern", "StartFromCenter", "AlignToCenter", "EndWithPattern"): Where the pattern unit is anchored on the segment: at its start, centered with a unit starting at the center, centered with a unit centered on the center, or at its end.

string ("None", "FromBottomLeftToTopRight", "FromTopLeftToBottomRight"): The diagonal frame of a pattern cell: none, or from the bottom left to the top right corner, or from the top left to the bottom right corner.

string ("TopLeft", "TopCenter", "TopRight", "MiddleLeft", "Center", "MiddleRight", "BottomLeft", "BottomCenter", "BottomRight"): Anchor point of the beam cross section on a 3x3 grid.

### ColumnCoreAnchor

string ("TopLeft", "TopCenter", "TopRight", "MiddleLeft", "Center", "MiddleRight", "BottomLeft", "BottomCenter", "BottomRight"): Anchor point of the column core on a 3x3 grid.

### SlabReferencePlaneLocation

string ("Top", "CoreTop", "CoreBottom", "Bottom"): Location of the slab reference plane.

### WallReferenceLineLocation

string ("Outside", "Center", "Inside", "CoreOutside", "CoreCenter", "CoreInside"): The Core* values only have an effect on a Composite or Profile wall (structureType) - a Basic wall has no core skin, and Archicad falls back to the nearest non-core equivalent (e.g. CoreCenter becomes Center).

### MEPPreferenceTableDomain

string ("Piping", "Ventilation", "CableCarrier"): The MEP domain of the segment preference tables.

### MEPPreferenceRowIndex

integer: The position of the row in its preference table, as ModifyMEPPreferenceTables expects it. Rows that cannot be read are left out of GetMEPPreferenceTables, so this is not always the position in the rows list.

### MEPPreferenceTableType

string ("Segment", "Elbow", "Branch", "Transition"): The kind of preference table container: the segment tables (circular and rectangular ducts share one container), or the elbow, branch or transition tables. CableCarrier has only segment tables, transition tables are available from Archicad 29.

### MEPPreferenceRowChange

object: Changes one row of a preference table, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns. Only the given values are changed. A value that does not belong to the kind of table is an error; the read-only values (reference ids, branchAxisAngle, isValid, and angle of an elbow table) are ignored.
- `index` (MEPPreferenceRowIndex, required)
- `delete` (boolean): Deletes the row. The circular segment tables, and the elbow tables in Archicad 28, have a fixed row for each reference id; there the row is emptied instead. Cannot be combined with new values.
- `diameter` (number): Circular segment and elbow tables.
- `wallThickness` (number): Circular segment tables.
- `value` (number): Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables. These tables keep their rows ordered by value, so a changed value can move the row; the indices of the other rows given in the same call are followed.
- `radius` (number): Elbow tables.
- `mainAxisDiameter` (number): Branch tables.
- `branchAxisDiameter` (number): Branch tables.
- `length` (number): Branch tables and piping transition tables.
- `branchOffset` (number): Branch tables.
- `connectionLength` (number): Branch tables.
- `beginDiameter` (number): Transition tables.
- `endDiameter` (number): Transition tables.
- `angle` (number): Ventilation transition tables, in the unit GetMEPPreferenceTables returns it. Read-only (ignored) in elbow tables.
- `description` (string)
- `referenceId` (integer): Read-only, ignored.
- `mainAxisReferenceId` (integer): Read-only, ignored.
- `branchAxisReferenceId` (integer): Read-only, ignored.
- `beginReferenceId` (integer): Read-only, ignored.
- `endReferenceId` (integer): Read-only, ignored.
- `branchAxisAngle` (number): Read-only, ignored.
- `isValid` (boolean): Read-only, ignored.

### MEPPreferenceTableChange

object: Changes one preference table, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns. Only the given values and rows are changed.
- `guid` (string, required): The guid of the table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables.
- `name` (string): The new name of the table.
- `isEditable` (boolean): Read-only, ignored.
- `useIndividualSegmentLengths` (boolean): Segment tables only. Available from Archicad 29.
- `minimumSegmentationLength` (number): Segment tables only; the maximum is kept when not given. Available from Archicad 29.
- `maximumSegmentationLength` (number): Segment tables only; the minimum is kept when not given. Available from Archicad 29.
- `rows` (array of MEPPreferenceRowChange): The rows to change or delete, each at most once. All indices refer to the table before this call.
- `newRows` (array of object): Rows to add to a rectangular duct or cable carrier segment table, after the other changes. Adding rows to the other tables is not supported yet.
  - `value` (number, required)
  - `description` (string)

### AssociativeWitnessPoint

object: A witness point of a dimension. Give elementId (with line, inIndex, special, nodeType, nodeStatus and nodeId as needed) for a point associated with an element, or only coordinate for a static point that is not associated with any element, like a point added by hand on empty space. A witness point takes either elementId or coordinate, not both.
- `elementId` (ElementId)
- `coordinate` (Coordinate2D): The position of a static (non-associative) witness point. Use it instead of elementId; the other fields are ignored for a static point.
- `line` (boolean)
- `inIndex` (integer)
- `special` (integer)
- `nodeType` (integer)
- `nodeStatus` (integer)
- `nodeId` (number)

### CoordinateWitnessPoint

object
- `coordinate` (Coordinate2D)
- `coordinate3D` (Coordinate3D)
- `dimensionPosition` (Coordinate2D)
- `dimensionValue` (number)
- `witnessForm` (string ("None", "Small", "Large", "Fix", "Unknown"))
- `witnessVal` (number)
- `baseElementId` (ElementId)
- `line` (boolean): True when the witness point lies on an edge of the base element rather than at a node (API_Base line).
- `inIndex` (integer): Subindex of the base element's node (API_Neig inIndex).
- `special` (integer): Non-zero for special references such as a wall plane, a beam, window or door hole, or a mesh ridge (API_Base special).
- `nodeType` (integer): Reserved by Archicad for section dimensions (API_Base node_typ).
- `nodeStatus` (integer): Reserved by Archicad for section dimensions (API_Base node_status).
- `nodeId` (number): Polygon vertex id of the base element, from its memo's vertexIDs, for elements with a polygon.

### InteriorElevationData

object
- `nodeCoordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The corner points of the connected segment chain. Each consecutive pair of points becomes one segment, so a room with four walls needs five points to be closed, or four to be left open.
- `depth` (number): How far each segment looks. Applied to every segment. Defaults to 1.0.
- `name` (string): Name of the interior elevation. Each segment is named after it.
- `id` (string): ID string of the interior elevation.
- `floorIndex` (integer): The story to place the interior elevation on. Defaults to the current story.

### HotlinkInstanceChange

object
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `origin` (HotlinkOrigin): If z is omitted, the instance's current z is kept.
- `rotationAngle` (number): Rotation about the origin, counter-clockwise, in radians.
- `mirrored` (boolean): Reflect the module's local X axis before the rotation.
- `floorDifference` (integer)
- `skipNested` (boolean)
- `suspendFixAngle` (boolean)
- `ignoreTopFloorLinks` (boolean)
- `relinkWallOpenings` (boolean)
- `adjustLevelDiffs` (boolean)
- `layerIndex` (integer): Move the instance to this layer.

### HotlinkInstanceCreation

object
- `hotlinkNodeId` (HotlinkNodeId, required): The node to place, from GetHotlinks or CreateHotlinkNodes. On Archicad 25 a node that has never been placed cannot be read, so a node created through the API can only be placed from Archicad 26 on.
- `origin` (HotlinkOrigin, required): If z is omitted, the instance is placed at 0.
- `rotationAngle` (number): Optional rotation about the origin, counter-clockwise, in radians. Defaults to 0.
- `mirrored` (boolean): Optional. Reflects the module's local X axis before the rotation. Defaults to false.
- `floorIndex` (integer): Optional story the instance is placed on. Defaults to the current story.
- `floorDifference` (integer): Optional story offset applied to the module's stories. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.
- `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer of the instance. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default layer.
- `skipNested` (boolean): Optional. Do not place hotlinks nested inside the module. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.
- `suspendFixAngle` (boolean): Optional. Rotate fixed-angle elements with the module. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.
- `ignoreTopFloorLinks` (boolean): Optional. Top-linked elements keep their height rather than their top story link. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.
- `relinkWallOpenings` (boolean): Optional. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.
- `adjustLevelDiffs` (boolean): Optional. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.

### ElementIFCClassificationReference

object: An IFC classification reference (IfcClassificationReference) of an element. The text fields are missing when the reference has no value for them.
- `identification` (string): The identification of the classification reference, for example a classification code.
- `name` (string): The name of the classification reference.
- `location` (string): The location of the classification reference, for example a URL.
- `description` (string): The description of the classification reference. Given from Archicad 29.
- `referencedSource` (object, required): The classification (IfcClassification) the reference belongs to.

  - `edition` (string): The edition of the classification. Missing when it has no value.
  - `editionDate` (string): The edition date of the classification. Given only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27, missing when it has no value.
  - `description` (string): The description of the classification. Given only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27, missing when it has no value.
  - `location` (string): The location of the classification, for example a URL. Given only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27, missing when it has no value.
- `source` (string ("preview", "local")): Where the reference comes from: preview (mapped by the preview IFC export translator) or local (stored on the element). Missing in Archicad 25, 26 and 27, where the storedOnly input chooses between the stored references and all of them.

### Body3D

object: One solid body of an element's 3D model: a flat vertex list in world coordinates and the planar faces referencing it. The faces are not triangulated: a face is a closed loop of vertex indices (counterclockwise seen from outside the body) plus the loops of its holes.
- `vertices` (array of Coordinate3D, required): The vertices of the body in world coordinates (meters, absolute Z).
- `polygons` (array of object, required): The faces of the body.
  - `vertexIds` (array of integer, required): The outer contour of the face: 0-based indices into vertices.
  - `holes` (array of object): The holes in the face, each a closed loop of 0-based indices into vertices.
  - `surfaceId` (AttributeId): The surface attribute of the face. Left out when the face's material is not a project attribute (for example one defined by a GDL script).

### WallDetails

object
- `geometryType` (WallGeometryType, required)
- `begCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
- `endCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
- `zCoordinate` (number, required)
- `flipped` (boolean)
- `height` (number, required): height relative to bottom
- `bottomOffset` (number, required): base level of the wall relative to the floor level
- `offset` (number, required): wall's base line's offset from ref. line
- `arcAngle` (number): The arc angle of the curved wall in radians.
- `begThickness` (number): Thickness at the beginning of wall, it will return 0 for poly wall type
- `endThickness` (number): Thickness at the end of wall, it will return 0 for poly wall type
- `polygonOutline` (array of Coordinate2D): Polygon outline in case of polygonal wall
- `polygonArcs` (array of PolyArc): Polygon arcs in case of polygonal wall
- `structureType` (WallStructureType)
- `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId)
- `compositeId` (AttributeId)
- `profileId` (AttributeId)
- `referenceLineLocation` (WallReferenceLineLocation)
- `profileType` (WallProfileType): Only Normal/Slanted/Trapez are settable via ModifyWalls - Poly needs a profile attribute wired through a separate mechanism. slantAlpha/slantBeta only have an effect once this is Slanted or Trapez.
- `slantAlpha` (number): Only has an effect once profileType is set to Slanted or Trapez.
- `slantBeta` (number): Only has an effect once profileType is set to Slanted or Trapez.
- `topOffset` (number): Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.
- `relativeTopStory` (number): Non-zero links the wall's top to another story instead of an explicit height - do not set together with 'height' via ModifyWalls in the same call.
- `zoneRel` (WallZoneRelation)
- `visibility` (StoryVisibility): On Archicad 29 a wall knows only 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories' (Wall Settings offers no Custom option), so a wall can read back a combination the dialog cannot show - a wall fresh from the Wall tool defaults may report showOnHome false with showRelAbove 1, which Wall Settings shows as an empty Show on Stories field (#852). See ModifyWalls for which combinations can be written.
- `isAutoOnStoryVisibility` (boolean): When true (the default on a new wall), Archicad recomputes 'visibility' automatically from the wall's vertical extent and ignores any value set for it.
- `referenceMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial)
- `oppositeMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial)
- `sideMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial)
- `cutFillPen` (OverriddenPen)
- `cutFillBackgroundPen` (OverriddenPen)
- `contourPen` (integer): Pen of the wall's own contour/reference outline (API_WallType::contPen) - distinct from cutFillPen, which is the cut fill pattern's pen inherited from the building material/composite/profile. Unlike cutFillPen this is not inheritable/overridable, it is the wall's own pen index directly, the same field used regardless of structureType (Basic, Composite or Profile).
- `contourPen3D` (integer): Pen of the wall's contour in 3D views (API_WallType::contPen3D).
- `contourLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the wall's own contour (API_WallType::contLtype) - pairs with contourPen, which only sets the pen, not the line type.
- `belowViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type used when "OutLines Only" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup (API_WallType::belowViewLineType). Corresponds to the "Uncut Lines" value in the Wall Settings dialog.
- `aboveViewLinePen` (integer): Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup. Corresponds to the "Overhead Line Pens" value in the Wall Settings dialog.
- `aboveViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.
- `displayOption` (DisplayOption)
- `viewDepthLimitation` (ViewDepthLimitation): Only has an effect on a multi-story wall (relativeTopStory/topOffset making it span more than one story).
- `connectionPriority` (integer): Priority of the wall in a junction with other elements (API_WallType::wallConnPriority - higher wins the cut/cover at the junction). Archicad ignores writes to this field; read-only in practice.
- `useCompositePriority` (boolean): When true, the Composite's own priority is used at junctions instead of connectionPriority.
- `junctionSequence` (integer): Tie-breaker (0-999) used when two walls meet with the same connectionPriority, or when 3+ walls meet in a junction (API_WallType::sequence). Archicad ignores writes to this field; read-only in practice.
- `linkToSettings` (LinkToSettings): newCreationMode is expected to read back as false after creation; Archicad resolves the relative story selection to an absolute floor index.
- `inheritEndSurface` (boolean): The end surface of the wall is inherited from the adjoining wall.
- `alignTexture` (boolean): Align texture mapping to the wall's edges.
- `offsetFromOutside` (number): Distance between the reference line and the outside face of the wall. Output only - not settable via ModifyWalls.
- `polyCanChange` (boolean): The polygonal wall's corners can be changed in case of L and T connections. Only meaningful for a Polygonal wall (geometryType).
- `materialsChained` (boolean): Whether the surface materials are chained.
- `logHeight` (number): Height of the log for log walls. 0 means a normal (non-log) wall.
- `hasWindow` (boolean): Whether the wall has at least one Window. Output only.
- `hasDoor` (boolean): Whether the wall has at least one Door. Output only.

object

### ObjectDetails

object: Shared shape for Object and Lamp elements (both use the same API_ObjectType struct). lightColor/lightIsOn only apply to Lamps. Per the Archicad SDK's own remarks, per-story visibility (visibility.showRelAbove/showRelBelow) and visibility.linkToSettings.newCreationMode were 'not extended' for Object/Lamp the way they were for other element types - still settable here for schema symmetry, but Archicad may silently ignore them.
- `libPart` (LibPartDetails, required)
- `ownerElementId` (ElementId)
- `ownerElementType` (ElementType)
- `origin` (Coordinate3D, required)
- `dimensions` (Coordinate3D, required)
- `angle` (number, required)
- `pen` (integer)
- `lineTypeId` (AttributeId)
- `surfaceId` (AttributeId): Material/Surface override (API_ObjectType.mat).
- `sectionFillId` (AttributeId)
- `sectionFillPen` (integer)
- `sectionFillBackgroundPen` (integer)
- `sectionContourPen` (integer)
- `useObjectPens` (boolean): Use the pen defined in the library part instead of 'pen'.
- `useObjectLineTypes` (boolean): Use the line type defined in the library part instead of 'lineTypeId'.
- `useObjectMaterials` (boolean): Use the materials defined in the library part instead of 'surfaceId'.
- `useObjectSectionAttributes` (boolean): Use the section attributes defined in the library part instead of 'sectionFillId'/'sectionFillPen'/'sectionFillBackgroundPen'/'sectionContourPen'.
- `reflected` (boolean)
- `useFixSize` (boolean): Use the A/B (dimensions.x/dimensions.y) values as fixed sizes.
- `fixPoint` (integer): 0-based index of the hotspot to keep fixed when the object is resized (raw API_ObjectType.fixPoint value, not 1-based).
- `offset` (Coordinate2D): Offset of the symbol's origin from the insertion point. Reported accurately here, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (always reports the library part's own default hotspot offset regardless of what is sent) - same class of read-only-in-practice field as Morph's bodyType/edgeType/level.
- `useFixedAngle` (boolean): Use a fixed rotation angle (API_ObjectType.fixedAngle - stored as Int32 in the API despite being boolean in practice). Reported accurately here, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify.
- `isAutoOnStoryVisibility` (boolean): Recalculate per-story visibility automatically from the object's vertical extent ('All Relevant Stories').
- `lightColor` (ColorRGB): Lamp only. Reported accurately here, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (always reports the library part's own default light color). lightIsOn (the on/off state) does not have this problem.
- `lightIsOn` (boolean): Lamp only.
- `visibility` (StoryVisibility)
- `linkToSettings` (LinkToSettings)

### MeshModificationData

object: The fields to modify on the Mesh. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is.
- `floorIndex` (integer)
- `level` (number): The Z reference level of coordinates.
- `skirtType` (MeshSkirtType)
- `skirtLevel` (number): The height of the skirt.
- `ridges` (MeshRidges)
- `showLines` (boolean): Whether to show secondary mesh lines on plan.
- `contourPen` (integer): Pen attribute index for the mesh contour line.
- `levelPen` (integer): Pen attribute index for the mesh level lines.
- `lineTypeIndex` (integer): Line type attribute index for the mesh contour.
- `polygonCoordinates` (array of Coordinate3D): The 3D coordinates of the outline polygon of the mesh. Replaces the existing boundary entirely; the existing outline arcs are removed unless polygonArcs is also given, and the existing holes are kept unless holes is also given.
- `polygonArcs` (array of PolyArc): Polygon outline arcs of the mesh. Replaces the existing outline arcs; when given without polygonCoordinates, they apply to the existing outline.
- `holes` (array of Hole3D): The 3D holes of the mesh. Replaces all existing holes; an empty array removes them. When given without polygonCoordinates, the existing outline is kept.
- `sublines` (array of MeshSubline): The leveling sublines inside the polygon of the mesh. Replaces existing sublines entirely.

### MorphBody

object: A Morph's full body geometry: an indexed vertex list plus one entry per face (polygon). Shared shape between GetDetailsOfElements' output and CreateMorphs/ModifyMorphs' input - what Get reports is what Create/Modify accept back. There is no fillet/chamfer operation in the Archicad API - a caller wanting rounded geometry must supply the already-tessellated facets here; edgeOverrides only controls how an existing straight edge is DISPLAYED (hidden/visible/smooth-shaded), not its shape.
- `bodyType` (string ("Solid", "Surface")): Whether the body is a closed solid or an open surface shell. Reported accurately on Get; on Create/Modify this is set on the element but a confirmed Archicad SDK bug means it may not take effect (bodyType has been observed always coming back Solid regardless of what was requested - see edgeOverrides' note).
- `isClosed` (boolean): READ-ONLY, Get output only (ignored if sent to Create/Modify). Geometrically computed (Modeler::MeshBody::IsClosedBody): true if every edge in the body has exactly two adjacent faces (a watertight/manifold volume), false if any edge borders only one face (an open shell / has holes or gaps). Distinct from bodyType, which is the caller's declared INTENT (Solid vs Surface) rather than the actual computed geometry - a body can be declared bodyType 'Solid' yet still be geometrically open if a face is missing.
- `edgeDefault` (string ("HardVisible", "HardHidden", "SoftHidden")): Default display status for every edge that has no entry in edgeOverrides. Reported accurately on Get. On Create/Modify it takes effect from Archicad 29 on, where it is applied to every edge of the element with ACAPI_Element_ChangeMorphEdgeType right after the element is created or changed (e.g. 'HardHidden' hides all edges of a triangulated body). On Archicad 28 and earlier it is set on the element but does not take effect due to the same confirmed Archicad SDK bug as edgeOverrides (element.morph.edgeType is silently discarded by ACAPI_Element_Create/Change).
- `vertices` (array of Coordinate3D, required): Flat, indexed vertex list, local to the Morph's own placement (not world coordinates). A Solid body needs at least 4 (a tetrahedron, the minimum closed volume); a Surface body has no closedness requirement at all - the minimum is 2 vertices joined by a single wireEdge (a lone vertex with no edge at all is rejected by Archicad itself, confirmed live) - enforced with a bodyType-aware error message, not by this minItems floor alone.
- `polygons` (array of MorphPolygon): One entry per face loop (into `vertices`), counterclockwise as seen from outside the body. Optional - a body made entirely of wireEdges (see below) needs none. Set "filled": false on an entry to create only that loop's edges (e.g. the outline of a pyramid's side faces) without an actual filled face.
- `wireEdges` (array of object): Standalone edges that belong to no face at all (e.g. a bare rectangle outline, or a pyramid with a filled base but wireframe-only sides - set "filled": false on a polygons entry for a whole closed loop like that instead, this is for individual edges not already covered by any polygon loop). Reported accurately by GetDetailsOfElements (every edge with zero adjacent faces); accepted back by CreateMorphs/ModifyMorphs. Identifies an edge by the (unordered) pair of vertex indices it connects - reuses whatever edge already exists between those two vertices if the polygons above happen to share it.
  - `vertexIds` (array of integer, required)
- `edgeOverrides` (array of object): READ-ONLY in practice: reported accurately by GetDetailsOfElements (reflecting whatever Archicad itself currently has), but CreateMorphs/ModifyMorphs silently ignore this field on input - per-edge display status cannot be set by an add-on due to a confirmed, still-unresolved Archicad SDK bug (element.morph.edgeType/bodyType are silently discarded by ACAPI_Element_Create/Change; see the GRAPHISOFT community forum thread 'Help with setting morph's hidden edges in the API'). To hide or smooth ALL edges of a Morph use edgeDefault, which does take effect from Archicad 29 on. Sparse when present - only edges whose display status differs from edgeDefault get an entry. Identifies an edge by the (unordered) pair of vertex indices it connects.
  - `vertexIds` (array of integer, required)
  - `hidden` (boolean): Hide this edge's line entirely.
  - `smooth` (boolean): Shade the two adjacent faces smoothly across this edge instead of as a hard crease - the 'aide a la courbe' rounded-look hint. Does not change actual geometry.
  - `silhouetteOnly` (boolean): Show this edge's line only where it forms a silhouette/contour from the current viewpoint.

### MorphDetails

object
- `origin` (Coordinate3D, required): Translation component of the Morph's placement transform (tranmat's origin column).
- `xAxis` (Coordinate3D): X axis of the Morph's placement transform (tranmat's first column). Omit on Create to get an identity rotation; give all three of xAxis/yAxis/zAxis together or none at all.
- `yAxis` (Coordinate3D): Y axis of the Morph's placement transform (tranmat's second column). Give all three of xAxis/yAxis/zAxis together or none at all.
- `zAxis` (Coordinate3D): Z axis of the Morph's placement transform (tranmat's third column). Give all three of xAxis/yAxis/zAxis together or none at all.
- `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId): The Morph's building material - a single, whole-volume property (what the mass is 'made of', governing cut-fill/quantity takeoff), NOT settable per face. Per-face appearance is controlled separately by each polygon's own surfaceId (see MorphBody) - confirmed live these are two independent, unrelated attributes (a Morph can have one uniform building material while showing a different Surface finish on each face).
- `surfaceId` (AttributeId): The Morph's own default Surface (element.morph.material) - used for any face that has no per-face surfaceId override of its own (see MorphBody polygons[].surfaceId). Distinct from buildingMaterialId (the whole-volume material). Confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this specific field when set through ACAPI_Element_Create alone (reproduced identically on Archicad 27 and 29 - not a version-specific issue, unlike polygons[].surfaceId below); CreateMorphs works around this transparently with an internal follow-up Change right after Create, so this field behaves correctly end-to-end despite the underlying quirk.
- `body` (MorphBody, required)
- `castShadow` (boolean): Whether the body casts shadow in 3D.
- `receiveShadow` (boolean): Whether the body receives shadow in 3D.
- `isAutoOnStoryVisibility` (boolean): When true, the per-story visibility (showContour/showFill) is calculated automatically from the Morph's vertical extent instead of using the explicit values.
- `showContour` (StoryVisibility): Which stories display this Morph's contour. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Create/Modify do not reliably apply it (showAllBelow/showRelAbove/showRelBelow silently come back reset even when explicitly set and isAutoOnStoryVisibility is false) - the same class of confirmed Archicad SDK write bug as bodyType/edgeType/level (see MorphBody's notes). Set on the element regardless since doing so is harmless and forward-compatible.
- `showFill` (StoryVisibility): Which stories display this Morph's floor plan fill. Same write-reliability caveat as showContour.
- `linkToSettings` (LinkToSettings)
- `displayOption` (DisplayOption)
- `viewDepthLimitation` (ViewDepthLimitation)
- `cutFillPen` (integer): Overridden cut fill foreground pen (otherwise inherited from the building material). Omit to leave uninherited/unset.
- `cutFillBackgroundPen` (integer): Overridden cut fill background pen (otherwise inherited from the building material). Omit to leave uninherited/unset.
- `cutLineType` (AttributeId): Line type of the cut contour.
- `cutLinePen` (integer): Pen of the cut contour.
- `uncutLineType` (AttributeId): Line type of the (uncut) contour.
- `uncutLinePen` (integer): Pen of the (uncut) contour.
- `overheadLineType` (AttributeId): Line type of the overhead part (floor plan only).
- `overheadLinePen` (integer): Pen of the overhead part (floor plan only).
- `useCoverFillType` (boolean): Use a dedicated floor plan fill instead of the one from the building material.
- `outlineContourDisplay` (boolean): Outline contour display.
- `coverFillType` (AttributeId): Floor plan fill type (only used when useCoverFillType is true).
- `coverFillPen` (integer): Floor plan fill foreground pen.
- `coverFillBGPen` (integer): Floor plan fill background pen.
- `use3DHatching` (boolean): Derive the floor plan fill from the 3D material instead of coverFillType.
- `coverFillOrientation` (CoverFillOrientation)
- `useDistortedCoverFill` (boolean): Show the floor plan hatching as if projected onto a plane.
- `textureProjectionType` (TextureProjectionType)
- `textureProjectionCoords` (array of Coordinate3D): Texture projection coordinate system: origin, then 3 axis endpoints.
- `level` (number): Z position of the free shape relative to the floor level. Reported accurately on Get, but a confirmed Archicad SDK bug means it may not take effect on Create/Modify (same class of bug as bodyType/edgeType - see MorphBody's notes).

### DrawingDetails

object
- `pos` (Coordinate2D, required): Position of the drawing's reference point on the layout.
- `angle` (number, required): Rotation angle of the drawing in radians.
- `ratio` (number, required): Scale ratio applied to the drawing relative to its source view.
- `drawingScale` (number, required): The nominal scale of the drawing.
- `modelOffset` (Coordinate2D, required): Offset of the model origin within the drawing.
- `isCutWithFrame` (boolean, required): Whether the drawing is clipped by a custom polygon (see clipPolygon) instead of showing the full auto-fit extent.
- `bounds` (BoundingBox2D, required): Bounds of the drawing on the layout.
- `clipPolygon` (array of Coordinate2D): Polygon used to clip the drawing view, in layout coordinates (meters on the layout, the same coordinate system as pos and bounds - not the coordinates of the source view's model). Archicad stores it as is; pos, angle, ratio and modelOffset are not applied to it. Present only when isCutWithFrame is true.
- `navigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required): Archicad's internal identifier of this Drawing's link (API_DrawingType::drawingGuid as Archicad reports it). This is NOT the navigator item id of the source view: CreateDrawings passes the source view in this field, but once the Drawing is created Archicad reports its own identifier, which is different for every Drawing (even two Drawings of the same view), is neither the source view nor the Drawing's item in the Layout Book, and is not accepted by navigator commands such as GetViewSettings. To find the source view of a placed Drawing, use the sourceNavigatorItemId of its DrawingItem in the Layout Book tree (GetNavigatorItemTree). Read-only: Archicad has no API to relink a Drawing to a different source (see ChangeDrawingLink).
- `nameType` (DrawingNameType, required)
- `customName` (string): The drawing's custom title name. Present only when nameType is CustomName.
- `numberingType` (DrawingNumberingType, required)
- `customNumber` (string): The drawing's custom title ID. Present only when numberingType is CustomNumber.
- `isInNumbering` (boolean, required): Whether the drawing is included in the automatic drawing numbering sequence.
- `isScaleIncludedInAutotextAndIndex` (boolean, required): The 'Include scale in Autotext and index' checkbox of Drawing Settings (API_DrawingType::includeInAutoTextsAndIES): whether the drawing's scale is included in the 'Drawing Scale' and 'Original Scale' Autotexts and in indexes.
- `hasBorderLine` (boolean, required): Whether the drawing shows a printable border (Drawing Settings > Frame > Add Printable Border).
- `borderLineTypeIndex` (integer, required): Attribute index of the line type of the drawing's border.
- `borderPenIndex` (integer, required): Pen index of the drawing's border.
- `borderSize` (number, required): Border size of the drawing (API_DrawingType::borderSize), in meters.
- `titleLibraryPartIndex` (number, required): Library part index of the drawing title (API_DrawingTitle::libInd). A negative/invalid index means no title object is instantiated; setting it to a valid index (e.g. copied from another drawing) makes Archicad create the title's own placed element.
- `titleElementId` (ElementId): Id of the drawing title, itself a placed GDL object element (font/pen/size aside, its own settings are reachable like any other element, e.g. with GetGDLParametersOfElements/SetGDLParametersOfElements). Absent if the drawing has no title object.

object

### LevelDimensionDetails

object
- `position` (Coordinate2D, required): The location of the marker.
- `level` (number, required): The level the dimension shows in meters: the height of the owner element at the position for an associative level dimension, the floor level or the static value otherwise.
- `staticLevel` (boolean, required): The static flag as Archicad reports it. A level dimension created with a fixed 'level' and no parent keeps that value although Archicad reads this flag as false.
- `ownerElementId` (ElementId): Present only for an associative level dimension: the element it measures.
- `ownerElementType` (ElementType): Present only for an associative level dimension.
- `dimForm` (integer, required): Marker type 0-19.
- `needPlus` (boolean, required)
- `pen` (integer, required)
- `textHeight` (number, required): Height of the dimension text in millimeters.
- `textPen` (integer, required)
- `markerSize` (number, required): Size of the marker in millimeters.
- `angle` (number, required): Rotation angle of the marker in radians.
- `origin` (DimensionOrigin, required)

### TextDetails

object
- `text` (string, required): The text content. Newlines separate the lines.
- `rawText` (string): The text content as read with Archicad's autotext flag turned off, so an autotext shows its key (e.g. '<PROJECTNUMBER>') instead of its value. Present only when the flag could be switched for the read.
- `position` (Coordinate2D, required): The placement position of the text.
- `angle` (number, required): The rotation angle in radians (same as style.angle).
- `height` (number, required): The character height in millimeters (same as style.height).
- `pen` (integer, required): The pen attribute index (same as style.penIndex).
- `justification` (Justification, required): Same as style.justification.
- `zCoordinate` (number, required): The level of the text's floor.
- `style` (TextStyleDetails, required): The flat fields above are the subset SetDetailsOfElements takes back.
- `paragraphCount` (integer, required): Read-only: number of paragraphs in the memo (Tapir's own Create/Modify commands always produce 1).
- `runs` (array of TextRunDetails): The styled runs of the content, present whenever the content has paragraphs (always for content Tapir created); one entry per run, a single run too, as a run may carry a pen, font, face or size of its own. Concatenating the runs' text in order gives the full content.

### StairDetails

object: The settings of a Stair element, the ones CreateStairs takes. The finishes and the structure are modeled by the Stair's subelements (risers, treads and structures), which GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements lists.
- `stepNum` (integer, required): Number of risers (steps).
- `riserHeight` (number, required): Height of each riser.
- `treadDepth` (number, required): The tread depth (going) stored in the Stair's settings. Archicad does not keep it in step with the modeled treads: a placed stair can read 0 or 1 here, so take the modeled going from the geometry of its treads or risers (Get3DGeometryOfElements) instead.
- `flightWidth` (number, required): Width of the stair flight.
- `totalHeight` (number, required): Total height of the stair.
- `level` (number, required): Height of the stair base above the home story level.
- `zCoordinate` (number, required): Absolute elevation of the stair base.
- `finishVisible` (boolean, required): Whether the tread/riser finishes are modeled. If false only the stair structure (e.g. a monolith) is.
- `baseLinePoints` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The baseline polyline the stair is placed along, in model coordinates, as given to CreateStairs.
- `baseLineArcs` (array of PolyArc): The curved segments of the baseline, present only when it has any.

### SectionDetails

object: The geometry of a Section (CutPlane) marker on the floor plan, the fields CreateSections takes.
- `name` (string, required): The name of the section.
- `idStr` (string, required): The reference ID of the section.
- `mainCoordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The points of the section line, from start to end. More than two for a broken section line. Empty when the line cannot be read.
- `depthCoordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The points of the depth line, the far boundary of the section. Empty when it cannot be read.
- `startCoordinate` (Coordinate2D): The first point of the section line (startCoordinate of CreateSections).
- `endCoordinate` (Coordinate2D): The last point of the section line (endCoordinate of CreateSections).
- `depth` (number): The distance of the first depth point from the first segment of the section line (depth of CreateSections).
- `viewDirection` (Coordinate2D): The unit vector perpendicular to the first segment of the section line, pointing to the side of the depth line: the direction the section looks in. CreateSections puts it to the left of the start to end direction.

### StoryParameters

object: Represents all parameters of a single project story, including its unique identifiers. Used in API responses.
- `index` (integer, required): The story index.
- `floorId` (integer, required): Unique ID of the story.
- `dispOnSections` (boolean, required): Story level lines should appear on sections and elevations.
- `level` (number, required): The story level.
- `height` (number): Story height, calculated as the level of the story above minus this story's level. The topmost story gets its height from the virtual story that Archicad keeps above it in the story settings; only an Archicad that did not report that virtual story would leave the top story without a height.
- `name` (string, required): The name of the story.
- `ifcId` (string): The IFC GlobalId of the story, i.e. of the IfcBuildingStorey it is exported as (the same identifier the IFC Project Manager shows). Available from Archicad 28; older versions omit it.
